Set up a minimal CLAUDE.md (and optionally skills and hooks) for this repo. CLAUDE.md is loaded into every Claude Code session, so it must be concise — only include what Claude would get wrong without it.

## Phase 1: Ask what to set up

Use AskUserQuestion to find out what the user wants:

- "Which CLAUDE.md files should /init set up?"
  Options: "Project CLAUDE.md" | "Personal CLAUDE.local.md" | "Both project + personal"
  Description for project: "Team-shared instructions checked into source control — architecture, coding standards, common workflows."
  Description for personal: "Your private preferences for this project (gitignored, not shared) — your role, sandbox URLs, preferred test data, workflow quirks."

- "Also set up skills and hooks?"
  Options: "Skills + hooks" | "Skills only" | "Hooks only" | "Neither, just CLAUDE.md"
  Description for skills: "On-demand capabilities you or Claude invoke with `/skill-name` — good for repeatable workflows and reference knowledge."
  Description for hooks: "Deterministic shell commands that run on tool events (e.g., format after every edit). Claude can't skip them."

## Phase 2: Explore the codebase

Launch a subagent to survey the codebase, and ask it to read key files to understand the project: manifest files (package.json, Cargo.toml, pyproject.toml, go.mod, pom.xml, etc.), README, Makefile/build configs, CI config, existing CLAUDE.md, .claude/rules/, AGENTS.md, .cursor/rules or .cursorrules, .github/copilot-instructions.md, .windsurfrules, .clinerules, .mcp.json.

Detect:
- Build, test, and lint commands (especially non-standard ones)
- Languages, frameworks, and package manager
- Project structure (monorepo with workspaces, multi-module, or single project)
- Code style rules that differ from language defaults
- Non-obvious gotchas, required env vars, or workflow quirks
- Existing .claude/skills/ and .claude/rules/ directories
- Formatter configuration (prettier, biome, ruff, black, gofmt, rustfmt, or a unified format script like `npm run format` / `make fmt`)
- Git worktree usage: run `git worktree list` to check if this repo has multiple worktrees (only relevant if the user wants a personal CLAUDE.local.md)

Note what you could NOT figure out from code alone — these become interview questions.

## Phase 3: Fill in the gaps

Use AskUserQuestion to gather what you still need to write good CLAUDE.md files and skills. Ask only things the code can't answer.

If the user chose project CLAUDE.md or both: ask about codebase practices — non-obvious commands, gotchas, branch/PR conventions, required env setup, testing quirks. Skip things already in README or obvious from manifest files. Do not mark any options as "recommended" — this is about how their team works, not best practices.

If the user chose personal CLAUDE.local.md or both: ask about them, not the codebase. Do not mark any options as "recommended" — this is about their personal preferences, not best practices. Examples of questions:
  - What's their role on the team? (e.g., "backend engineer", "data scientist", "new hire onboarding")
  - How familiar are they with this codebase and its languages/frameworks? (so Claude can calibrate explanation depth)
  - Do they have personal sandbox URLs, test accounts, API key paths, or local setup details Claude should know?
  - Only if Phase 2 found multiple git worktrees: ask whether their worktrees are nested inside the main repo (e.g., `.claude/worktrees/<name>/`) or siblings/external (e.g., `../myrepo-feature/`). If nested, the upward file walk finds the main repo's CLAUDE.local.md automatically — no special handling needed. If sibling/external, the personal content should live in a home-directory file (e.g., `~/.claude/<project-name>-instructions.md`) and each worktree gets a one-line CLAUDE.local.md stub that imports it: `@~/.claude/<project-name>-instructions.md`. Never put this import in the project CLAUDE.md — that would check a personal reference into the team-shared file.
  - Any communication preferences? (e.g., "be terse", "always explain tradeoffs", "don't summarize at the end")

**Synthesize a proposal from Phase 2 findings** — e.g., format-on-edit if a formatter exists, a `/verify` skill if tests exist, a CLAUDE.md note for anything from the gap-fill answers that's a guideline rather than a workflow. For each, pick the artifact type that fits, **constrained by the Phase 1 skills+hooks choice**:

  - **Hook** (stricter) — deterministic shell command on a tool event; Claude can't skip it. Fits mechanical, fast, per-edit steps: formatting, linting, running a quick test on the changed file.
  - **Skill** (on-demand) — you or Claude invoke `/skill-name` when you want it. Fits workflows that don't belong on every edit: deep verification, session reports, deploys.
  - **CLAUDE.md note** (looser) — influences Claude's behavior but not enforced. Fits communication/thinking preferences: "plan before coding", "be terse", "explain tradeoffs".

  **Respect Phase 1's skills+hooks choice as a hard filter**: if the user picked "Skills only", downgrade any hook you'd suggest to a skill or a CLAUDE.md note. If "Hooks only", downgrade skills to hooks (where mechanically possible) or notes. If "Neither", everything becomes a CLAUDE.md note. Never propose an artifact type the user didn't opt into.

**Show the proposal via AskUserQuestion's `preview` field, not as a separate text message** — the dialog overlays your output, so preceding text is hidden. The `preview` field renders markdown in a side-panel (like plan mode); the `question` field is plain-text-only. Structure it as:

  - `question`: short and plain, e.g. "Does this proposal look right?"
  - Each option gets a `preview` with the full proposal as markdown. The "Looks good — proceed" option's preview shows everything; per-item-drop options' previews show what remains after that drop.
  - **Keep previews compact — the preview box truncates with no scrolling.** One line per item, no blank lines between items, no header. Example preview content:

    • **Format-on-edit hook** (automatic) — `ruff format <file>` via PostToolUse
    • **/verify skill** (on-demand) — `make lint && make typecheck && make test`
    • **CLAUDE.md note** (guideline) — "run lint/typecheck/test before marking done"

  - Option labels stay short ("Looks good", "Drop the hook", "Drop the skill") — the tool auto-adds an "Other" free-text option, so don't add your own catch-all.

**Build the preference queue** from the accepted proposal. Each entry: {type: hook|skill|note, description, target file, any Phase-2-sourced details like the actual test/format command}. Phases 4-7 consume this queue.

## Phase 4: Write CLAUDE.md (if user chose project or both)

Write a minimal CLAUDE.md at the project root. Every line must pass this test: "Would removing this cause Claude to make mistakes?" If no, cut it.

**Consume `note` entries from the Phase 3 preference queue whose target is CLAUDE.md** (team-level notes) — add each as a concise line in the most relevant section. These are the behaviors the user wants Claude to follow but didn't need guaranteed (e.g., "propose a plan before implementing", "explain the tradeoffs when refactoring"). Leave personal-targeted notes for Phase 5.

Include:
- Build/test/lint commands Claude can't guess (non-standard scripts, flags, or sequences)
- Code style rules that DIFFER from language defaults (e.g., "prefer type over interface")
- Testing instructions and quirks (e.g., "run single test with: pytest -k 'test_name'")
- Repo etiquette (branch naming, PR conventions, commit style)
- Required env vars or setup steps
- Non-obvious gotchas or architectural decisions
- Important parts from existing AI coding tool configs if they exist (AGENTS.md, .cursor/rules, .cursorrules, .github/copilot-instructions.md, .windsurfrules, .clinerules)

Exclude:
- File-by-file structure or component lists (Claude can discover these by reading the codebase)
- Standard language conventions Claude already knows
- Generic advice ("write clean code", "handle errors")
- Detailed API docs or long references — use `@path/to/import` syntax instead (e.g., `@docs/api-reference.md`) to inline content on demand without bloating CLAUDE.md
- Information that changes frequently — reference the source with `@path/to/import` so Claude always reads the current version
- Long tutorials or walkthroughs (move to a separate file and reference with `@path/to/import`, or put in a skill)
- Commands obvious from manifest files (e.g., standard "npm test", "cargo test", "pytest")

Be specific: "Use 2-space indentation in TypeScript" is better than "Format code properly."

Do not repeat yourself and do not make up sections like "Common Development Tasks" or "Tips for Development" — only include information expressly found in files you read.

Prefix the file with:

```
# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
```

If CLAUDE.md already exists: read it, propose specific changes as diffs, and explain why each change improves it. Do not silently overwrite.

For projects with multiple concerns, suggest organizing instructions into `.claude/rules/` as separate focused files (e.g., `code-style.md`, `testing.md`, `security.md`). These are loaded automatically alongside CLAUDE.md and can be scoped to specific file paths using `paths` frontmatter.

For projects with distinct subdirectories (monorepos, multi-module projects, etc.): mention that subdirectory CLAUDE.md files can be added for module-specific instructions (they're loaded automatically when Claude works in those directories). Offer to create them if the user wants.

## Phase 5: Write CLAUDE.local.md (if user chose personal or both)

Write a minimal CLAUDE.local.md at the project root. This file is automatically loaded alongside CLAUDE.md. After creating it, add `CLAUDE.local.md` to the project's .gitignore so it stays private.

**Consume `note` entries from the Phase 3 preference queue whose target is CLAUDE.local.md** (personal-level notes) — add each as a concise line. If the user chose personal-only in Phase 1, this is the sole consumer of note entries.

Include:
- The user's role and familiarity with the codebase (so Claude can calibrate explanations)
- Personal sandbox URLs, test accounts, or local setup details
- Personal workflow or communication preferences

Keep it short — only include what would make Claude's responses noticeably better for this user.

If Phase 2 found multiple git worktrees and the user confirmed they use sibling/external worktrees (not nested inside the main repo): the upward file walk won't find a single CLAUDE.local.md from all worktrees. Write the actual personal content to `~/.claude/<project-name>-instructions.md` and make CLAUDE.local.md a one-line stub that imports it: `@~/.claude/<project-name>-instructions.md`. The user can copy this one-line stub to each sibling worktree. Never put this import in the project CLAUDE.md. If worktrees are nested inside the main repo (e.g., `.claude/worktrees/`), no special handling is needed — the main repo's CLAUDE.local.md is found automatically.

If CLAUDE.local.md already exists: read it, propose specific additions, and do not silently overwrite.

## Phase 6: Suggest and create skills (if user chose "Skills + hooks" or "Skills only")

Skills add capabilities Claude can use on demand without bloating every session.

**First, consume `skill` entries from the Phase 3 preference queue.** Each queued skill preference becomes a SKILL.md tailored to what the user described. For each:
- Name it from the preference (e.g., "verify-deep", "session-report", "deploy-sandbox")
- Write the body using the user's own words from the interview plus whatever Phase 2 found (test commands, report format, deploy target). If the preference maps to an existing bundled skill (e.g., `/verify`), write a project skill that adds the user's specific constraints on top — tell the user the bundled one still exists and theirs is additive.
- Ask a quick follow-up if the preference is underspecified (e.g., "which test command should verify-deep run?")

**Then suggest additional skills** beyond the queue when you find:
- Reference knowledge for specific tasks (conventions, patterns, style guides for a subsystem)
- Repeatable workflows the user would want to trigger directly (deploy, fix an issue, release process, verify changes)

For each suggested skill, provide: name, one-line purpose, and why it fits this repo.

If `.claude/skills/` already exists with skills, review them first. Do not overwrite existing skills — only propose new ones that complement what is already there.

Create each skill at `.claude/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md`:

```yaml
---
name: <skill-name>
description: <what the skill does and when to use it>
---

<Instructions for Claude>
```

Both the user (`/<skill-name>`) and Claude can invoke skills by default. For workflows with side effects (e.g., `/deploy`, `/fix-issue 123`), add `disable-model-invocation: true` so only the user can trigger it, and use `$ARGUMENTS` to accept input.

## Phase 7: Suggest additional optimizations

Tell the user you're going to suggest a few additional optimizations now that CLAUDE.md and skills (if chosen) are in place.

Check the environment and ask about each gap you find (use AskUserQuestion):

- **GitHub CLI**: Run `which gh` (or `where gh` on Windows). If it's missing AND the project uses GitHub (check `git remote -v` for github.com), ask the user if they want to install it. Explain that the GitHub CLI lets Claude help with commits, pull requests, issues, and code review directly.

- **Linting**: If Phase 2 found no lint config (no .eslintrc, ruff.toml, .golangci.yml, etc. for the project's language), ask the user if they want Claude to set up linting for this codebase. Explain that linting catches issues early and gives Claude fast feedback on its own edits.

- **Proposal-sourced hooks** (if user chose "Skills + hooks" or "Hooks only"): Consume `hook` entries from the Phase 3 preference queue. If Phase 2 found a formatter and the queue has no formatting hook, offer format-on-edit as a fallback. If the user chose "Neither" or "Skills only" in Phase 1, skip this bullet entirely.

  For each hook preference (from the queue or the formatter fallback):

  1. Target file: default based on the Phase 1 CLAUDE.md choice — project → `.claude/settings.json` (team-shared, committed); personal → `.claude/settings.local.json`. Only ask if the user chose "both" in Phase 1 or the preference is ambiguous. Ask once for all hooks, not per-hook.

  2. Pick the event and matcher from the preference:
     - "after every edit" → `PostToolUse` with matcher `Write|Edit`
     - "when Claude finishes" / "before I review" → `Stop` event (fires at the end of every turn — including read-only ones)
     - "before running bash" → `PreToolUse` with matcher `Bash`
     - "before committing" (literal git-commit gate) → **not a hooks.json hook.** Matchers can't filter Bash by command content, so there's no way to target only `git commit`. Route this to a git pre-commit hook (`.git/hooks/pre-commit`, husky, pre-commit framework) instead — offer to write one. If the user actually means "before I review and commit Claude's output", that's `Stop` — probe to disambiguate.
     Probe if the preference is ambiguous.

  3. **Load the hook reference** (once per `/init` run, before the first hook): invoke the Skill tool with `skill: 'update-config'` and args starting with `[hooks-only]` followed by a one-line summary of what you're building — e.g., `[hooks-only] Constructing a PostToolUse/Write|Edit format hook for .claude/settings.json using ruff`. This loads the hooks schema and verification flow into context. Subsequent hooks reuse it — don't re-invoke.

  4. Follow the skill's **"Constructing a Hook"** flow: dedup check → construct for THIS project → pipe-test raw → wrap → write JSON → `jq -e` validate → live-proof (for `Pre|PostToolUse` on triggerable matchers) → cleanup → handoff. Target file and event/matcher come from steps 1–2 above.

Act on each "yes" before moving on.

## Phase 8: Summary and next steps

Recap what was set up — which files were written and the key points included in each. Remind the user these files are a starting point: they should review and tweak them, and can run `/init` again anytime to re-scan.

Then tell the user that you'll be introducing a few more suggestions for optimizing their codebase and Claude Code setup based on what you found. Present these as a single, well-formatted to-do list where every item is relevant to this repo. Put the most impactful items first.

When building the list, work through these checks and include only what applies:
- If frontend code was detected (React, Vue, Svelte, etc.): `/plugin install frontend-design@claude-plugins-official` gives Claude design principles and component patterns so it produces polished UI; `/plugin install playwright@claude-plugins-official` lets Claude launch a real browser, screenshot what it built, and fix visual bugs itself.
- If you found gaps in Phase 7 (missing GitHub CLI, missing linting) and the user said no: list them here with a one-line reason why each helps.
- If tests are missing or sparse: suggest setting up a test framework so Claude can verify its own changes.
- To help you create skills and optimize existing skills using evals, Claude Code has an official skill-creator plugin you can install. Install it with `/plugin install skill-creator@claude-plugins-official`, then run `/skill-creator <skill-name>` to create new skills or refine any existing skill. (Always include this one.)
- Browse official plugins with `/plugin` — these bundle skills, agents, hooks, and MCP servers that you may find helpful. You can also create your own custom plugins to share them with others. (Always include this one.)

## KEY CONVENTIONS & GOTCHAS

### Code Naming:
- **Files:** kebab-case (`social-links.ts`)
- **Components:** PascalCase (`SkillsMultiSelect`)
- **Functions/Variables:** camelCase (`createProject`)
- **Database columns:** snake_case (Drizzle casing config)

### Architecture Patterns (4 core patterns):
1. **Container-Presentational:** pages call `getServerSession()` and query data, pass to presentational components
2. **Server Action Hardening:** authenticate → validate (Zod) → execute (try-catch) → revalidate
3. **Data Access Facade:** all reads go through `lib/queries/` (one file per entity)
4. **Error Boundaries:** `error.tsx` and `loading.tsx` for recovery and loading UI

### Security:
- **Two-layer auth:** optimistic redirect via `proxy.ts` (UX only) + real auth in pages/actions via `getServerSession()`
- **CSP with nonces** in proxy.ts
- **Server Actions validated** with Zod `.safeParse()`
- **SQL injection prevented** via Drizzle parameterized queries
- **CSRF protected** by better-auth + Next.js framework
- **Env vars:** secrets NOT prefixed with `NEXT_PUBLIC_` (but `.env` is committed!)

### Performance:
- **React Compiler enabled** — no need for useMemo/useCallback/React.memo
- **Code splitting** via `next/dynamic` for heavy components
- **Streaming** via `loading.tsx` Suspense boundaries
- **Bundle optimization:** lucide-react, react-icons, @radix-ui/react-icons configured with `optimizePackageImports`
- **Caching:** React Server Component caching (`cacheComponents: true`), `"use cache"` directive available

### Testing Strategy:
- **TDD for:** Zod schemas, utility functions, Server Action logic
- **Test-After for:** junction table sync, client components (optional), pages, auth flows
- **Tools:** Vitest (jsdom environment, jiti for TS config paths), Playwright (E2E, 3 browsers)
- **Mocking:** vi.mock at module level, use vi.mocked() for type-safe access

### Known Issues/Non-Obvious Gotchas:
1. **`.env` file is committed to git** containing production database tokens, auth secrets, and Blob credentials. Security risk.
2. **No error.tsx or loading.tsx files yet** — marked as needed in AGENTS-PATTERNS.md
3. **No sitemap.ts, robots.ts, or OG image generation** — SEO setup pending
4. **Playwright config** has webServer commented out (dev server setup incomplete)
5. **env files pattern:** should be `.env.local` (not committed), but `.env` is in repo. This contradicts `.gitignore`.
6. **Zod schemas exist but validation may not be complete** across all actions (migration in progress per AGENTS-PATTERNS.md)
7. **Skills directory (.agents/skills/)** takes 22+ folders; Prettier/CSpell skip it intentionally (`ignorePaths`)
8. **Husky hooks must be installed manually** — `ignore-scripts=true` in .npmrc, run `pnpm run hooks:install`

1	# AGENTS.md
2	
3	Personal portfolio with a public page and an admin dashboard (CMS) — built with Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4.2, Drizzle ORM, Turso, and better-auth.
4	
5	## Package Manager
6	
7	**Always use pnpm.** Never use npm, npx, or yarn. Use `pnpm dlx` instead of `npx`.
8	
9	## Commands
10	
11	| Command         | Description                        |
12	| --------------- | ---------------------------------- |
13	| `pnpm dev`      | Start dev server (Turbopack)       |
14	| `pnpm build`    | Production build                   |
15	| `pnpm lint`     | ESLint                             |
16	| `pnpm db:setup` | Generate + push Drizzle migrations |
17	| `pnpm start`    | Start production server            |
18	| `pnpm test`     | Vitest (watch mode)                |
19	
20	## Tech Stack
21	
22	| Category   | Technology                                         |
23	| ---------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
24	| Framework  | Next.js 16, App Router, React Compiler             |
25	| Language   | TypeScript (strict)                                |
26	| Styling    | Tailwind CSS 4.2, tw-animate-css                   |
27	| Database   | Turso (libSQL) via Drizzle ORM                     |
28	| Auth       | better-auth (email/password, sign-up disabled)     |
29	| UI         | shadcn/ui, Lucide icons, react-icons, cmdk, sonner |
30	| Animations | Motion, @number-flow/react, tw-animate-css         |
31	
32	## Project Structure
33	
34	```
35	app/
36	├── (admin)/          # Dashboard + login (protected)
37	├── (public)/         # Portfolio page (public)
38	├── api/              # Auth routes (better-auth)
39	└── layout.tsx        # Root layout
40	components/
41	├── admin/            # Dashboard components
42	├── auth/             # Auth components
43	├── public/           # Public portfolio components
44	└── ui/               # shadcn/ui components
45	db/schema/            # Drizzle schema (source of truth for DB structure)
46	lib/
47	├── actions/          # Server Actions
48	├── queries/          # Data access facade (read queries)
49	├── schemas/          # Zod validation schemas
50	├── auth.ts           # better-auth config
51	├── auth-client.ts    # better-auth client
52	├── server-session.ts # Session helper
53	├── types.d.ts        # Ambient / shared types
54	└── utils.ts          # Shared utilities (cn, formatDate, etc.)
55	```
56	
57	## Naming Conventions
58	
59	- **Files**: kebab-case (`social-links.ts`)
60	- **Components**: PascalCase (`SkillsMultiSelect`)
61	- **Functions/Variables**: camelCase (`createProject`)
62	- **Database columns**: snake_case (Drizzle casing config)
63	
64	## Knowledge Resolution Order
65	
66	1. This file + `AGENTS-*.md` sub-files
67	2. Agent Skills (`.cursor/skills/`)
68	3. Cursor's indexed docs
69	4. Web search (last resort)
70	
71	## Common Tasks
72	
73	> **Before adding a new entity, execute the following skill** — read the SKILL.md and follow its instructions:
74	>
75	> 1. `.cursor/skills/drizzle-orm/SKILL.md`
76	
77	**Add a new entity**: schema in `db/schema/` → `pnpm db:setup` → actions in `lib/actions/` → Zod schema in `lib/schemas/` → query in `lib/queries/` → dashboard page → public page.

86	**Add a UI component**: add in `components/ui/` using Radix primitives + Tailwind + `cn()`.

1	# AGENTS-SETUP.md
2	
3	First-time setup, environment configuration, and development prerequisites.
4	
5	> **Before making schema changes or running Drizzle migrations, execute the following skill** — read the SKILL.md and follow its instructions:
6	>
7	> 1. `.cursor/skills/drizzle-orm/SKILL.md`
8	
9	> **Before configuring Tailwind theme or CSS variables, execute the following skill** — read the SKILL.md and follow its instructions:
10	>
11	> 1. `.cursor/skills/tailwind-design-system/SKILL.md`
12	
13	---
14	
15	## Prerequisites
16	
17	- Node.js 24+
18	- pnpm 10.33.0 via the repo's `packageManager` field
19	- Turso CLI (optional, for local DB management)
20	
21	## Environment Variables
22	
23	Create a `.env.local` file:
24	
25	```env
26	TURSO_DATABASE_URL=libsql://your-database.turso.io
27	TURSO_AUTH_TOKEN=your-auth-token
28	BETTER_AUTH_SECRET=your-secret-key
29	BETTER_AUTH_URL=http://localhost:3000
30	```
31	
32	## Installation
33	
34	```bash
35	pnpm i
36	pnpm run hooks:install
37	```
38	
39	`ignore-scripts=true` is enabled in `.npmrc`, so lifecycle scripts do not run during install. Husky hooks must be installed manually with `pnpm run hooks:install`.
40	
41	## Making Schema Changes
42	
43	1. Edit schema files in `db/schema/`
44	2. Run `pnpm db:setup` to generate migrations and push to Turso
45	
46	## Agent Skills Installation Policy
47	
48	- Every new skill installed via `skills.sh` CLI must also be added to the `skills:install` script in `package.json`.
49	- Keep `skills:install` as the single source of truth for reproducible skill setup across environments.
50
```
</details></tool-use>

1	# AGENTS-CONVENTIONS.md
2	
3	Code conventions for the portfolio project — JSDoc guidelines that go beyond what the linter and TypeScript enforce.
4	
5	> **Before implementing complex type logic, generics, or utility types, execute the following skill** — read the SKILL.md and follow its instructions:
6	>
7	> 1. `.cursor/skills/typescript-advanced-types/SKILL.md`
8	
9	---
10	
11	## JSDoc
12	
13	Since TypeScript already provides type safety, use JSDoc to add **semantic context** — the "why", not the "what". Do not restate information that types already express.
14	
15	### When to Document
16	
17	Document when there is:
18	
19	- Non-obvious logic or business rules
20	- Side effects (revalidation, redirects, external calls)
21	- Security assumptions or constraints
22	- Possible errors or edge cases
23	- Deprecations or temporary workarounds
24	
25	Skip JSDoc for:
26	
27	- Self-explanatory functions where the name + types say it all
28	- Simple component props already typed with an interface
29	- One-liner utilities with clear names (e.g., `formatDate`)
30	
31	### Approved Tags
32	
33	| Tag           | Use for                                                                   | Example context                                      |
34	| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
35	| `@param`      | Only when the name/type isn't self-explanatory, or to clarify constraints | `@param id - Must be > 0, validated upstream by Zod` |
36	| `@returns`    | Only when the return value has non-obvious meaning                        | `@returns null when the user has no active session`  |
37	| `@throws`     | Server actions / functions that throw or redirect                         | `@throws Redirects to /login if unauthenticated`     |
38	| `@example`    | Complex utilities where usage isn't obvious                               | `@example cn("base", condition && "extra")`          |
39	| `@deprecated` | Superseded code that still exists                                         | `@deprecated Use getServerSession() instead`         |
40	| `@see`        | Link to related code, docs, or decisions                                  | `@see AGENTS-SECURITY.md for auth pattern`           |
41	| `@todo`       | Known improvements pending                                                | `@todo Add Zod validation (issue #42)`               |
42	
43	Avoid `@type`, `@typedef`, `@callback` — TypeScript handles these.
44	
45	### Where to Prioritize
46	
47	| Location                               | Priority   | Reason                                             |
48	| -------------------------------------- | ---------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
49	| `lib/actions/*` (Server Actions)       | **High**   | Side effects, auth checks, revalidation, redirects |
50	| `lib/auth.ts`, `lib/server-session.ts` | **High**   | Security assumptions, session flow                 |
51	| `db/schema/*`                          | **Medium** | Relationships, constraints, enum meanings          |
52	| `components/ui/*` (reusable)           | **Medium** | Prop behavior, variants, accessibility notes       |
53	| `lib/utils.ts`                         | **Low**    | Only if logic is non-trivial                       |
54	| Page/layout components                 | **Low**    | Only for unusual data fetching or auth patterns    |
55	
56	### Examples
57	
58	**Server Action** (`lib/actions/`):
59	
60	```typescript
61	/**
62	 * Updates a project and its associated skills.
63	 * Revalidates both the dashboard and public page caches.
64	 *
65	 * @throws Redirects to /login if the session is invalid.
66	 * @throws Error if the project ID does not exist.
67	 */
68	export async function updateProject(formData: FormData) {
69		// ...
70	}
71	```
72	
73	**Schema** (`db/schema/`):
74	
75	```typescript
76	/**
77	 * Tracks employment status changes over time.
78	 * Each row is an immutable snapshot — never update, only insert.
79	 */
80	export const employmentHistory = sqliteTable('employment_history', {
81		// ...
82	});
83	```
84	
85	**Auth helper** (`lib/`):
86	
87	```typescript
88	/**
89	 * Retrieves the current admin session from cookies.
90	 *
91	 * @returns The session object, or `null` if unauthenticated.
92	 * @see AGENTS-SECURITY.md — "Auth Protection Pattern" for the two-layer approach.
93	 */
94	export async function getServerSession() {
95		// ...
96	}
97	```
98	
99	**UI component** (`components/ui/`):
100	
101	```typescript
102	/**
103	 * Combobox for selecting multiple skills with search filtering.
104	 * Renders as a popover with a command palette (cmdk).
105	 *
106	 * @see https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/combobox
107	 */
108	```
109	
110	**Deprecation**:
111	
112	```typescript
113	/**
114	 * @deprecated Replaced by `getServerSession()`. Will be removed in v2.
115	 */
116	export function getSessionFromCookie() {
117		// ...
118	}
119	```
120	
121	### Style Rules
122	
123	- Use `/** ... */` (not `//` or `/* */`) so editors parse the JSDoc
124	- First line: concise summary (what + why, one sentence)
125	- Blank line before tags if there is a description body
126	- Keep descriptions under 80 characters per line when possible
127	- Write in English, imperative mood ("Retrieves...", not "This function retrieves...")
128
```

1	# AGENTS-PATTERNS.md
2	
3	Design patterns and architecture guidelines for the portfolio project.
4	
5	> **Before refactoring component architecture or splitting components, execute the following skill** — read the SKILL.md and follow its instructions:
6	>
7	> 1. `.cursor/skills/vercel-composition-patterns/SKILL.md`
8	
9	> **Before implementing Next.js file-system conventions or App Router patterns, execute the following skills** — read each SKILL.md and follow its instructions:
10	>
11	> 1. `.cursor/skills/next-best-practices/SKILL.md`
12	> 2. `.cursor/skills/nextjs-app-router-patterns/SKILL.md`
13	
14	> **Before optimizing Server Actions or React performance, execute the following skill** — read the SKILL.md and follow its instructions:
15	>
16	> 1. `.cursor/skills/vercel-react-best-practices/SKILL.md`
17	
18	**Related coverage in other AGENTS files (do not duplicate):**
19	
20	- `AGENTS-SECURITY.md` — Server Action auth/validation rules, CSP nonce in `proxy.ts`
21	- `AGENTS-TESTING.md` — TDD for Zod schemas, Server Action test patterns
22	- `AGENTS-PERFORMANCE.md` — Server vs Client decision tree, loading/streaming
23	- `AGENTS-ACCESSIBILITY.md` — Semantic layout landmarks, heading hierarchy
24	- [AGENTS-SEO.md](./AGENTS-SEO.md) — Metadata templates, OG images, sitemap, robots
25	
26	---
27	
28	## Overview
29	
30	| Pattern                  | What It Solves                                            | Where It Applies                   |
31	| ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
32	| Container-Presentational | Page files mix data fetching with 200+ lines of UI        | Admin dashboard pages, public page |
33	| Server Action Hardening  | Actions have no auth, no validation, no error handling    | All `lib/actions/` files           |
34	| Data Access Facade       | DB queries duplicated inline across page files            | All pages that query the database  |
35	| Error Boundaries         | Zero error recovery — failed DB query crashes entire page | All route segments                 |
36	
37	---
38	
39	## 1. Container-Presentational Pattern
40	
41	Split each page into a **Container** (the `page.tsx` — fetches data, checks auth, passes props) and a **Presentational** component (receives data via props, renders UI).
42	
43	```
44	app/(admin)/dashboard/projects/
45	├── page.tsx                    # Container — ~50 lines max
46	components/admin/
47	├── projects-table.tsx          # Presentational — table UI
48	├── entity-empty-state.tsx      # Shared reusable empty state
49	```
50	
51	### Template
52	
53	```typescript
54	// app/(admin)/dashboard/projects/page.tsx
55	import { getProjectsWithSkills } from "@/lib/queries/projects";
56	import { ProjectsTable } from "@/components/admin/projects-table";
57	import { getServerSession } from "@/lib/server-session";
58	import { redirect } from "next/navigation";
59	
60	export default async function ProjectsPage() {
61	  const session = await getServerSession();
62	  if (!session) redirect("/login");
63	
64	  const projects = await getProjectsWithSkills();
65	  return <ProjectsTable projects={projects} />;
66	}
67	```
68	
69	### Rules
70	
71	- **Page files (`page.tsx`) must not exceed ~50 lines** — if they do, UI is leaking into the container
72	- **Presentational components receive all data via props** — never call `db` directly
73	- **Shared formatting utilities go in `lib/utils.ts`** — not redefined per page (`formatDate`, `getStatusVariant`)
74	- **Presentational components are `"use client"` only when they need interactivity** (delete buttons, sort toggles) — keep as Server Components when purely displaying data
75	- **Empty states use a shared `EntityEmptyState` component** — same pattern across all entities
76	
77	---
78	
79	## 2. Server Action Hardening (Strategy-like)
80	
81	Every Server Action follows a **4-step strategy**: authenticate → validate → execute → revalidate. Each entity defines its own Zod schema in `lib/schemas/`, but the structure is identical.
82	
83	### 4-Step Template
84	
85	```typescript
86	'use server';
87	
88	import { getServerSession } from '@/lib/server-session';
89	import { redirect } from 'next/navigation';
90	import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache';
91	import { db } from '@/db';
92	import { entitySchema } from '@/lib/schemas/entity';
93	
94	export async function createEntity(formData: FormData) {
95		// 1. AUTHENTICATE
96		const session = await getServerSession();
97		if (!session) redirect('/login');
98	
99		// 2. VALIDATE
100		const parsed = entitySchema.safeParse({
101			name: formData.get('name'),
102		});
103		if (!parsed.success) return { error: parsed.error.flatten().fieldErrors };
104	
105		// 3. EXECUTE
106		try {
107			await db.insert(table).values(parsed.data);
108		} catch {
109			return { error: 'Failed to create entity.' };
110		}
111	
112		// 4. REVALIDATE / REDIRECT
113		redirect('/dashboard/entities');
114	}
115	```
116	
117	### Action Return Type
118	
119	```typescript
120	type ActionResult = { error: string } | { error: Record<string, string[]> } | void; // success — redirect happens
121	```
122	
123	### Rules
124	
125	- **Every action starts with `getServerSession()`** — no exceptions; redirect to `/login` if `null`
126	- **Every action validates with Zod `.safeParse()`** — never trust `formData.get()` directly
127	- **Wrap DB operations in try-catch** — return user-friendly messages, never expose raw errors
128	- **Remove all `console.log` statements** from actions
129	- **Transform empty strings to `undefined`** — forms submit `""` for empty optional fields; use `.or(z.literal(""))` or `.transform()`
130	- **Zod schemas live in `lib/schemas/`** — one file per entity (projects.ts, experiences.ts, skills.ts, social-links.ts, settings.ts)
131	
132	### Migration Order (per entity)
133	
134	1. Create Zod schema in `lib/schemas/`
135	2. Write Vitest tests for the schema (TDD — see `AGENTS-TESTING.md`)
136	3. Add auth + validation + try-catch to each action
137	4. Remove `console.log` statements
138	5. Test the full flow in the browser
139	
140	---
141	
142	## 3. Data Access Facade
143	
144	Encapsulate all Drizzle read queries in `lib/queries/` — one file per entity. Pages import these functions instead of using `db` directly.
145	
146	```
147	lib/queries/
148	├── projects.ts        # getProjectsWithSkills, getProjectById
149	├── experiences.ts     # getExperiencesWithSkills, getExperienceById
150	├── skills.ts          # getAllSkills
151	├── social-links.ts    # getAllSocialLinks
152	├── settings.ts        # getSiteSettings
153	```
154	
155	### Template
156	
157	```typescript
158	// lib/queries/projects.ts
159	import 'server-only';
160	import { db } from '@/db';
161	import { projects } from '@/db/schema/portfolio';
162	import { asc, eq } from 'drizzle-orm';
163	
164	export async function getProjectsWithSkills() {
165		return db.query.projects.findMany({
166			with: {
167				projectSkills: { columns: {}, with: { skill: { columns: { id: true, name: true } } } },
168			},
169			orderBy: [asc(projects.order)],
170		});
171	}
172	```
173	
174	### Rules
175	
176	- **Pages never import `db` directly** — always go through `lib/queries/`
177	- **Server Actions still use `db` directly** — writes don't benefit from a read-only facade
178	- **One file per entity** — mirrors `lib/actions/` structure
179	- **Add `"server-only"` import** — prevents accidental client-side import
180	- **Keep functions simple** — one Drizzle query per function, no business logic
181	- **Caching goes here** — add `"use cache"` + `cacheLife()` inside facade functions; all callers benefit automatically
182	
183	---
184	
185	## 4. Error Boundaries
186	
187	Add `error.tsx` and `loading.tsx` files to route segments for error recovery and loading states.
188	
189	### Minimum Required Files
190	
191	| File                                | Catches                                     |
192	| ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
193	| `app/error.tsx`                     | Root-level fallback for any unhandled error |
194	| `app/(admin)/dashboard/error.tsx`   | Database failures, auth errors in dashboard |
195	| `app/(public)/error.tsx`            | Database failures on public portfolio page  |
196	| `app/(admin)/dashboard/loading.tsx` | Skeleton while dashboard data loads         |
197	| `app/(public)/loading.tsx`          | Skeleton while public page data loads       |
198	| `app/not-found.tsx`                 | Custom 404 page                             |
199	
200	### Template
201	
202	```typescript
203	// app/(admin)/dashboard/error.tsx
204	"use client";
205	
206	export default function DashboardError({
207	  error,
208	  reset,
209	}: {
210	  error: Error & { digest?: string };
211	  reset: () => void;
212	}) {
213	  // Log error, show generic message, provide reset button + "go back" link
214	  return (/* Card with error icon, message, reset button, home link */);
215	}
216	```
217	
218	### Rules
219	
220	- **`error.tsx` must have `"use client"`** — required by Next.js
221	- **Never display `error.message` to users** — may contain SQL errors or stack traces; show generic message
222	- **Always provide a `reset` button** and a "go back" escape hatch
223	- **Use `error.digest` for server-side error correlation** — matches server logs
224	- **Root `error.tsx` does NOT catch root layout errors** — use `global-error.tsx` only if root layout can fail (unlikely in this project)
225	- **Pair `error.tsx` with `loading.tsx`** — error boundaries handle failures; loading files handle the pending state
226	- **Skeleton UIs must match the shape of actual content** — minimizes layout shift during streaming
227	
228	---
229	
230	## 5. Next.js File-System Conventions (Summary)
231	
232	> Full convention reference with detailed explanations and code: [AGENTS-PATTERNS-REFERENCE.md](./AGENTS-PATTERNS-REFERENCE.md)
233	
234	### Quick Reference
235	
236	| Convention           | File                    | Used in Project                                | Status                       |
237	| -------------------- | ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
238	| Page                 | `page.tsx`              | Yes — 9 pages                                  | Active                       |
239	| Layout               | `layout.tsx`            | Yes — root, admin, public                      | Active                       |
240	| Loading              | `loading.tsx`           | No                                             | **Needed**                   |
241	| Error                | `error.tsx`             | No                                             | **Needed**                   |
242	| Global Error         | `global-error.tsx`      | No                                             | Optional                     |
243	| Not Found            | `not-found.tsx`         | No                                             | **Needed**                   |
244	| Forbidden            | `forbidden.tsx`         | No                                             | Experimental — not yet       |
245	| Unauthorized         | `unauthorized.tsx`      | No                                             | Experimental — not yet       |
246	| Route Handler        | `route.ts`              | Yes — auth routes                              | Active                       |
247	| Proxy                | `proxy.ts`              | Yes — auth + CSP                               | Active                       |
248	| Template             | `template.tsx`          | No                                             | Not needed                   |
249	| Default              | `default.tsx`           | No                                             | Not needed                   |
250	| Route Groups         | `(folder)`              | Yes — `(admin)`, `(public)`                    | Active                       |
251	| Dynamic Segments     | `[param]`, `[...param]` | Yes — `[id]`, `[...all]`                       | Active                       |
252	| Parallel Routes      | `@folder`               | No                                             | Not needed                   |
253	| Intercepting Routes  | `(.)folder`             | No                                             | Not needed                   |
254	| Route Segment Config | `export const dynamic`  | No                                             | Prefer `"use cache"` instead |
255	| Metadata Files       | Various                 | Partial — see [AGENTS-SEO.md](./AGENTS-SEO.md) | **Needed**                   |
256	
257	### Files to Create Before Production
258	
259	| Priority   | File                                                                         | Why                                        |
260	| ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
261	| **High**   | `app/error.tsx`, `app/(admin)/dashboard/error.tsx`, `app/(public)/error.tsx` | Error recovery                             |
262	| **High**   | `app/(admin)/dashboard/loading.tsx`, `app/(public)/loading.tsx`              | Loading skeletons                          |
263	| **High**   | `app/not-found.tsx`                                                          | Custom 404                                 |
264	| **Medium** | `app/sitemap.ts`, `app/robots.ts`, OG image, favicons                        | SEO (see [AGENTS-SEO.md](./AGENTS-SEO.md)) |
265	| **Low**    | `app/(admin)/dashboard/not-found.tsx`                                        | Admin 404 for missing entities             |
266	| **Low**    | `instrumentation.ts`                                                         | Production error tracking                  |
267	
268	### Key Convention Rules
269	
270	- `params` and `searchParams` are **promises** in Next.js 16 — always `await` before accessing
271	- Pages are async Server Components — keep them as thin containers after applying pattern 1
272	- Every admin page must call `getServerSession()` at the top
273	- Layouts **cannot** access `searchParams` — only `params` and `children`
274	- A `route.ts` in the same segment as `page.tsx` will conflict — they can't coexist
275	- Route Segment Config (`export const dynamic`, etc.) is disabled when `cacheComponents: true` — prefer `"use cache"` directive
276	
277	---
278	
279	## Pattern Interaction
280	
281	The four patterns work together in a typical admin page:
282	
283	```
284	Request → page.tsx (Container)
285	            ├── getServerSession()            ← Error Boundary catches auth failures
286	            ├── getProjectsWithSkills()       ← Data Access Facade (lib/queries/)
287	            │                                    └── Error Boundary catches DB failures
288	            └── <ProjectsTable />             ← Presentational Component
289	                    └── deleteProject()        ← Hardened Server Action
290	                          ├── getServerSession()
291	                          ├── Zod safeParse
292	                          ├── try-catch DB operation
293	                          └── revalidatePath
294	```
295	
296	### Migration Flow
297	
298	When refactoring existing pages, follow this order:
299	
300	1. Create Zod schemas (`lib/schemas/`)
301	2. Harden server actions (auth + validation + try-catch)
302	3. Create data access facades (`lib/queries/`)
303	4. Extract presentational components (`components/admin/`)
304	5. Simplify page files to containers
305	6. Add `error.tsx` and `loading.tsx` files
306	
307	---
308	
309	## Implementation Checklist
310	
311	### Per Entity (projects, experiences, skills, social-links, settings)
312	
313	- [ ] Zod schema in `lib/schemas/` + Vitest tests
314	- [ ] Server actions hardened (auth + validation + try-catch + no console.log)
315	- [ ] Query functions in `lib/queries/`
316	- [ ] Presentational table component in `components/admin/`
317	- [ ] Page file simplified to container-only (~50 lines)
318	
319	### Global (once)
320	
321	- [ ] `app/error.tsx`, `app/(admin)/dashboard/error.tsx`, `app/(public)/error.tsx`
322	- [ ] `app/(admin)/dashboard/loading.tsx`, `app/(public)/loading.tsx`
323	- [ ] `app/not-found.tsx`, `app/(admin)/dashboard/not-found.tsx`
324	- [ ] Shared `EntityEmptyState` component
325	- [ ] `formatDate` and `formatDateRange` moved to `lib/utils.ts`
326
```

1	# AGENTS-PATTERNS-REFERENCE.md
2	
3	Detailed Next.js file-system convention reference and full implementation templates extracted from [AGENTS-PATTERNS.md](./AGENTS-PATTERNS.md). Read this file when you need the full code for a specific convention or pattern — the main file has the rules and decision guidance.
4	
5	> **Skill directives apply here.** Follow the skill execution instructions at the top of [AGENTS-PATTERNS.md](./AGENTS-PATTERNS.md) before writing any code based on this reference.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Next.js File-System Conventions
10	
11	Next.js uses a file-system based router where specific file names inside `app/` have special meaning. Reference: [Next.js File Conventions](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions)
12	
13	---
14	
15	### Page
16	
17	**File**: `page.tsx` — Makes a route segment publicly accessible.
18	
19	**Used in project**: Yes.
20	
21	| Page                                                               | Path                                                |
22	| ------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------- |
23	| Root redirect                                                      | `app/page.tsx`                                      |
24	| Public portfolio                                                   | `app/(public)/page.tsx`                             |
25	| Login                                                              | `app/(admin)/login/page.tsx`                        |
26	| Dashboard overview                                                 | `app/(admin)/dashboard/page.tsx`                    |
27	| Projects list                                                      | `app/(admin)/dashboard/projects/page.tsx`           |
28	| New project                                                        | `app/(admin)/dashboard/projects/new/page.tsx`       |
29	| Edit project                                                       | `app/(admin)/dashboard/projects/[id]/edit/page.tsx` |
30	| ... (same pattern for experiences, skills, social-links, settings) |                                                     |
31	
32	**Project rules**:
33	
34	- Pages are async Server Components — they fetch data and render content
35	- After applying the Container-Presentational pattern, pages should be thin containers (~50 lines max)
36	- Every admin page must call `getServerSession()` at the top
37	- The `page.tsx` default export receives optional `params` and `searchParams` props (both are promises in Next.js 16)
38	
39	```typescript
40	export default async function Page({
41		params,
42		searchParams,
43	}: {
44		params: Promise<{ id: string }>;
45		searchParams: Promise<{ [key: string]: string | string[] | undefined }>;
46	}) {
47		const { id } = await params;
48		// ...
49	}
50	```
51	
52	---
53	
54	### Layout
55	
56	**File**: `layout.tsx` — Shared UI that wraps a route segment and its children. Persists across navigations without re-rendering.
57	
58	**Used in project**: Yes.
59	
60	| Layout          | Path                               | Purpose                                    |
61	| --------------- | ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
62	| Root            | `app/layout.tsx`                   | HTML shell, fonts, global styles, metadata |
63	| Admin dashboard | `app/(admin)/dashboard/layout.tsx` | Sidebar, header, auth wrapper              |
64	| Public          | `app/(public)/layout.tsx`          | Public page shell with semantic landmarks  |
65	
66	**Project rules**:
67	
68	- Root layout must include `<html>` and `<body>` tags
69	- Layouts are Server Components by default — keep them as Server Components
70	- The admin dashboard layout should eventually use real session data instead of the current `mockUser`
71	- Layouts **cannot** access `searchParams` — only `params` and `children`
72	- Do **not** add `"use client"` to layouts unless absolutely necessary
73	
74	```typescript
75	export default async function Layout({
76	  children,
77	  params,
78	}: {
79	  children: React.ReactNode;
80	  params: Promise<{ slug: string }>;
81	}) {
82	  return <section>{children}</section>;
83	}
84	```
85	
86	---
87	
88	### Loading
89	
90	**File**: `loading.tsx` — Instant loading UI shown while a route segment's content is being fetched. Wraps the sibling `page.tsx` in a `<Suspense>` boundary automatically.
91	
92	**Used in project**: No — **needs to be added**.
93	
94	See [AGENTS-PATTERNS.md § Error Boundaries](./AGENTS-PATTERNS.md#4-error-boundaries) for which route segments need `loading.tsx` files.
95	
96	**Key behaviors**:
97	
98	- Shown immediately on navigation — provides instant feedback before data arrives
99	- Server Component by default — can render Skeleton components without JS
100	- Shared layouts remain interactive while loading shows
101	- Navigation is interruptible — user can navigate away before loading completes
102	
103	**Implementation**:
104	
105	```typescript
106	// app/(admin)/dashboard/loading.tsx
107	import { Skeleton } from "@/components/ui/skeleton";
108	
109	export default function DashboardLoading() {
110	  return (
111	    <div className="space-y-6">
112	      <div className="flex items-center justify-between">
113	        <div className="space-y-2">
114	          <Skeleton className="h-8 w-48" />
115	          <Skeleton className="h-4 w-64" />
116	        </div>
117	        <Skeleton className="h-10 w-36" />
118	      </div>
119	      <Skeleton className="h-[400px] w-full rounded-lg" />
120	    </div>
121	  );
122	}
123	```
124	
125	---
126	
127	### Error
128	
129	**File**: `error.tsx` — Fallback UI when a runtime error occurs in a route segment. Must be a Client Component (`"use client"`).
130	
131	**Used in project**: No — **needs to be added**.
132	
133	**Props**:
134	
135	- `error: Error & { digest?: string }` — the error object. In production, server errors show a generic message; use `digest` to correlate with server logs
136	- `reset: () => void` — re-renders the route segment to attempt recovery
137	
138	**Key behaviors**:
139	
140	- Wraps `page.tsx` in a React Error Boundary
141	- Errors bubble up to the nearest parent `error.tsx` if not caught locally
142	- Does **not** catch errors in the same-level `layout.tsx` — only in `page.tsx` and children
143	- Root `app/error.tsx` does **not** catch root layout errors (use `global-error.tsx` for that)
144	
145	**Implementation**:
146	
147	```typescript
148	// app/(admin)/dashboard/error.tsx
149	"use client";
150	
151	import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button";
152	import { Card, CardContent } from "@/components/ui/card";
153	import { AlertTriangle } from "lucide-react";
154	
155	interface DashboardErrorProps {
156	  error: Error & { digest?: string };
157	  reset: () => void;
158	}
159	
160	export default function DashboardError({ error, reset }: DashboardErrorProps) {
161	  return (
162	    <div className="flex items-center justify-center min-h-[50vh]">
163	      <Card className="max-w-md w-full">
164	        <CardContent className="flex flex-col items-center py-12 text-center">
165	          <div className="rounded-full bg-destructive/10 p-4 mb-4">
166	            <AlertTriangle className="size-8 text-destructive" />
167	          </div>
168	          <h2 className="text-lg font-semibold mb-2">Algo salió mal</h2>
169	          <p className="text-muted-foreground mb-6">
170	            Ha ocurrido un error inesperado. Puedes intentar de nuevo o volver al inicio.
171	          </p>
172	          <div className="flex gap-3">
173	            <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => window.location.href = "/dashboard"}>
174	              Ir al inicio
175	            </Button>
176	            <Button onClick={reset}>
177	              Intentar de nuevo
178	            </Button>
179	          </div>
180	        </CardContent>
181	      </Card>
182	    </div>
183	  );
184	}
185	```
186	
187	### Error Logging
188	
189	```typescript
190	// In error.tsx — log but don't display
191	useEffect(() => {
192		console.error('Dashboard error:', error);
193		// TODO: Send to error tracking service (Sentry, etc.)
194	}, [error]);
195	```

1	# AGENTS-SECURITY.md
2	
3	Security guidelines for the portfolio project — all security layers for a Next.js 16 app deployed on Vercel with better-auth, Drizzle ORM, and Turso.
4	
5	> Full implementation code (proxy.ts, next.config.ts headers, SDK examples, audit commands): [AGENTS-SECURITY-REFERENCE.md](./AGENTS-SECURITY-REFERENCE.md)
6	
7	> **Before implementing or modifying authentication, execute the following skill** — read the SKILL.md and follow its instructions:
8	>
9	> 1. `.cursor/skills/better-auth-best-practices/SKILL.md`
10	
11	> **Before writing or reviewing database queries, execute the following skill** — read the SKILL.md and follow its instructions:
12	>
13	> 1. `.cursor/skills/drizzle-orm/SKILL.md`
14	
15	> **Before hardening Server Actions, execute the following skills** — read each SKILL.md and follow its instructions:
16	>
17	> 1. `.cursor/skills/vercel-react-best-practices/SKILL.md`
18	> 2. `.cursor/skills/next-best-practices/SKILL.md`
19	
20	---
21	
22	## Content Security Policy (CSP)
23	
24	CSP protects against XSS, clickjacking, and code injection by declaring trusted content sources. Implemented via nonces in `proxy.ts`.
25	
26	**How it works**: `proxy.ts` generates a unique nonce per request → adds it to the `Content-Security-Policy` header → Next.js applies the nonce to scripts/styles → only matching scripts execute.
27	
28	### CSP Skeleton (in proxy.ts)
29	
30	```typescript
31	const nonce = Buffer.from(crypto.randomUUID()).toString('base64');
32	const isDev = process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development';
33	
34	const cspHeader = `
35	  default-src 'self';
36	  script-src 'self' 'nonce-${nonce}' 'strict-dynamic'${isDev ? " 'unsafe-eval'" : ''};
37	  style-src 'self'${isDev ? " 'unsafe-inline'" : ` 'nonce-${nonce}'`};
38	  img-src 'self' blob: data: https:;
39	  font-src 'self';
40	  object-src 'none';
41	  base-uri 'self';
42	  form-action 'self';
43	  frame-ancestors 'none';
44	  upgrade-insecure-requests;
45	`;
46	// Set on both request and response headers. Full implementation in reference file.
47	```
48	
49	### Rules
50	
51	- **Dev mode requires `'unsafe-eval'`** for React error stack traces and `'unsafe-inline'` for Tailwind HMR — NOT in production
52	- **CSP makes pages dynamically rendered** — nonces change per request, so CSP pages cannot be statically generated
53	- **If adding third-party scripts**, add their domains to `script-src` and `connect-src`
54	- **Read the nonce** in Server Components via `(await headers()).get("x-nonce")` for `<Script>` tags
55	
56	> Full `proxy.ts` CSP implementation and CSP directives reference: [AGENTS-SECURITY-REFERENCE.md](./AGENTS-SECURITY-REFERENCE.md#csp-full-implementation)
57	
58	---
59	
60	## Security Headers
61	
62	Six headers configured in `next.config.ts` via the `headers()` function:
63	
64	| Header                                             | Purpose                                                    |
65	| -------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
66	| `X-DNS-Prefetch-Control: on`                       | DNS prefetching for external links                         |
67	| `Strict-Transport-Security`                        | Forces HTTPS for 2 years, all subdomains, preload-eligible |
68	| `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN`                      | Prevents iframe embedding (clickjacking)                   |
69	| `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`                  | Prevents MIME-type sniffing                                |
70	| `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin` | Limits referrer info on cross-origin                       |
71	| `Permissions-Policy`                               | Disables camera, microphone, geolocation, browsing-topics  |
72	
73	### Rules
74	
75	- **Do NOT add `X-XSS-Protection`** — deprecated, can introduce vulnerabilities. CSP replaces it
76	- **Do NOT set `Cache-Control` for `_next/static`** — Next.js handles immutable caching automatically
77	- **HSTS preload** — only submit to preload list after confirming HTTPS on all subdomains (irreversible)
78	
79	> Full `next.config.ts` headers implementation: [AGENTS-SECURITY-REFERENCE.md](./AGENTS-SECURITY-REFERENCE.md#security-headers-implementation)
80	
81	---
82	
83	## Auth Protection Pattern
84	
85	Two-layer approach as recommended by [better-auth Next.js docs](https://www.better-auth.com/docs/integrations/next#auth-protection):
86	
87	**Layer 1 — Optimistic redirects via `proxy.ts`** (UX only, NOT secure):
88	
89	- Checks cookie existence only — no DB call, no session validation
90	- Logged-in users on `/login` → redirect to `/dashboard`
91	- Logged-out users on `/dashboard` → redirect to `/login`
92	- Anyone can forge a cookie — this layer is purely for avoiding page flash
93	
94	**Layer 2 — Real auth in every page/action** (the actual security):
95	
96	```typescript
97	// Every protected page and Server Action must do this:
98	const session = await getServerSession();
99	if (!session) redirect('/login');
100	```
101	
102	`getServerSession()` in `lib/server-session.ts` validates the session against the database, wrapped in `cache()` to deduplicate within a request.
103	
104	### Rules
105	
106	- **NEVER rely on `proxy.ts` for security** — it only checks cookie existence
107	- **ALWAYS call `getServerSession()` in every protected page and every Server Action**
108	- **`cache()` wrapping** ensures multiple calls in the same request only hit the DB once
109	- **Session cookie cache (5 min)** in `lib/auth.ts` reduces DB load — tradeoff: revoked session valid up to 5 min
110	- **Add `"server-only"` import** to `server-session.ts`
111	
112	---
113	
114	## Server Actions Security
115	
116	Every action follows the **4-step pattern**: authenticate → validate → execute → revalidate. See [AGENTS-PATTERNS.md § Server Action Hardening](./AGENTS-PATTERNS.md#2-server-action-hardening-strategy-like) for the template.
117	
118	### Rules
119	
120	- **Step 1 (Auth) is mandatory** — `getServerSession()` first, redirect if `null`
121	- **Step 2 uses Zod `.safeParse()`** — never trust `formData.get()` directly
122	- **Step 3 uses Drizzle ORM** — never concatenate strings into SQL
123	- **Never expose internal errors** — return user-friendly messages, log internals server-side
124	- **`formData.get()` returns `FormDataEntryValue | null`** — handle `null` before Zod
125	- **Remove all `console.log` statements** from production code
126	
127	### Revalidate vs Redirect (Step 4)
128	
129	| Scenario                              | Use                                     | Why                   |
130	| ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
131	| **Create** (user on `/new` or dialog) | `redirect("/dashboard/entities")`       | Navigate back to list |
132	| **Update** (user stays on same page)  | `revalidatePath("/dashboard/entities")` | Refresh in-place      |
133	| **Delete** (user stays on same page)  | `revalidatePath("/dashboard/entities")` | Seamless UI refresh   |
134	
135	`redirect()` already triggers a fresh render — a preceding `revalidatePath()` to the same path is redundant.
136	
137	---
138	
139	## Input Validation with Zod
140	
141	Schemas in `lib/schemas/` — see [AGENTS-PATTERNS.md § Zod Schemas](./AGENTS-PATTERNS.md#2-server-action-hardening-strategy-like).
142	
143	- **Validate on the server** — client-side validation is UX only; the Server Action is the security boundary
144	- **Use `.safeParse()`** — graceful error handling without try-catch
145	- **Set max lengths** — prevent DoS via long inputs; match DB column constraints
146	- **Use `.or(z.literal(""))` for optional URL fields** — empty form strings aren't valid URLs
147	- **Transform empty strings to `undefined`** via `.transform()`
148	
149	---
150	
151	## SQL Injection Prevention
152	
153	Drizzle ORM produces parameterized queries by default. Safe patterns:
154	
155	```typescript
156	db.select().from(projects).where(eq(projects.id, id)); // Query builder — safe
157	db.insert(projects).values({ title, description }); // Insert — safe
158	sql<number>`COALESCE(MAX(${projects.order}), 0)`; // sql template — safe (parameterized)
159	```
160	
161	**Never do**:
162	
163	- `db.execute(\`SELECT \* FROM projects WHERE id = ${id}\`)` — SQL injection
164	- `sql.raw(\`... WHERE title = '${title}'\`)` — SQL injection
165	- Dynamic table/column names from user input
166	
167	### Rules
168	
169	- **Always use the Drizzle query builder** or `sql` template literal
170	- **Never use `sql.raw()` with user input**
171	- **Validate IDs as numbers before queries** — even though Drizzle parameterizes
172	
173	---
174	
175	## Secure Environment Variables
176	
177	| Pattern         | Exposure                                   | Examples                                                       |
178	| --------------- | ------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
179	| `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` | Bundled in client JS (visible to everyone) | `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL`                                          |
180	| No prefix       | Server-only (never sent to browser)        | `TURSO_DATABASE_URL`, `TURSO_AUTH_TOKEN`, `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` |
181	
182	### Rules
183	
184	- **NEVER prefix secrets with `NEXT_PUBLIC_`**
185	- **NEVER commit `.env.local` to git** — verify `.gitignore` includes it
186	- **Generate `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`** with `openssl rand -base64 32` (at least 32 chars)
187	- **On Vercel, use Sensitive Environment Variables** — encrypted, non-readable after creation
188	- **Use different values per environment** (Production, Preview, Development)
189	
190	---
191	
192	## CSRF Protection
193	
194	- **better-auth verifies `Origin` header** on all mutation requests — rejects if origin doesn't match `trustedOrigins`
195	- **Next.js Server Actions are protected by default** — framework validates `Origin` header; no additional CSRF tokens needed
196	- **Do NOT set `disableCSRFCheck: true`** or `disableOriginCheck: true` in better-auth
197	- **Session cookies use `SameSite: 'lax'`** by default — allows top-level navigations, blocks cross-site form submissions
198	- **Custom API routes** (beyond `/api/auth/*`) need manual CSRF token verification
199	
200	---
```

1	# AGENTS-PERFORMANCE.md
2	
3	Performance guidelines for the portfolio project — project-specific guidance that ties together the installed skills.
4	
5	> **Before implementing caching (`use cache`, PPR, `cacheLife`, `cacheTag`), execute the following skill** — read the SKILL.md and follow its instructions:
6	>
7	> 1. `.cursor/skills/next-cache-components/SKILL.md`
8	
9	> **Before optimizing bundle or rendering performance, execute the following skill** — read the SKILL.md and follow its instructions:
10	>
11	> 1. `.cursor/skills/vercel-react-best-practices/SKILL.md`
12	
13	> **Before adjusting Next.js data patterns or RSC boundaries, execute the following skill** — read the SKILL.md and follow its instructions:
14	>
15	> 1. `.cursor/skills/next-best-practices/SKILL.md`
16	
17	> **Before restructuring component tree for performance, execute the following skill** — read the SKILL.md and follow its instructions:
18	>
19	> 1. `.cursor/skills/vercel-composition-patterns/SKILL.md`
20	
21	---
22	
23	## React Compiler
24	
25	Enabled in this project (`reactCompiler: true` in `next.config.ts`). Automatically inserts memoization at build time.
26	
27	| Before (manual)                     | After (compiler handles it)         |
28	| ----------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
29	| `useMemo(() => calc(data), [data])` | `const result = calc(data)`         |
30	| `useCallback((id) => fn(id), [fn])` | `const handler = (id) => fn(id)`    |
31	| `React.memo(Component)`             | `function Component(props) { ... }` |
32	
33	### Rules
34	
35	- **Do NOT use `useMemo`, `useCallback`, or `React.memo`** — redundant with the compiler
36	- **Write plain, readable code** — the compiler optimizes it
37	- **Keep components pure** — same output for same props, no mutations during render
38	- **Side effects only in `useEffect`, event handlers, or Server Actions**
39	- **Do NOT use `React.forwardRef`** — React 19 supports `ref` as a regular prop
40	- If the compiler can't safely optimize code, it silently skips it (no errors)
41	
42	---
43	
44	## Dynamic Imports & Code Splitting
45	
46	Use `next/dynamic` to reduce initial JS bundle:
47	
48	```typescript
49	import dynamic from "next/dynamic";
50	
51	const HeavyEditor = dynamic(() => import("@/components/admin/editor"), {
52	  loading: () => <Spinner />,
53	});
54	
55	const ChartComponent = dynamic(() => import("@/components/chart"), {
56	  ssr: false,
57	  loading: () => <div className="h-64 animate-pulse bg-muted rounded-md" />,
58	});
59	```
60	
61	### When to Use
62	
63	- Heavy components not visible on initial load (modals, editors, charts)
64	- Admin-only components behind authentication
65	- Client-only libraries using browser APIs (`window`, `document`)
66	
67	### What NOT to Dynamically Import
68	
69	- Layout components (header, sidebar) — always needed immediately
70	- Small, lightweight components — overhead outweighs savings
71	- Server Components — automatically code-split by Next.js
72	
73	### Project-Specific Guidance
74	
75	| Component                  | Dynamic? | Reason                          |
76	| -------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------- |
77	| Admin sidebar/header       | No       | Always visible                  |
78	| Login form                 | No       | Lightweight, needed immediately |
79	| Skills multi-select (cmdk) | Yes      | Heavy dependency, only in forms |
80	| Data tables                | No       | Primary dashboard content       |
81	| Delete confirmation dialog | Yes      | Only on user action             |
82	| Public portfolio page      | No       | All content is primary          |
83	
84	---
85	
86	## Loading Files & Streaming
87	
88	`loading.tsx` files wrap their sibling `page.tsx` in `<Suspense>` automatically, streaming the layout while data loads.
89	
90	### Skeleton Pattern
91	
92	```typescript
93	// app/(admin)/dashboard/projects/loading.tsx
94	export default function Loading() {
95	  return (
96	    <div className="space-y-4">
97	      <div className="flex items-center justify-between">
98	        <div className="h-8 w-48 animate-pulse rounded-md bg-muted" />
99	        <div className="h-10 w-32 animate-pulse rounded-md bg-muted" />
100	      </div>
101	      {/* Match the shape of actual content to minimize layout shift */}
102	    </div>
103	  );
104	}
105	```
106	
107	### Granular Streaming
108	
109	For pages with multiple independent data sources, use separate `<Suspense>` boundaries:
110	
111	```typescript
112	<Suspense fallback={<StatsSkeleton />}>
113	  <DashboardStats />
114	</Suspense>
115	<Suspense fallback={<ProjectsSkeleton />}>
116	  <RecentProjects />
117	</Suspense>
118	```
119	
120	### Where to Add Loading Files
121	
122	| Route                                    | Needed? | Reason                     |
123	| ---------------------------------------- | ------- | -------------------------- |
124	| `app/(admin)/dashboard/*/page.tsx` (all) | Yes     | All fetch from DB          |
125	| `app/(public)/page.tsx`                  | Yes     | Fetches all portfolio data |
126	| `app/(admin)/login/page.tsx`             | No      | No data fetching           |
127	
128	---
129	
130	## Bundle Optimization
131	
132	### `optimizePackageImports`
133	
134	Already configured in `next.config.ts` for `lucide-react`, `react-icons`, `@radix-ui/react-icons`. Ensures only used exports are bundled even with barrel file imports.
135	
136	### Rules
137	
138	- **Import specific exports** — `import { Heart } from "lucide-react"`, not `import * as Icons`
139	- **No barrel imports** (`import * as ...`) — tree shaking may miss some
140	- **Analyze periodically** — `pnpm next experimental-analyze` to find oversized dependencies
141	
142	---
143	
144	## Server vs Client Decision Tree
145	
146	```
147	Is the component interactive (onClick, onChange, state, effects)?
148	├── NO → Server Component (default, no directive)
149	│   - Zero client JS, direct DB access, secrets stay on server
150	│
151	└── YES → Does the ENTIRE component need interactivity?
152	    ├── NO → Split: data fetching in Server Component, pass props to Client
153	    └── YES → Client Component ("use client")
154	        - Keep small, import into Server parent, never fetch data inside
155	```
156	
157	### Project-Specific Boundaries
158	
159	| Component                  | Type   | Reason                         |
160	| -------------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------ |
161	| Dashboard layout           | Server | Static structure               |
162	| Sidebar navigation         | Client | Active state, mobile toggle    |
163	| Projects list page         | Server | Data fetching, table rendering |
164	| Delete confirmation dialog | Client | Modal state, click handlers    |
165	| Login form                 | Client | Form state, submission         |
166	| Public portfolio page      | Server | Static rendering, SEO          |
167	| Skills multi-select        | Client | Combobox interactivity (cmdk)  |
168	
169	---
170	
171	## Core Web Vitals
172	
173	### LCP (Largest Contentful Paint) — Loading
174	
175	| Rating            | Threshold |
176	| ----------------- | --------- |
177	| Good              | <= 2.5s   |
178	| Needs Improvement | 2.5s–4.0s |
179	| Poor              | > 4.0s    |
180	
181	**Optimizations in this project**: `priority` on above-fold images, `next/font` for fonts, `"use cache"` + `cacheLife` for data, Server Components on public page, `loading.tsx` for instant shell.
182	
183	### INP (Interaction to Next Paint) — Interactivity
184	
185	| Rating            | Threshold   |
186	| ----------------- | ----------- |
187	| Good              | <= 200ms    |
188	| Needs Improvement | 200ms–500ms |
189	| Poor              | > 500ms     |
190	
191	**Optimizations**: React Compiler auto-memoization, Server Components by default (minimal client JS), dynamic imports for heavy components, `startTransition` for mutations.
192	
193	### CLS (Cumulative Layout Shift) — Visual Stability
194	
195	| Rating            | Threshold |
196	| ----------------- | --------- |
197	| Good              | <= 0.1    |
198	| Needs Improvement | 0.1–0.25  |
199	| Poor              | > 0.25    |
200
```
