```text
1	# AGENTS-ACCESSIBILITY.md
2	
3	Accessibility guidelines for the portfolio project — project-specific patterns using Next.js 16, shadcn/ui, Tailwind CSS 4.2, and Sonner.
4	
5	> **Before auditing or fixing accessibility, execute the following skills** — read each SKILL.md and follow its instructions:
6	>
7	> 1. `.cursor/skills/accessibility-compliance/SKILL.md`
8	> 2. `.cursor/skills/wcag-audit-patterns/SKILL.md`
9	
10	> **Before building or modifying shadcn/ui components with a11y requirements, execute the following skill** — read the SKILL.md and follow its instructions:
11	>
12	> 1. `.cursor/skills/shadcn/SKILL.md`
13	
14	---
15	
16	## Next.js Components over HTML
17	
18	**Always use Next.js components instead of HTML equivalents** — they provide built-in optimizations and accessibility.
19	
20	| HTML                 | Next.js Component | Import             | Why                                                          |
21	| -------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
22	| `<a>`                | `<Link>`          | `next/link`        | Client-side nav, prefetching, accessible by default          |
23	| `<form>`             | `<Form>`          | `next/form`        | Prefetches loading UI, progressive enhancement               |
24	| `<img>`              | `<Image>`         | `next/image`       | Lazy loading, responsive srcset, enforces `alt` + dimensions |
25	| Manual font `<link>` | `next/font`       | `next/font/google` | Self-hosted, zero layout shift                               |
26	| `<script>`           | `<Script>`        | `next/script`      | Loading strategies, avoids blocking                          |
27	
28	### Rules
29	
30	- **Never use `<a>` for internal links** — use `<Link>` (renders `<a>` with prefetching)
31	- **Never use `<img>`** — use `<Image>` which requires `alt`, `width`, `height` (or `fill`)
32	- **Never load fonts via `<link>` tags** — use `next/font` for self-hosting
33	- **Use `<Form>` from `next/form` for navigation forms** (search, filters); regular `<form>` with `action` is fine for Server Action mutations
34	
35	---
36	
37	## Semantic Layout Structure
38	
39	The public portfolio page must use semantic HTML landmarks in `(public)/layout.tsx`:
40	
41	```typescript
42	<>
43	  <SkipLink />
44	  <header>
45	    <nav aria-label="Main navigation">{/* Links */}</nav>
46	  </header>
47	  <main id="main-content" tabIndex={-1}>
48	    {children}
49	  </main>
50	  <footer>
51	    <nav aria-label="Social links">{/* Links */}</nav>
52	  </footer>
53	</>
54	```
55	
56	### Rules
57	
58	- Exactly **one `<main>`** per page
59	- `<nav>` needs `aria-label` when multiple navs exist on the same page
60	- Use `<section aria-labelledby="heading-id">` for major content sections (projects, experiences, skills)
61	- Admin dashboard uses shadcn `Sidebar` which handles landmarks via Radix
62	
63	### Section Pattern
64	
65	```typescript
66	<section aria-labelledby="projects-heading">
67	  <h2 id="projects-heading">Projects</h2>
68	  {/* Cards */}
69	</section>
70	```
71	
72	---
73	
74	## Skip Link
75	
76	Required for WCAG 2.4.1 (Bypass Blocks). Place as first child inside `<body>` or public layout.
77	
78	```typescript
79	// components/skip-link.tsx
80	export function SkipLink() {
81	  return (
82	    <a
83	      href="#main-content"
84	      className="sr-only focus:not-sr-only focus:absolute focus:top-4 focus:left-4 focus:z-50 focus:px-4 focus:py-2 focus:bg-primary focus:text-primary-foreground focus:rounded-md focus:outline-none focus:ring-2 focus:ring-ring focus:ring-offset-2"
85	    >
86	      Skip to main content
87	    </a>
88	  );
89	}
90	```
91	
92	The `<main>` element must have `id="main-content"` and `tabIndex={-1}` to receive focus.
93	
94	---
95	
96	## shadcn Component Accessibility Notes
97	
98	### Icon Buttons Need `aria-label`
99	
100	```typescript
101	// Icon-only button — MUST have aria-label
102	<Button variant="ghost" size="icon" aria-label="Delete project">
103	  <Trash2 className="h-4 w-4" aria-hidden="true" />
104	</Button>
105	```
106	
107	### Dialog — Auto-Accessible
108	
109	shadcn `Dialog` (Radix) automatically traps focus, returns focus on close, closes on Escape. **Always include `DialogTitle` and `DialogDescription`** — Radix uses them for `aria-labelledby`/`aria-describedby`. Hide description visually with `sr-only` if needed.
110	
111	### Table — Add `scope` and `caption`
112	
113	```typescript
114	<Table>
115	  <TableCaption>Portfolio projects managed from the dashboard</TableCaption>
116	  <TableHeader>
117	    <TableRow>
118	      <TableHead scope="col">Title</TableHead>
119	      <TableHead scope="col">Status</TableHead>
120	      <TableHead scope="col">Actions</TableHead>
121	    </TableRow>
122	  </TableHeader>
123	  <TableBody>
124	    {projects.map((p) => (
125	      <TableRow key={p.id}>
126	        <TableCell>{p.title}</TableCell>
127	        <TableCell>{p.status}</TableCell>
128	        <TableCell>
129	          <Button variant="ghost" size="icon" aria-label={`Edit ${p.title}`}>
130	            <Pencil className="h-4 w-4" aria-hidden="true" />
131	          </Button>
132	        </TableCell>
133	      </TableRow>
134	    ))}
135	  </TableBody>
136	</Table>
137	```
138	
139	### Select, DropdownMenu, Tabs
140	
141	Auto-accessible via Radix. Just ensure: `Select` has a visible label (or `aria-label`), `DropdownMenu` trigger has a descriptive name, `Tabs` content is associated automatically.
142	
143	---
144	
145	## Accessible Forms
146	
147	Every form field must have: (1) visible `<Label>`, (2) error messages via `aria-describedby`, (3) `aria-invalid` on error, (4) `aria-required` for required fields.
148	
149	shadcn's `FormField` + `FormLabel` + `FormMessage` handles this automatically with React Hook Form. Add `aria-required="true"` on required inputs.
150	
151	### Required Field Indication
152	
153	```typescript
154	<FormLabel>
155	  Project Title <span aria-label="required" className="text-destructive">*</span>
156	</FormLabel>
157	```
158	
159	### Rules
160	
161	- **Never use toasts as the only error feedback** — show inline errors via `FormMessage` first; toasts are supplementary
162	- **Toast messages must convey meaning via text** — screen readers can't see icon colors
163	
164	---
165	
166	## Sonner Toasts
167	
168	Sonner handles ARIA live regions automatically:
169	
170	- Success/info toasts: `aria-live="polite"` (non-interrupting)
171	- Error toasts: `role="alert"` (interrupting)
172	- Keyboard-dismissible
173	
174	**Rules**: Always provide descriptive text messages. Keep to 1-2 sentences.
175	
176	---
177	
178	## Accessible Images
179	
180	Always use `next/image` which enforces `alt` at the TypeScript level.
181	
182	| Image Type         | Alt Text                                                          |
183	| ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
184	| Project screenshot | Describe what it shows: `"Dashboard view of task management app"` |
185	| Company logo       | Company name: `"Vercel logo"`                                     |
186	| Decorative         | `alt="" aria-hidden="true"`                                       |
187	| Profile photo      | `"Gonzalo Pozo, Full Stack Developer"`                            |
188	
189	### Rules
190	
191	- **Informative images need meaningful alt text** — TypeScript enforces the prop exists but not the value
192	- **Decorative images**: `alt=""` + `aria-hidden="true"`
193	- **Complex images**: use `<figure>` + `<figcaption>` + `aria-describedby`
194	
195	---
196	
197	## Motion Preferences
198	
199	Add to `app/globals.css` to disable animations for users who prefer reduced motion:
200
```

1	# AGENTS-DESIGN.md
2	
3	Visual design system for the portfolio's public page — theme tokens, bento grid vocabulary, card anatomy, pill navbar, and interactive patterns.
4	
5	> **Before applying or extending this design system, execute the following skills** — read each SKILL.md and follow its instructions:
6	>
7	> 1. `.cursor/skills/shadcn/SKILL.md` (component styling, token usage)
8	> 2. `.cursor/skills/tailwind-design-system/SKILL.md` (Tailwind v4 `@theme`, OKLCH)
9	> 3. `.cursor/skills/frontend-design/SKILL.md` (visual quality, polish)
10	> 4. `.cursor/skills/web-design-guidelines/SKILL.md` (compliance review)
11	
12	**Related coverage in other AGENTS files (do not duplicate):**
13	
14	- `AGENTS-ANIMATIONS.md` — timing, easing, Motion/NumberFlow rules
15	- `AGENTS-ACCESSIBILITY.md` — contrast ratios, touch targets, reduced motion, landmarks
16	- `AGENTS-PERFORMANCE.md` — code splitting, loading states, bundle optimization
17	
18	---
19	
20	## 1. Design Philosophy
21	
22	Spatial density and card scale ARE the visual language. Visual hierarchy comes from card size contrast, not from typographic weight or color loudness. The portfolio should feel **technical but warm** — a developer who cares about craft.
23	
24	### Principles
25	
26	1. **Cards first** — every piece of content lives inside a card. The grid IS the layout.
27	2. **Generous radii** — large corner radii on cards, pill-shaped nav. Soften the technical content.
28	3. **Surface contrast, not shadow** — cards float via background-to-card color difference, not drop shadows.
29	4. **Luminous accent on dark** — dark mode is the hero. Primary cyan glows, amber accent energizes.
30	5. **Restraint** — one primary, one accent, cool neutrals. No color noise.
31	6. **Every decision works in both themes** — light and dark are designed in parallel, not as afterthoughts.
32	
33	---
34	
35	## 2. Theme Tokens
36	
37	All color values are in OKLCH for perceptual uniformity (as recommended by the `tailwind-design-system` skill). The tokens map directly to shadcn/ui's variable system and the existing `@theme inline` block in `globals.css`.
38	
39	> **Implementation note**: when applying these tokens, replace the hex values in `:root` and `.dark` selectors in `globals.css`. The `@theme inline` block that maps `--color-*: var(--*)` stays unchanged.
40	
41	### 2.1 Color Palette — Light Mode
42	
43	Design intent: Lavender-tinted off-white background, pure white cards, deep sapphire primary, vivid warm gold accent. Distinctly indigo-leaning — not teal.
44	
45	```css
46	:root {
47		--background: oklch(0.975 0.008 270);
48		--foreground: oklch(0.155 0.025 270);
49	
50		--card: oklch(1 0 0);
51		--card-foreground: oklch(0.155 0.025 270);
52	
53		--popover: oklch(1 0 0);
54		--popover-foreground: oklch(0.155 0.025 270);
55	
56		--primary: oklch(0.4 0.17 250);
57		--primary-foreground: oklch(0.985 0.005 250);
58	
59		--secondary: oklch(0.945 0.012 270);
60		--secondary-foreground: oklch(0.195 0.025 270);
61	
62		--muted: oklch(0.92 0.008 270);
63		--muted-foreground: oklch(0.43 0.02 265);
64	
65		--accent: oklch(0.7 0.18 55);
66		--accent-foreground: oklch(0.2 0.05 55);
67	
68		--destructive: oklch(0.55 0.22 25);
69		--destructive-foreground: oklch(0.985 0.005 25);
70	
71		--border: oklch(0.885 0.012 270);
72		--input: oklch(0.885 0.012 270);
73		--ring: oklch(0.48 0.17 250);
74	}
75	```
76	
77	### 2.2 Color Palette — Dark Mode
78	
79	Design intent: Deep indigo-black surface with real blue tint, elevated cards with indigo sheen, electric blue primary, vivid gold accent. Moody and immersive.
80	
81	```css
82	.dark {
83		--background: oklch(0.12 0.025 275);
84		--foreground: oklch(0.95 0.008 265);
85	
86		--card: oklch(0.175 0.022 270);
87		--card-foreground: oklch(0.95 0.008 265);
88	
89		--popover: oklch(0.175 0.022 270);
90		--popover-foreground: oklch(0.95 0.008 265);
91	
92		--primary: oklch(0.75 0.17 235);
93		--primary-foreground: oklch(0.12 0.035 235);
94	
95		--secondary: oklch(0.225 0.018 275);
96		--secondary-foreground: oklch(0.91 0.008 265);
97	
98		--muted: oklch(0.225 0.018 275);
99		--muted-foreground: oklch(0.58 0.016 265);
100	
101		--accent: oklch(0.8 0.17 50);
102		--accent-foreground: oklch(0.12 0.045 50);
103	
104		--destructive: oklch(0.64 0.2 25);
105		--destructive-foreground: oklch(0.12 0.025 25);
106	
107		--border: oklch(0.265 0.018 275);
108		--input: oklch(0.265 0.018 275);
109		--ring: oklch(0.75 0.17 235);
110	}
111	```
112	
113	### 2.3 Color Design Rationale
114	
115	| Token              | Light                                        | Dark                                         | Design intent                                                   |
116	| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
117	| `background`       | Lavender off-white (L=0.975, C=0.008, H=270) | Deep indigo-black (L=0.12, C=0.025, H=275)   | Tinted surfaces with personality, not neutral                   |
118	| `card`             | Pure white (L=1.0)                           | Elevated indigo (L=0.175, C=0.022, H=270)    | Cards float above background via surface contrast               |
119	| `primary`          | Deep sapphire (L=0.40, C=0.17, H=250)        | Electric blue (L=0.75, C=0.17, H=235)        | Signature color — rich indigo-blue, clearly different from teal |
120	| `accent`           | Vivid warm gold (L=0.70, C=0.18, H=55)       | Bright gold (L=0.80, C=0.17, H=50)           | Complementary warmth, high saturation for CTAs                  |
121	| `muted-foreground` | Mid gray (L=0.43)                            | Subdued gray (L=0.58)                        | Secondary text — verify ≥ 4.5:1 contrast during implementation  |
122	| `border`           | Cool lavender line (L=0.885, C=0.012, H=270) | Indigo-tinted line (L=0.265, C=0.018, H=275) | Visible but non-competing                                       |
123	
124	The hue axis centers on **H=250** (sapphire-indigo) for primary and **H=50–55** (warm gold) for accent — a complementary pair that creates strong visual tension. All neutral surfaces share **H=265–275** (cool indigo-gray) for cohesion. Chroma is pushed higher than typical (C=0.17) for both primary and accent to give the palette real personality.
125	
126	### 2.4 Status Tokens
127	
128	Replace hardcoded status colors (e.g., `text-green-600`, `text-amber-400`, `text-cyan-600` in `grid-item.tsx`) with semantic tokens:
129	
130	```css
131	:root {
132		--status-active: oklch(0.52 0.175 155);
133		--status-in-progress: oklch(0.48 0.17 250);
134		--status-archived: oklch(0.62 0.15 70);
135	}
136	.dark {
137		--status-active: oklch(0.7 0.175 155);
138		--status-in-progress: oklch(0.7 0.15 235);
139		--status-archived: oklch(0.74 0.15 70);
140	}
141	```
142	
143	Register in `@theme inline`:
144	
145	```css
146	--color-status-active: var(--status-active);
147	--color-status-in-progress: var(--status-in-progress);
148	--color-status-archived: var(--status-archived);
149	```
150	
151	Usage: `text-status-active`, `text-status-in-progress`, `text-status-archived`.
152	
153	### 2.5 Chart Palette
154	
155	Five-color palette derived from the primary/accent axis, perceptually balanced for data visualization:
156	
157	```css
158	:root {
159		--chart-1: oklch(0.4 0.17 250);
160		--chart-2: oklch(0.6 0.2 35);
161		--chart-3: oklch(0.5 0.18 300);
162		--chart-4: oklch(0.5 0.14 185);
163		--chart-5: oklch(0.55 0.17 145);
164	}
165	.dark {
166		--chart-1: oklch(0.75 0.17 235);
167		--chart-2: oklch(0.74 0.17 35);
168		--chart-3: oklch(0.7 0.16 300);
169		--chart-4: oklch(0.68 0.13 185);
170		--chart-5: oklch(0.72 0.16 145);
171	}
172	```
173	
174	### 2.6 Sidebar Tokens (Admin Dashboard)
175	
176	Mirror the card surface for seamless integration. The sidebar is admin-only; these values keep it visually consistent with the main theme.
177	
178	```css
179	:root {
180		--sidebar: oklch(1 0 0);
181		--sidebar-foreground: oklch(0.155 0.025 270);
182		--sidebar-primary: oklch(0.4 0.17 250);
183		--sidebar-primary-foreground: oklch(0.985 0.005 250);
184		--sidebar-accent: oklch(0.945 0.012 270);
185		--sidebar-accent-foreground: oklch(0.195 0.025 270);
186		--sidebar-border: oklch(0.885 0.012 270);
187		--sidebar-ring: oklch(0.48 0.17 250);
188	}
189	.dark {
190		--sidebar: oklch(0.175 0.022 270);
191		--sidebar-foreground: oklch(0.95 0.008 265);
192		--sidebar-primary: oklch(0.75 0.17 235);
193		--sidebar-primary-foreground: oklch(0.12 0.035 235);
194		--sidebar-accent: oklch(0.225 0.018 275);
195		--sidebar-accent-foreground: oklch(0.91 0.008 265);
196		--sidebar-border: oklch(0.265 0.018 275);

199	```

```text
1	# AGENTS-ANIMATIONS.md
2	
3	Animation guidelines for the portfolio project — when and how to use the three animation layers: Tailwind CSS, Motion (Framer Motion), and NumberFlow.
4	
5	**Animation libraries in this project:**
6	
7	- `tw-animate-css` — Tailwind-compatible animation utilities used by shadcn/ui (fadeIn, slideIn, etc.)
8	- `motion` (v12+) — React animation library for layout, gestures, exit animations, orchestration
9	- `@number-flow/react` — Animated number component for counters and statistics
10	
11	> **Before designing or implementing animations/visual polish, execute the following skill** — read the SKILL.md and follow its instructions:
12	>
13	> 1. `.cursor/skills/frontend-design/SKILL.md`
14	
15	**Related coverage in other AGENTS files (do not duplicate):**
16	
17	- `AGENTS-ACCESSIBILITY.md` > Motion Preferences — `prefers-reduced-motion` CSS
18	- `AGENTS-PERFORMANCE.md` > Dynamic Imports — `next/dynamic` for heavy components
19	
20	---
21	
22	## When to Use Each Layer
23	
24	| Situation                                    | Use                                                 | Why                              |
25	| -------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
26	| Spinners, pulses, simple hover effects       | **Tailwind** (`animate-*`, `transition-*`)          | Zero JS, GPU-accelerated         |
27	| shadcn component transitions (Dialog, Sheet) | **tw-animate-css** (built in)                       | Pre-configured, consistent       |
28	| Icon state changes (copy→check, like toggle) | **Motion** (`AnimatePresence`)                      | CSS can't do enter/exit cleanly  |
29	| Layout animations (list reorder, add/remove) | **Motion** (`layout` prop)                          | CSS can't animate FLIP           |
30	| Animated number counters                     | **NumberFlow**                                      | Purpose-built, accessible        |
31	| Page transitions                             | **Motion** or CSS View Transitions                  | Prefer CSS for simple fades      |
32	| Scroll-triggered animations                  | **Motion** (`useInView`) or Tailwind `motion-safe:` | Motion for complex orchestration |
33	
34	### Rules
35	
36	- **Default to Tailwind** — no JS overhead
37	- **Motion requires `"use client"`** — uses hooks and event handlers
38	- **NumberFlow only for numeric values**
39	- **Never install GSAP, anime.js, etc.** — Motion covers all needs
40	
41	---
42	
43	## Tailwind CSS Animations
44	
45	### Built-in Utilities
46	
47	| Utility          | Use                    |
48	| ---------------- | ---------------------- |
49	| `animate-spin`   | Loading spinners       |
50	| `animate-ping`   | Notification badges    |
51	| `animate-pulse`  | Skeleton loaders       |
52	| `animate-bounce` | Scroll-down indicators |
53	
54	### Transition Pattern
55	
56	```typescript
57	<div className="transition-transform duration-200 ease-out hover:-translate-y-0.5">
58	  {/* Card hover lift */}
59	</div>
60	```
61	
62	### Reduced Motion
63	
64	Use `motion-safe:` and `motion-reduce:` variants:
65	
66	```typescript
67	<svg className="motion-safe:animate-spin h-5 w-5" />
68	```
69	
70	### Custom Animations
71	
72	Define in `globals.css` via `@theme` directive for reusable animations:
73	
74	```css
75	@theme {
76		--animate-wiggle: wiggle 0.3s ease-in-out;
77		@keyframes wiggle {
78			0%,
79			100% {
80				transform: rotate(-3deg);
81			}
82			50% {
83				transform: rotate(3deg);
84			}
85		}
86	}
87	```
88	
89	Use as `animate-wiggle`. Prefer this over inline `animate-[...]` for animations used more than once.
90	
91	---
92	
93	## Motion (Framer Motion)
94	
95	Import from `motion/react` (not `framer-motion` — package renamed):
96	
97	```typescript
98	'use client';
99	import { motion, AnimatePresence } from 'motion/react';
100	```
101	
102	### Basic Animation
103	
104	```typescript
105	<motion.div
106	  initial={{ opacity: 0, y: 10 }}
107	  animate={{ opacity: 1, y: 0 }}
108	  transition={{ duration: 0.3, ease: "easeOut" }}
109	>
110	  {children}
111	</motion.div>
112	```
113	
114	### Enter/Exit Animations (AnimatePresence)
115	
116	Wrap items that mount/unmount to animate exits:
117	
118	```typescript
119	<AnimatePresence mode="wait" initial={false}>
120	  {isCopied ? (
121	    <motion.div key="check"
122	      initial={{ scale: 0 }} animate={{ scale: 1 }} exit={{ scale: 0 }}
123	      transition={{ duration: 0.15 }}>
124	      <Check className="h-4 w-4" aria-hidden="true" />
125	    </motion.div>
126	  ) : (
127	    <motion.div key="copy" /* same animation props */>
128	      <Copy className="h-4 w-4" aria-hidden="true" />
129	    </motion.div>
130	  )}
131	</AnimatePresence>
132	```
133	
134	### Layout Animations
135	
136	Use `layout` prop for automatic FLIP when size/position changes:
137	
138	```typescript
139	<motion.ul layout>
140	  <AnimatePresence>
141	    {items.map((item) => (
142	      <motion.li key={item.id} layout
143	        initial={{ opacity: 0 }} animate={{ opacity: 1 }} exit={{ opacity: 0 }}
144	        transition={{ duration: 0.2 }}>
145	        {item.title}
146	      </motion.li>
147	    ))}
148	  </AnimatePresence>
149	</motion.ul>
150	```
```
</details></tool-use>

1	# AGENTS-TESTING.md
2	
3	Testing strategy, conventions, and project-specific patterns for a Next.js 16 application tested with Vitest (unit) and Playwright (E2E).
4	
5	> Full mock code blocks, CI workflow YAML, and auth setup: [AGENTS-TESTING-REFERENCE.md](./AGENTS-TESTING-REFERENCE.md)
6	
7	> **Before writing Vitest unit tests, execute the following skill** — read the SKILL.md and follow its instructions:
8	>
9	> 1. `.cursor/skills/vitest/SKILL.md`
10	
11	> **Before writing Playwright E2E tests, execute the following skill** — read the SKILL.md and follow its instructions:
12	>
13	> 1. `.cursor/skills/playwright-best-practices/SKILL.md`
14	
15	**Related coverage in other AGENTS files (do not duplicate):**
16	
17	- `AGENTS-SECURITY.md` — 4-step authenticate/validate/execute/revalidate pattern that tests must verify
18	- `AGENTS-ACCESSIBILITY.md` — Manual a11y testing checklist
19	
20	---
21	
22	## Testing Philosophy
23	
24	### TDD Where It Hurts
25	
26	Use TDD (test first) where bugs have real impact and the feedback loop is fast. Use Test-After for framework-coupled or UI-heavy code.
27	
28	| Code Layer                           | Strategy                                  | Tool         |
29	| ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------- | ------------ |
30	| Zod validation schemas               | **TDD** (test first)                      | Vitest       |
31	| Utility functions (`lib/utils.ts`)   | **TDD** (test first)                      | Vitest       |
32	| Server Action logic                  | **TDD for validation, Test-After for DB** | Vitest       |
33	| Junction table sync logic            | **Test-After**                            | Vitest       |
34	| Client Components with custom logic  | **Test-After** (optional)                 | Vitest + RTL |
35	| Pages, layouts, route flows          | **Test-After**                            | Playwright   |
36	| Auth flows (login, protected routes) | **Test-After**                            | Playwright   |
37	| Public page rendering                | **Test-After**                            | Playwright   |
38	
39	**TDD cycle**: Red (failing test) → Green (minimum code to pass) → Refactor (clean up, tests stay green) → Repeat.
40	
41	### When NOT to Write Tests
42	
43	- **shadcn/ui primitives** — already tested by Radix UI upstream
44	- **better-auth configuration** — declarative config, not testable logic
45	- **Tailwind CSS classes** — visual output, not unit-testable
46	- **Next.js framework behavior** (routing, layouts, streaming) — tested by the Next.js team
47	- **Simple data fetching pages** with no business logic — covered by E2E naturally
48	- **React Server Components with unit tests** — async RSCs not supported by any unit testing tool; use Playwright
49	
50	---
51	
52	## Tool Setup
53	
54	### Vitest
55	
56	**Config file**: `vitest.config.mts` — already in the repo.
57	
58	Project-specific settings:
59	
60	- `environment: 'jsdom'` — simulates DOM for component tests (override per-file with `// @vitest-environment node`)
61	- `plugins: [tsconfigPaths()]` — resolves `@/*` path alias
62	- `include: ['tests/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}']` — only `tests/` directory
63	- `exclude: ['e2e/**']` — keeps Playwright tests separate
64	- `globals: false` — explicit imports required
65	- `css: false` — skips Tailwind processing in tests
66	
67	### Playwright
68	
69	**Config file**: `playwright.config.ts` — already in the repo.
70	
71	Project-specific settings:
72	
73	- `testDir: './e2e'` — all E2E tests in `e2e/`
74	- `baseURL: 'http://localhost:3000'` — enables `page.goto('/')`
75	- `webServer: { command: 'pnpm dev' }` — auto-starts dev server
76	- `trace: 'on-first-retry'` — captures traces for debugging CI failures
77	- `forbidOnly: !!process.env.CI` — fails CI if `.only` is left in
78	
79	---
80	
81	## Test File Location & Naming
82	
83	```
84	tests/                         # Vitest unit & component tests
85	├── schemas/                   # Zod schema validation tests
86	│   ├── project.test.ts
87	│   ├── experience.test.ts
88	│   ├── skill.test.ts
89	│   ├── social-link.test.ts
90	│   └── settings.test.ts
91	├── actions/                   # Server Action logic tests
92	│   └── projects.test.ts       # (one per entity)
93	├── utils/
94	│   └── utils.test.ts
95	└── components/                # Client component tests (optional)
96	
97	e2e/                           # Playwright E2E tests
98	├── auth.spec.ts               # Login, logout, protected route redirects
99	├── projects.spec.ts           # CRUD flows
100	├── public-page.spec.ts        # Public portfolio rendering
101	└── accessibility.spec.ts      # axe-core automated checks
102	```
103	
104	### Naming Rules
105	
106	| Convention | Vitest                                                         | Playwright                                   |
107	| ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
108	| Extension  | `.test.ts` / `.test.tsx`                                       | `.spec.ts`                                   |
109	| Directory  | `tests/`                                                       | `e2e/`                                       |
110	| File names | Mirror source (`projects.test.ts` → `lib/actions/projects.ts`) | Named by flow (`auth.spec.ts`)               |
111	| Test names | Behavior: `"rejects empty title"`                              | User action: `"should create a new project"` |
112	
113	---
114	
115	## Mocking Strategy
116	
117	> Full mock code blocks with complete implementations: [AGENTS-TESTING-REFERENCE.md](./AGENTS-TESTING-REFERENCE.md#mocking-code-blocks)
118	
119	### Summary
120	
121	| Dependency                | Mock Target            | Pattern                                                                  |
122	| ------------------------- | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
123	| Database (Turso/Drizzle)  | `@/db`                 | `vi.mock("@/db", () => ({ db: { insert: vi.fn()... } }))`                |
124	| Authentication            | `@/lib/server-session` | `vi.mock(...)` then `vi.mocked(getServerSession).mockResolvedValue(...)` |
125	| `redirect()`              | `next/navigation`      | Mock to throw `Error("REDIRECT:/path")` — mirrors Next.js behavior       |
126	| `revalidatePath()`        | `next/cache`           | `vi.mock("next/cache", () => ({ revalidatePath: vi.fn() }))`             |
127	| `headers()` / `cookies()` | `next/headers`         | `vi.mock("next/headers", ...)`                                           |
128	| `FormData`                | Manual creation        | Helper: `createFormData(record)` — see reference file                    |
129	
130	### Rules
131	
132	- **Mock at the module level** (`vi.mock(...)`) — Vitest hoists these calls automatically
133	- **Use `vi.mocked()` for type-safe mock access** — gives TypeScript autocompletion
134	- **Reset mocks between tests** — `beforeEach(() => { vi.clearAllMocks(); })`
135	- **Don't mock what you're testing** — test the schema? Don't mock Zod. Test the action? Mock the DB, not the action
136	- **Prefer shallow mocks** — only mock what the specific test needs
137	
138	---
139	
140	## What to Test Per Entity
141	
142	### Vitest (Unit Tests)
143	
144	| What to Test                                  | Example                                                        |
145	| --------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
146	| Schema accepts valid data                     | All required fields present, correct types                     |
147	| Schema rejects missing required fields        | Empty title, empty description                                 |
148	| Schema rejects invalid values                 | Status `"deleted"` (not in enum), title over 200 chars         |
149	| Schema handles optional fields                | Empty URL allowed, invalid URL rejected                        |
150	| Schema `.or(z.literal(""))` for optional URLs | Empty string passes, `"not-a-url"` fails                       |
```

1	# React Composition Patterns
2	
3	**Version 1.0.0**  
4	Engineering  
5	January 2026
6	
7	> **Note:**  
8	> This document is mainly for agents and LLMs to follow when maintaining,  
9	> generating, or refactoring React codebases using composition. Humans  
10	> may also find it useful, but guidance here is optimized for automation  
11	> and consistency by AI-assisted workflows.
12	
13	---
14	
15	## Abstract
16	
17	Composition patterns for building flexible, maintainable React components. Avoid boolean prop proliferation by using compound components, lifting state, and composing internals. These patterns make codebases easier for both humans and AI agents to work with as they scale.
18	
19	---
20	
21	## Table of Contents
22	
23	1. [Component Architecture](#1-component-architecture) — **HIGH**
24	   - 1.1 [Avoid Boolean Prop Proliferation](#11-avoid-boolean-prop-proliferation)
25	   - 1.2 [Use Compound Components](#12-use-compound-components)
26	2. [State Management](#2-state-management) — **MEDIUM**
27	   - 2.1 [Decouple State Management from UI](#21-decouple-state-management-from-ui)
28	   - 2.2 [Define Generic Context Interfaces for Dependency Injection](#22-define-generic-context-interfaces-for-dependency-injection)
29	   - 2.3 [Lift State into Provider Components](#23-lift-state-into-provider-components)
30	3. [Implementation Patterns](#3-implementation-patterns) — **MEDIUM**
31	   - 3.1 [Create Explicit Component Variants](#31-create-explicit-component-variants)
32	   - 3.2 [Prefer Composing Children Over Render Props](#32-prefer-composing-children-over-render-props)
33	4. [React 19 APIs](#4-react-19-apis) — **MEDIUM**
34	   - 4.1 [React 19 API Changes](#41-react-19-api-changes)
35	
36	---
37	
38	## 1. Component Architecture
39	
40	**Impact: HIGH**
41	
42	Fundamental patterns for structuring components to avoid prop
43	proliferation and enable flexible composition.
44	
45	### 1.1 Avoid Boolean Prop Proliferation
46	
47	**Impact: CRITICAL (prevents unmaintainable component variants)**
48	
49	Don't add boolean props like `isThread`, `isEditing`, `isDMThread` to customize
50	
51	component behavior. Each boolean doubles possible states and creates
52	
53	unmaintainable conditional logic. Use composition instead.
54	
55	**Incorrect: boolean props create exponential complexity**
56	
57	```tsx
58	function Composer({
59	  onSubmit,
60	  isThread,
61	  channelId,
62	  isDMThread,
63	  dmId,
64	  isEditing,
65	  isForwarding,
66	}: Props) {
67	  return (
68	    <form>
69	      <Header />
70	      <Input />
71	      {isDMThread ? (
72	        <AlsoSendToDMField id={dmId} />
73	      ) : isThread ? (
74	        <AlsoSendToChannelField id={channelId} />
75	      ) : null}
76	      {isEditing ? (
77	        <EditActions />
78	      ) : isForwarding ? (
79	        <ForwardActions />
80	      ) : (
81	        <DefaultActions />
82	      )}
83	      <Footer onSubmit={onSubmit} />
84	    </form>
85	  )
86	}
87	```
88	
89	**Correct: composition eliminates conditionals**
90	
91	```tsx
92	// Channel composer
93	function ChannelComposer() {
94	  return (
95	    <Composer.Frame>
96	      <Composer.Header />
97	      <Composer.Input />
98	      <Composer.Footer>
99	        <Composer.Attachments />
100	        <Composer.Formatting />
```
</details></tool-use>

2	
3	**Version 1.0.0**  
4	Vercel Engineering

6	
7	> **Note:**  
8	> This document is mainly for agents and LLMs to follow when maintaining,

12	
13	---
14	
15	## Abstract
16	
17	Comprehensive performance optimization guide for React and Next.js applications, designed for AI agents and LLMs. Contains 40+ rules across 8 categories, prioritized by impact from critical (eliminating waterfalls, reducing bundle size) to incremental (advanced patterns). Each rule includes detailed explanations, real-world examples comparing incorrect vs. correct implementations, and specific impact metrics to guide automated refactoring and code generation.
18	
19	---
20	
21	## Table of Contents

## PROJECT STRUCTURE & FRAMEWORK DETECTION

### Frameworks/Languages Used:
- **Backend:** Next.js 16 (App Router), Node.js 24+
- **Frontend:** React 19, TypeScript (strict)
- **Styling:** Tailwind CSS 4.2 (with @tailwindcss/postcss), Radix UI primitives
- **Database:** Turso (libSQL) via Drizzle ORM
- **Authentication:** better-auth (email/password, sign-ups disabled)
- **UI Components:** shadcn/ui, cmdk (command palette), sonner (toasts)
- **Icons:** Lucide, react-icons
- **Animations:** Motion (Framer Motion v12+), @number-flow/react, tw-animate-css
- **Testing:** Vitest (unit), Playwright (E2E)
- **Build:** Turbopack, React Compiler enabled
- **Package Manager:** pnpm 10.33.0 (strict)

### Project Type:
**Portfolio CMS** — Personal portfolio website with:
- Public portfolio page (`app/(public)/`)
- Admin dashboard with authentication (`app/(admin)/dashboard/`)
- Entity management: projects, experiences, skills, social-links, settings
- Server Actions for CRUD operations
- Drizzle ORM for database operations

### Structure:
```
app/                   # Next.js 16 App Router
├── (admin)/          # Route group: protected dashboard

├── api/              # Auth routes (better-auth)

components/

lib/

e2e/                  # Playwright E2E tests

## KEY CONVENTIONS & GOTCHAS

### Code Naming:
- **Files:** kebab-case (`social-links.ts`)
- **Components:** PascalCase (`SkillsMultiSelect`)
- **Functions/Variables:** camelCase (`createProject`)
- **Database columns:** snake_case (Drizzle casing config)

### Architecture Patterns (4 core patterns):
1. **Container-Presentational:** pages call `getServerSession()` and query data, pass to presentational components
2. **Server Action Hardening:** authenticate → validate (Zod) → execute (try-catch) → revalidate
3. **Data Access Facade:** all reads go through `lib/queries/` (one file per entity)
4. **Error Boundaries:** `error.tsx` and `loading.tsx` for recovery and loading UI

### Security:
- **Two-layer auth:** optimistic redirect via `proxy.ts` (UX only) + real auth in pages/actions via `getServerSession()`
- **CSP with nonces** in proxy.ts
- **Server Actions validated** with Zod `.safeParse()`
- **SQL injection prevented** via Drizzle parameterized queries
- **CSRF protected** by better-auth + Next.js framework
- **Env vars:** secrets NOT prefixed with `NEXT_PUBLIC_` (but `.env` is committed!)

### Performance:
- **React Compiler enabled** — no need for useMemo/useCallback/React.memo
- **Code splitting** via `next/dynamic` for heavy components
- **Streaming** via `loading.tsx` Suspense boundaries
- **Bundle optimization:** lucide-react, react-icons, @radix-ui/react-icons configured with `optimizePackageImports`
- **Caching:** React Server Component caching (`cacheComponents: true`), `"use cache"` directive available

### Testing Strategy:
- **TDD for:** Zod schemas, utility functions, Server Action logic
- **Test-After for:** junction table sync, client components (optional), pages, auth flows
- **Tools:** Vitest (jsdom environment, jiti for TS config paths), Playwright (E2E, 3 browsers)
- **Mocking:** vi.mock at module level, use vi.mocked() for type-safe access

### Known Issues/Non-Obvious Gotchas:
1. **`.env` file is committed to git** containing production database tokens, auth secrets, and Blob credentials. Security risk.
2. **No error.tsx or loading.tsx files yet** — marked as needed in AGENTS-PATTERNS.md
3. **No sitemap.ts, robots.ts, or OG image generation** — SEO setup pending
4. **Playwright config** has webServer commented out (dev server setup incomplete)
5. **env files pattern:** should be `.env.local` (not committed), but `.env` is in repo. This contradicts `.gitignore`.
6. **Zod schemas exist but validation may not be complete** across all actions (migration in progress per AGENTS-PATTERNS.md)
7. **Skills directory (.agents/skills/)** takes 22+ folders; Prettier/CSpell skip it intentionally (`ignorePaths`)
8. **Husky hooks must be installed manually** — `ignore-scripts=true` in .npmrc, run `pnpm run hooks:install`

metadata:

Vitest is a next-generation testing framework powered by Vite. It provides a Jest-compatible API with native ESM, TypeScript, and JSX support out of the box. Vitest shares the same config, transformers, resolvers, and plugins with your Vite app.

**Key Features:**
- Vite-native: Uses Vite's transformation pipeline for fast HMR-like test updates
- Jest-compatible: Drop-in replacement for most Jest test suites
- Smart watch mode: Only reruns affected tests based on module graph
- Native ESM, TypeScript, JSX support without configuration
- Multi-threaded workers for parallel test execution
- Built-in coverage via V8 or Istanbul
- Snapshot testing, mocking, and spy utilities

> The skill is based on Vitest 3.x, generated at 2026-01-28.

This skill guides creation of distinctive, production-grade frontend interfaces that avoid generic "AI slop" aesthetics. Implement real working code with exceptional attention to aesthetic details and creative choices.

The user provides frontend requirements: a component, page, application, or interface to build. They may include context about the purpose, audience, or technical constraints.

## Design Thinking

Before coding, understand the context and commit to a BOLD aesthetic direction:
- **Purpose**: What problem does this interface solve? Who uses it?
- **Tone**: Pick an extreme: brutally minimal, maximalist chaos, retro-futuristic, organic/natural, luxury/refined, playful/toy-like, editorial/magazine, brutalist/raw, art deco/geometric, soft/pastel, industrial/utilitarian, etc. There are so many flavors to choose from. Use these for inspiration but design one that is true to the aesthetic direction.
- **Constraints**: Technical requirements (framework, performance, accessibility).
- **Differentiation**: What makes this UNFORGETTABLE? What's the one thing someone will remember?

**CRITICAL**: Choose a clear conceptual direction and execute it with precision. Bold maximalism and refined minimalism both work - the key is intentionality, not intensity.

Then implement working code (HTML/CSS/JS, React, Vue, etc.) that is:
- Production-grade and functional
- Visually striking and memorable
- Cohesive with a clear aesthetic point-of-view
- Meticulously refined in every detail

## Frontend Aesthetics Guidelines

Focus on:
- **Typography**: Choose fonts that are beautiful, unique, and interesting. Avoid generic fonts like Arial and Inter; opt instead for distinctive choices that elevate the frontend's aesthetics; unexpected, characterful font choices. Pair a distinctive display font with a refined body font.

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project

Personal portfolio with a public page and an admin dashboard (CMS) — Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4.2, Drizzle ORM, Turso, better-auth.

## Package Manager

**Always use pnpm.** Never use npm, npx, or yarn. Use `pnpm dlx` instead of `npx`.

## Commands

| Command | Description |
|---|---|
| `pnpm dev` | Dev server (Turbopack) |
| `pnpm build` | Production build |
| `pnpm lint` | ESLint |
| `pnpm lint:fix` | ESLint --fix |
| `pnpm format` | Prettier --write |
| `pnpm format:check` | Prettier --check |
| `pnpm spellcheck` | CSpell |
| `pnpm test` | Vitest (watch) |
| `pnpm test -- --run` | Vitest (single run) |
| `pnpm db:setup` | Drizzle generate + push |
| `pnpm knip` | Detect unused exports |

## Naming Conventions

- **Files**: kebab-case (`social-links.ts`)
- **Components**: PascalCase (`SkillsMultiSelect`)
- **Functions/Variables**: camelCase (`createProject`)
- **Database columns**: snake_case (Drizzle casing config)

## Code Style

- Tabs (width 4), single quotes, JSX double quotes, trailing commas, print width 100
- No `console.log` in `app/` and `components/` (`console.warn`/`console.error` OK)
- React Compiler is enabled — never use `useMemo`, `useCallback`, or `React.memo`
- ESLint flat config (`eslint.config.mts`) with React Compiler plugin at error level
- Prettier with `prettier-plugin-tailwindcss` (always last plugin)

## Architecture Patterns

1. **Container-Presentational**: pages call `getServerSession()` + query data → pass to presentational components
2. **Server Action Hardening**: authenticate → validate (Zod `.safeParse()`) → execute (try-catch) → `revalidatePath()`
3. **Data Access Facade**: all reads through `lib/queries/` (one file per entity)
4. **Error Boundaries**: `error.tsx` and `loading.tsx` per route segment

## Security

- Two-layer auth: optimistic redirect via `proxy.ts` (UX only) + real auth in pages/actions via `getServerSession()`
- Server Actions must validate input with Zod `.safeParse()` before any DB operation
- Never prefix secrets with `NEXT_PUBLIC_`
- CSP with nonces configured in proxy.ts

## Git Conventions

- Conventional Commits enforced via commitlint (`feat:`, `fix:`, `build:`, `docs:`, `perf:`, etc.)
- Pre-commit hook: lint-staged runs ESLint → Prettier → CSpell
- After cloning: run `pnpm run hooks:install` to set up Husky

## Adding Entities

Schema in `db/schema/` → `pnpm db:setup` → actions in `lib/actions/` → Zod schema in `lib/schemas/` → query in `lib/queries/` → dashboard page → public page.

## UI Components

Add in `components/ui/` using Radix primitives + Tailwind + `cn()`. Follow the design system in AGENTS-DESIGN.md for theme tokens, grid vocabulary, and card variants.

## Testing

- TDD for: Zod schemas, utility functions, Server Action logic
- Test-after for: junction table sync, client components, pages, auth flows
- Vitest with jsdom for unit tests (`tests/`), Playwright for E2E (`e2e/`)
- Use `vi.mock()` at module level, `vi.mocked()` for type-safe access

## Deep-Dive Guides

Read these files when working on related topics:

| Guide | When to read |
|---|---|
| AGENTS-SETUP.md | First-time setup, env vars, prerequisites |
| AGENTS-CONVENTIONS.md | JSDoc style, when and how to document |
| AGENTS-PATTERNS.md | Architecture — Container-Presentational, Server Action hardening, Data Access Facade |
| AGENTS-PATTERNS-REFERENCE.md | Full Next.js file-system conventions, detailed pattern implementations |
| AGENTS-SECURITY.md | Auth, CSP, headers, input validation, CSRF |
| AGENTS-SECURITY-REFERENCE.md | Full proxy.ts/CSP implementation, header configs |
| AGENTS-SEO.md | Metadata templates, OG images, sitemap, robots |
| AGENTS-PERFORMANCE.md | React Compiler, code splitting, loading states, Core Web Vitals |
| AGENTS-ACCESSIBILITY.md | Landmarks, skip link, forms, images, contrast, motion preferences |
| AGENTS-ANIMATIONS.md | Tailwind animations, Motion, NumberFlow |
| AGENTS-DESIGN.md | Theme tokens (OKLCH), bento grid system, card anatomy, typography |
| AGENTS-TESTING.md | Vitest, Playwright, mocking patterns, CI |
| AGENTS-TESTING-REFERENCE.md | Full mock code blocks, CI workflow YAML |

6	# Accessibility Compliance
7	
8	Master accessibility implementation to create inclusive experiences that work for everyone, including users with disabilities.
9	
10	## When to Use This Skill
11	
12	- Implementing WCAG 2.2 Level AA or AAA compliance
13	- Building screen reader accessible interfaces
14	- Adding keyboard navigation to interactive components
15	- Implementing focus management and focus trapping
16	- Creating accessible forms with proper labeling

21	## Core Capabilities
22	
23	### 1. WCAG 2.2 Guidelines
24	
25	- Perceivable: Content must be presentable in different ways
26	- Operable: Interface must be navigable with keyboard and assistive tech
27	- Understandable: Content and operation must be clear
28	- Robust: Content must work with current and future assistive technologies
29	
30	### 2. ARIA Patterns
31	
32	- Roles: Define element purpose (button, dialog, navigation)
33	- States: Indicate current condition (expanded, selected, disabled)
34	- Properties: Describe relationships and additional info (labelledby, describedby)
35	- Live regions: Announce dynamic content changes
36	
37	### 3. Keyboard Navigation
38	
39	- Focus order and tab sequence
40	- Focus indicators and visible focus states
41	- Keyboard shortcuts and hotkeys
42	- Focus trapping for modals and dialogs
43	
44	### 4. Screen Reader Support
45	
46	- Semantic HTML structure
47	- Alternative text for images
48	- Proper heading hierarchy
49	- Skip links and landmarks
50	
51	### 5. Mobile Accessibility
52	
53	- Touch target sizing (44x44dp minimum)
54	- VoiceOver and TalkBack compatibility
55	- Gesture alternatives
56	- Dynamic Type support
57	
58	## Quick Reference
59	
60	### WCAG 2.2 Success Criteria Checklist
61	
62	| Level | Criterion | Description                                          |
63	| ----- | --------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
64	| A     | 1.1.1     | Non-text content has text alternatives               |
65	| A     | 1.3.1     | Info and relationships programmatically determinable |
66	| A     | 2.1.1     | All functionality keyboard accessible                |
67	| A     | 2.4.1     | Skip to main content mechanism                       |
68	| AA    | 1.4.3     | Contrast ratio 4.5:1 (text), 3:1 (large text)        |
69	| AA    | 1.4.11    | Non-text contrast 3:1                                |
70	| AA    | 2.4.7     | Focus visible                                        |
71	| AA    | 2.5.8     | Target size minimum 24x24px (NEW in 2.2)             |
72	| AAA   | 1.4.6     | Enhanced contrast 7:1                                |
73	| AAA   | 2.5.5     | Target size minimum 44x44px                          |

76	
77	### Pattern 1: Accessible Button
78	
79	```tsx
80	interface ButtonProps extends React.ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement> {
81	  variant?: "primary" | "secondary";
82	  isLoading?: boolean;
83	}
84	
85	function AccessibleButton({
86	  children,
87	  variant = "primary",
88	  isLoading = false,
89	  disabled,
90	  ...props
91	}: ButtonProps) {
92	  return (
93	    <button
94	      // Disable when loading
95	      disabled={disabled || isLoading}
96	      // Announce loading state to screen readers
97	      aria-busy={isLoading}
98	      // Describe the button's current state
99	      aria-disabled={disabled || isLoading}
100	      className={cn(
101	        // Visible focus ring
102	        "focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-2",
103	        // Minimum touch target size (44x44px)
104	        "min-h-[44px] min-w-[44px]",
105	        variant === "primary" && "bg-primary text-primary-foreground",
106	        (disabled || isLoading) && "opacity-50 cursor-not-allowed",
107	      )}
108	      {...props}
109	    >
110	      {isLoading ? (
111	        <>
112	          <span className="sr-only">Loading</span>
113	          <Spinner aria-hidden="true" />
114	        </>
115	      ) : (
116	        children
117	      )}
118	    </button>
119	  );
120	}
121	```

123	### Pattern 2: Accessible Modal Dialog
124	
125	```tsx
126	import * as React from "react";
127	import { FocusTrap } from "@headlessui/react";
128	
129	interface DialogProps {
130	  isOpen: boolean;
131	  onClose: () => void;
132	  title: string;
133	  children: React.ReactNode;
134	}
135	
136	function AccessibleDialog({ isOpen, onClose, title, children }: DialogProps) {
137	  const titleId = React.useId();
138	  const descriptionId = React.useId();
139	
140	  // Close on Escape key
141	  React.useEffect(() => {
142	    const handleKeyDown = (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
143	      if (e.key === "Escape" && isOpen) {
144	        onClose();
145	      }
146	    };
147	    document.addEventListener("keydown", handleKeyDown);
148	    return () => document.removeEventListener("keydown", handleKeyDown);
149	  }, [isOpen, onClose]);
150	
151	  // Prevent body scroll when open
152	  React.useEffect(() => {
153	    if (isOpen) {
154	      document.body.style.overflow = "hidden";
155	    }
156	    return () => {
157	      document.body.style.overflow = "";
158	    };
159	  }, [isOpen]);
160	
161	  if (!isOpen) return null;
162	
163	  return (
164	    <div
165	      role="dialog"
166	      aria-modal="true"
167	      aria-labelledby={titleId}
168	      aria-describedby={descriptionId}
169	    >
170	      {/* Backdrop */}
171	      <div
172	        className="fixed inset-0 bg-black/50"
173	        aria-hidden="true"
174	        onClick={onClose}
175	      />
176	
177	      {/* Focus trap container */}
178	      <FocusTrap>
179	        <div className="fixed inset-0 flex items-center justify-center p-4">
180	          <div className="bg-background rounded-lg shadow-lg max-w-md w-full p-6">
181	            <h2 id={titleId} className="text-lg font-semibold">
182	              {title}
183	            </h2>
184	            <div id={descriptionId}>{children}</div>
185	            <button
186	              onClick={onClose}
187	              className="absolute top-4 right-4"
188	              aria-label="Close dialog"
189	            >
190	              <X className="h-4 w-4" />
191	            </button>
192	          </div>
193	        </div>
194	      </FocusTrap>
195	    </div>
196	  );
197	}
198	```

308	### Pattern 5: Live Region for Announcements
309	
310	```tsx
311	function useAnnounce() {
312	  const [message, setMessage] = React.useState("");
313	
314	  const announce = React.useCallback(
315	    (text: string, priority: "polite" | "assertive" = "polite") => {
316	      setMessage(""); // Clear first to ensure re-announcement
317	      setTimeout(() => setMessage(text), 100);
318	    },
319	    [],
320	  );
321	
322	  const Announcer = () => (
323	    <div
324	      role="status"
325	      aria-live="polite"
326	      aria-atomic="true"
327	      className="sr-only"
328	    >
329	      {message}
330	    </div>
331	  );
332	
333	  return { announce, Announcer };
334	}
335	
336	// Usage
337	function SearchResults({ results, isLoading }) {
338	  const { announce, Announcer } = useAnnounce();
339	
340	  React.useEffect(() => {
341	    if (!isLoading && results) {
342	      announce(`${results.length} results found`);
343	    }
344	  }, [results, isLoading, announce]);
345	
346	  return (
347	    <>
348	      <Announcer />
349	      <ul>{/* results */}</ul>
350	    </>
351	  );
352	}
353	```

358	// Contrast ratio utilities
359	function getContrastRatio(foreground: string, background: string): number {
360	  const fgLuminance = getLuminance(foreground);
361	  const bgLuminance = getLuminance(background);
362	  const lighter = Math.max(fgLuminance, bgLuminance);
363	  const darker = Math.min(fgLuminance, bgLuminance);
364	  return (lighter + 0.05) / (darker + 0.05);
365	}

367	// WCAG requirements
368	const CONTRAST_REQUIREMENTS = {

373	  },

385	
386	## Best Practices
387	
388	1. **Use Semantic HTML**: Prefer native elements over ARIA when possible
389	2. **Test with Real Users**: Include people with disabilities in user testing
390	3. **Keyboard First**: Design interactions to work without a mouse
391	4. **Don't Disable Focus Styles**: Style them, don't remove them
392	5. **Provide Text Alternatives**: All non-text content needs descriptions
393	6. **Support Zoom**: Content should work at 200% zoom
394	7. **Announce Changes**: Use live regions for dynamic content
395	8. **Respect Preferences**: Honor prefers-reduced-motion and prefers-contrast
396	
397	## Common Issues
398	
399	- **Missing alt text**: Images without descriptions
400	- **Poor color contrast**: Text hard to read against background
401	- **Keyboard traps**: Focus stuck in component
402	- **Missing labels**: Form inputs without associated labels
403	- **Auto-playing media**: Content that plays without user initiation
404	- **Inaccessible custom controls**: Recreating native functionality poorly
405	- **Missing skip links**: No way to bypass repetitive content
406	- **Focus order issues**: Tab order doesn't match visual order
407	
408	## Testing Tools
409	
410	- **Automated**: axe DevTools, WAVE, Lighthouse
411	- **Manual**: VoiceOver (macOS/iOS), NVDA/JAWS (Windows), TalkBack (Android)
412	- **Simulators**: NoCoffee (vision), Silktide (various disabilities)
413
```

1	---
2	name: better-auth-best-practices
3	description: Configure Better Auth server and client, set up database adapters, manage sessions, add plugins, and handle environment variables. Use when users mention Better Auth, betterauth, auth.ts, or need to set up TypeScript authentication with email/password, OAuth, or plugin configuration.
4	---
5	
6	# Better Auth Integration Guide
7	
8	**Always consult [better-auth.com/docs](https://better-auth.com/docs) for code examples and latest API.**
9	
10	---
11	
12	## Setup Workflow
13	
14	1. Install: `npm install better-auth`
15	2. Set env vars: `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` and `BETTER_AUTH_URL`
16	3. Create `auth.ts` with database + config
17	4. Create route handler for your framework
18	5. Run `npx @better-auth/cli@latest migrate`
19	6. Verify: call `GET /api/auth/ok` — should return `{ status: "ok" }`
20	
21	---
22	
23	## Quick Reference
24	
25	### Environment Variables
26	- `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` - Encryption secret (min 32 chars). Generate: `openssl rand -base64 32`
27	- `BETTER_AUTH_URL` - Base URL (e.g., `https://example.com`)
28	
29	Only define `baseURL`/`secret` in config if env vars are NOT set.
30	
31	### File Location
32	CLI looks for `auth.ts` in: `./`, `./lib`, `./utils`, or under `./src`. Use `--config` for custom path.
33	
34	### CLI Commands
35	- `npx @better-auth/cli@latest migrate` - Apply schema (built-in adapter)
36	- `npx @better-auth/cli@latest generate` - Generate schema for Prisma/Drizzle
37	- `npx @better-auth/cli mcp --cursor` - Add MCP to AI tools
38	
39	**Re-run after adding/changing plugins.**
40	
41	---
42	
43	## Core Config Options
44	
45	| Option | Notes |
46	|--------|-------|
47	| `appName` | Optional display name |
48	| `baseURL` | Only if `BETTER_AUTH_URL` not set |
49	| `basePath` | Default `/api/auth`. Set `/` for root. |
50	| `secret` | Only if `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` not set |
51	| `database` | Required for most features. See adapters docs. |
52	| `secondaryStorage` | Redis/KV for sessions & rate limits |
53	| `emailAndPassword` | `{ enabled: true }` to activate |
54	| `socialProviders` | `{ google: { clientId, clientSecret }, ... }` |
55	| `plugins` | Array of plugins |
56	| `trustedOrigins` | CSRF whitelist |
57	
58	---
59	
60	## Database
61	
62	**Direct connections:** Pass `pg.Pool`, `mysql2` pool, `better-sqlite3`, or `bun:sqlite` instance.
63	
64	**ORM adapters:** Import from `better-auth/adapters/drizzle`, `better-auth/adapters/prisma`, `better-auth/adapters/mongodb`.
65	
66	**Critical:** Better Auth uses adapter model names, NOT underlying table names. If Prisma model is `User` mapping to table `users`, use `modelName: "user"` (Prisma reference), not `"users"`.
67	
68	---
69	
70	## Session Management
71	
72	**Storage priority:**
73	1. If `secondaryStorage` defined → sessions go there (not DB)
74	2. Set `session.storeSessionInDatabase: true` to also persist to DB
75	3. No database + `cookieCache` → fully stateless mode
76	
77	**Cookie cache strategies:**
78	- `compact` (default) - Base64url + HMAC. Smallest.
79	- `jwt` - Standard JWT. Readable but signed.
80	- `jwe` - Encrypted. Maximum security.
81	
82	**Key options:** `session.expiresIn` (default 7 days), `session.updateAge` (refresh interval), `session.cookieCache.maxAge`, `session.cookieCache.version` (change to invalidate all sessions).
83	
84	---
85	
86	## User & Account Config
87	
88	**User:** `user.modelName`, `user.fields` (column mapping), `user.additionalFields`, `user.changeEmail.enabled` (disabled by default), `user.deleteUser.enabled` (disabled by default).
89	
90	**Account:** `account.modelName`, `account.accountLinking.enabled`, `account.storeAccountCookie` (for stateless OAuth).
91	
92	**Required for registration:** `email` and `name` fields.
93	
94	---
95	
96	## Email Flows
97	
98	- `emailVerification.sendVerificationEmail` - Must be defined for verification to work
99	- `emailVerification.sendOnSignUp` / `sendOnSignIn` - Auto-send triggers
100	- `emailAndPassword.sendResetPassword` - Password reset email handler
101	
102	---
103	
104	## Security
105	
106	**In `advanced`:**
107	- `useSecureCookies` - Force HTTPS cookies
108	- `disableCSRFCheck` - ⚠️ Security risk
109	- `disableOriginCheck` - ⚠️ Security risk  
110	- `crossSubDomainCookies.enabled` - Share cookies across subdomains
111	- `ipAddress.ipAddressHeaders` - Custom IP headers for proxies
112	- `database.generateId` - Custom ID generation or `"serial"`/`"uuid"`/`false`
113	
114	**Rate limiting:** `rateLimit.enabled`, `rateLimit.window`, `rateLimit.max`, `rateLimit.storage` ("memory" | "database" | "secondary-storage").
115	
116	---
117	
118	## Hooks
119	
120	**Endpoint hooks:** `hooks.before` / `hooks.after` - Array of `{ matcher, handler }`. Use `createAuthMiddleware`. Access `ctx.path`, `ctx.context.returned` (after), `ctx.context.session`.
121	
122	**Database hooks:** `databaseHooks.user.create.before/after`, same for `session`, `account`. Useful for adding default values or post-creation actions.
123	
124	**Hook context (`ctx.context`):** `session`, `secret`, `authCookies`, `password.hash()`/`verify()`, `adapter`, `internalAdapter`, `generateId()`, `tables`, `baseURL`.
125	
126	---
127	
128	## Plugins
129	
130	**Import from dedicated paths for tree-shaking:**
131	```
132	import { twoFactor } from "better-auth/plugins/two-factor"
133	```
134	NOT `from "better-auth/plugins"`.
135	
136	**Popular plugins:** `twoFactor`, `organization`, `passkey`, `magicLink`, `emailOtp`, `username`, `phoneNumber`, `admin`, `apiKey`, `bearer`, `jwt`, `multiSession`, `sso`, `oauthProvider`, `oidcProvider`, `openAPI`, `genericOAuth`.
137	
138	Client plugins go in `createAuthClient({ plugins: [...] })`.
139	
140	---
141	
142	## Client
143	
144	Import from: `better-auth/client` (vanilla), `better-auth/react`, `better-auth/vue`, `better-auth/svelte`, `better-auth/solid`.
145	
146	Key methods: `signUp.email()`, `signIn.email()`, `signIn.social()`, `signOut()`, `useSession()`, `getSession()`, `revokeSession()`, `revokeSessions()`.
147	
148	---
149	
150	## Type Safety
151	
152	Infer types: `typeof auth.$Infer.Session`, `typeof auth.$Infer.Session.user`.
153	
154	For separate client/server projects: `createAuthClient<typeof auth>()`.
155	
156	---
157	
158	## Common Gotchas
159	
160	1. **Model vs table name** - Config uses ORM model name, not DB table name
161	2. **Plugin schema** - Re-run CLI after adding plugins
162	3. **Secondary storage** - Sessions go there by default, not DB
163	4. **Cookie cache** - Custom session fields NOT cached, always re-fetched
164	5. **Stateless mode** - No DB = session in cookie only, logout on cache expiry
165	6. **Change email flow** - Sends to current email first, then new email
166	
167	---
168	
169	## Resources
170	
171	- [Docs](https://better-auth.com/docs)
172	- [Options Reference](https://better-auth.com/docs/reference/options)
173	- [LLMs.txt](https://better-auth.com/llms.txt)
174	- [GitHub](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth)
175	- [Init Options Source](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/blob/main/packages/core/src/types/init-options.ts)
```

15	# Drizzle ORM
16	
17	Modern TypeScript-first ORM with zero dependencies, compile-time type safety, and SQL-like syntax. Optimized for edge runtimes and serverless environments.
18	
19	## Quick Start
20	
21	### Installation
22	
23	```bash
24	# Core ORM
25	npm install drizzle-orm
26	
27	# Database driver (choose one)
28	npm install pg            # PostgreSQL
29	npm install mysql2        # MySQL
30	npm install better-sqlite3 # SQLite
31	
32	# Drizzle Kit (migrations)
33	npm install -D drizzle-kit
34	```
35	
36	### Basic Setup
37	
38	```typescript
39	// db/schema.ts
40	import { pgTable, serial, text, timestamp } from 'drizzle-orm/pg-core';
41	
42	export const users = pgTable('users', {
43	  id: serial('id').primaryKey(),
44	  email: text('email').notNull().unique(),
45	  name: text('name').notNull(),
46	  createdAt: timestamp('created_at').defaultNow(),
47	});
48	
49	// db/client.ts
50	import { drizzle } from 'drizzle-orm/node-postgres';
51	import { Pool } from 'pg';
52	import * as schema from './schema';
53	
54	const pool = new Pool({ connectionString: process.env.DATABASE_URL });
55	export const db = drizzle(pool, { schema });
56	```
57	
58	### First Query
59	
60	```typescript
61	import { db } from './db/client';
62	import { users } from './db/schema';
63	import { eq } from 'drizzle-orm';
64	
65	// Insert
66	const newUser = await db.insert(users).values({
67	  email: 'user@example.com',
68	  name: 'John Doe',
69	}).returning();
70	
71	// Select
72	const allUsers = await db.select().from(users);
73	
74	// Where
75	const user = await db.select().from(users).where(eq(users.id, 1));
76	
77	// Update
78	await db.update(users).set({ name: 'Jane Doe' }).where(eq(users.id, 1));
79	
80	// Delete
81	await db.delete(users).where(eq(users.id, 1));
82	```
83	
84	## Schema Definition
85	
86	### Column Types Reference
87	
88	| PostgreSQL | MySQL | SQLite | TypeScript |
89	|------------|-------|--------|------------|
90	| `serial()` | `serial()` | `integer()` | `number` |
91	| `text()` | `text()` | `text()` | `string` |
92	| `integer()` | `int()` | `integer()` | `number` |
93	| `boolean()` | `boolean()` | `integer()` | `boolean` |
94	| `timestamp()` | `datetime()` | `integer()` | `Date` |
95	| `json()` | `json()` | `text()` | `unknown` |
96	| `uuid()` | `varchar(36)` | `text()` | `string` |
97	
98	### Common Schema Patterns
99	
100	```typescript
101	import { pgTable, serial, text, varchar, integer, boolean, timestamp, json, unique } from 'drizzle-orm/pg-core';
102	
103	export const users = pgTable('users', {
104	  id: serial('id').primaryKey(),
105	  email: varchar('email', { length: 255 }).notNull().unique(),
106	  passwordHash: varchar('password_hash', { length: 255 }).notNull(),
107	  role: text('role', { enum: ['admin', 'user', 'guest'] }).default('user'),
108	  metadata: json('metadata').$type<{ theme: string; locale: string }>(),
109	  isActive: boolean('is_active').default(true),
110	  createdAt: timestamp('created_at').defaultNow().notNull(),
111	  updatedAt: timestamp('updated_at').defaultNow().notNull(),
112	}, (table) => ({
113	  emailIdx: unique('email_unique_idx').on(table.email),
114	}));
115	
116	// Infer TypeScript types
117	type User = typeof users.$inferSelect;
118	type NewUser = typeof users.$inferInsert;
119	```
120	
121	## Relations
122	
123	### One-to-Many
124	
125	```typescript
126	import { pgTable, serial, text, integer } from 'drizzle-orm/pg-core';
127	import { relations } from 'drizzle-orm';
128	
129	export const authors = pgTable('authors', {
130	  id: serial('id').primaryKey(),
131	  name: text('name').notNull(),
132	});
133	
134	export const posts = pgTable('posts', {
135	  id: serial('id').primaryKey(),
136	  title: text('title').notNull(),
137	  authorId: integer('author_id').notNull().references(() => authors.id),
138	});
139	
140	export const authorsRelations = relations(authors, ({ many }) => ({
141	  posts: many(posts),
142	}));
143	
144	export const postsRelations = relations(posts, ({ one }) => ({
145	  author: one(authors, {
146	    fields: [posts.authorId],
147	    references: [authors.id],
148	  }),
149	}));
150	
151	// Query with relations
152	const authorsWithPosts = await db.query.authors.findMany({
153	  with: { posts: true },
154	});
155	```
156	
157	### Many-to-Many
158	
159	```typescript
160	export const users = pgTable('users', {
161	  id: serial('id').primaryKey(),
162	  name: text('name').notNull(),
163	});
164	
165	export const groups = pgTable('groups', {
166	  id: serial('id').primaryKey(),
167	  name: text('name').notNull(),
168	});
169	
170	export const usersToGroups = pgTable('users_to_groups', {
171	  userId: integer('user_id').notNull().references(() => users.id),
172	  groupId: integer('group_id').notNull().references(() => groups.id),
173	}, (table) => ({
174	  pk: primaryKey({ columns: [table.userId, table.groupId] }),
175	}));
176	
177	export const usersRelations = relations(users, ({ many }) => ({
178	  groups: many(usersToGroups),
179	}));
180	
181	export const groupsRelations = relations(groups, ({ many }) => ({
182	  users: many(usersToGroups),
183	}));
184	
185	export const usersToGroupsRelations = relations(usersToGroups, ({ one }) => ({
186	  user: one(users, { fields: [usersToGroups.userId], references: [users.id] }),
187	  group: one(groups, { fields: [usersToGroups.groupId], references: [groups.id] }),
188	}));
189	```
190	
191	## Queries
192	
193	### Filtering
194	
195	```typescript
196	import { eq, ne, gt, gte, lt, lte, like, ilike, inArray, isNull, isNotNull, and, or, between } from 'drizzle-orm';
197	
198	// Equality
199	await db.select().from(users).where(eq(users.email, 'user@example.com'));
200	
201	// Comparison
202	await db.select().from(users).where(gt(users.id, 10));
203	
204	// Pattern matching
205	await db.select().from(users).where(like(users.name, '%John%'));
206	
207	// Multiple conditions
208	await db.select().from(users).where(
209	  and(
210	    eq(users.role, 'admin'),
211	    gt(users.createdAt, new Date('2024-01-01'))
212	  )
213	);
214	
215	// IN clause
216	await db.select().from(users).where(inArray(users.id, [1, 2, 3]));
217	
218	// NULL checks
219	await db.select().from(users).where(isNull(users.deletedAt));
220	```
221	
222	### Joins
223	
224	```typescript
225	import { eq } from 'drizzle-orm';
226	
227	// Inner join
228	const result = await db
229	  .select({
230	    user: users,
231	    post: posts,
232	  })
233	  .from(users)
234	  .innerJoin(posts, eq(users.id, posts.authorId));
235	
236	// Left join
237	const result = await db
238	  .select({
239	    user: users,
240	    post: posts,
241	  })
242	  .from(users)
243	  .leftJoin(posts, eq(users.id, posts.authorId));
244	
245	// Multiple joins with aggregation
246	import { count, sql } from 'drizzle-orm';
247	
248	const result = await db
249	  .select({
250	    authorName: authors.name,
251	    postCount: count(posts.id),
252	  })
253	  .from(authors)
254	  .leftJoin(posts, eq(authors.id, posts.authorId))
255	  .groupBy(authors.id);
256	```
257	
258	### Pagination & Sorting
259	
260	```typescript
261	import { desc, asc } from 'drizzle-orm';
262	
263	// Order by
264	await db.select().from(users).orderBy(desc(users.createdAt));
265	
266	// Limit & offset
267	await db.select().from(users).limit(10).offset(20);
268	
269	// Pagination helper
270	function paginate(page: number, pageSize: number = 10) {
271	  return db.select().from(users)
272	    .limit(pageSize)
273	    .offset(page * pageSize);
274	}
275	```
276	
277	## Transactions
278	
279	```typescript
280	// Auto-rollback on error
281	await db.transaction(async (tx) => {
282	  await tx.insert(users).values({ email: 'user@example.com', name: 'John' });
283	  await tx.insert(posts).values({ title: 'First Post', authorId: 1 });
284	  // If any query fails, entire transaction rolls back
285	});
286	
287	// Manual control
288	const tx = db.transaction(async (tx) => {
289	  const user = await tx.insert(users).values({ ... }).returning();
290	
291	  if (!user) {
292	    tx.rollback();
293	    return;
294	  }
295	
296	  await tx.insert(posts).values({ authorId: user.id });
297	});
298	```
299	
300	## Migrations
301	
302	### Drizzle Kit Configuration
303	
304	```typescript
305	// drizzle.config.ts
306	import type { Config } from 'drizzle-kit';
307	
308	export default {
309	  schema: './db/schema.ts',
310	  out: './drizzle',
311	  dialect: 'postgresql',
312	  dbCredentials: {
313	    url: process.env.DATABASE_URL!,
314	  },
315	} satisfies Config;
316	```
317	
318	### Migration Workflow
319	
320	```bash
321	# Generate migration
322	npx drizzle-kit generate
323	
324	# View SQL
325	cat drizzle/0000_migration.sql
326	
327	# Apply migration
328	npx drizzle-kit migrate
329	
330	# Introspect existing database
331	npx drizzle-kit introspect
332	
333	# Drizzle Studio (database GUI)
334	npx drizzle-kit studio
335	```
336	
337	### Example Migration
338	
339	```sql
340	-- drizzle/0000_initial.sql
341	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "users" (
342	  "id" serial PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL,
343	  "email" varchar(255) NOT NULL,
344	  "name" text NOT NULL,
345	  "created_at" timestamp DEFAULT now() NOT NULL,
346	  CONSTRAINT "users_email_unique" UNIQUE("email")
347	);
348	```
349	
350	## Navigation
351	
352	### Detailed References
353	
354	- **[🏗️ Advanced Schemas](./references/advanced-schemas.md)** - Custom types, composite keys, indexes, constraints, multi-tenant patterns. Load when designing complex database schemas.
355	
356	- **[🔍 Query Patterns](./references/query-patterns.md)** - Subqueries, CTEs, raw SQL, prepared statements, batch operations. Load when optimizing queries or handling complex filtering.
357	
358	- **[⚡ Performance](./references/performance.md)** - Connection pooling, query optimization, N+1 prevention, prepared statements, edge runtime integration. Load when scaling or optimizing database performance.
359	
360	- **[🔄 vs Prisma](./references/vs-prisma.md)** - Feature comparison, migration guide, when to choose Drizzle over Prisma. Load when evaluating ORMs or migrating from Prisma.
361	
362	## Red Flags
363	
364	**Stop and reconsider if:**
365	- Using `any` or `unknown` for JSON columns without type annotation
366	- Building raw SQL strings without using `sql` template (SQL injection risk)
367	- Not using transactions for multi-step data modifications
368	- Fetching all rows without pagination in production queries
369	- Missing indexes on foreign keys or frequently queried columns
370	- Using `select()` without specifying columns for large tables
371	
372	## Performance Benefits vs Prisma
373	
374	| Metric | Drizzle | Prisma |
375	|--------|---------|--------|
376	| **Bundle Size** | ~35KB | ~230KB |
377	| **Cold Start** | ~10ms | ~250ms |
378	| **Query Speed** | Baseline | ~2-3x slower |
379	| **Memory** | ~10MB | ~50MB |
380	| **Type Generation** | Runtime inference | Build-time generation |
381	
382	## Integration
383	
384	- **typescript-core**: Type-safe schema inference with `satisfies`
385	- **nextjs-core**: Server Actions, Route Handlers, Middleware integration
386	- **Database Migration**: Safe schema evolution patterns
387	
388	## Related Skills
389

391	- **prisma**: Alternative ORM comparison: Drizzle vs Prisma trade-offs
392	- **typescript**: Advanced TypeScript patterns for type-safe queries
393	- **nextjs**: Drizzle with Next.js Server Actions and API routes
394	- **sqlalchemy**: SQLAlchemy patterns for Python developers learning Drizzle
395	
396	[Full documentation available in these skills if deployed in your bundle]

1	---
2	name: find-skills
3	description: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.
4	---
5	
6	# Find Skills
7	
8	This skill helps you discover and install skills from the open agent skills ecosystem.
9	
10	## When to Use This Skill
11	
12	Use this skill when the user:
13	
14	- Asks "how do I do X" where X might be a common task with an existing skill
15	- Says "find a skill for X" or "is there a skill for X"
16	- Asks "can you do X" where X is a specialized capability
17	- Expresses interest in extending agent capabilities
18	- Wants to search for tools, templates, or workflows
19	- Mentions they wish they had help with a specific domain (design, testing, deployment, etc.)
20	
21	## What is the Skills CLI?
22	
23	The Skills CLI (`npx skills`) is the package manager for the open agent skills ecosystem. Skills are modular packages that extend agent capabilities with specialized knowledge, workflows, and tools.
24	
25	**Key commands:**
26	
27	- `npx skills find [query]` - Search for skills interactively or by keyword
28	- `npx skills add <package>` - Install a skill from GitHub or other sources
29	- `npx skills check` - Check for skill updates
30	- `npx skills update` - Update all installed skills
31	
32	**Browse skills at:** https://skills.sh/
33	
34	## How to Help Users Find Skills
35	
36	### Step 1: Understand What They Need
37	
38	When a user asks for help with something, identify:
39	
40	1. The domain (e.g., React, testing, design, deployment)
41	2. The specific task (e.g., writing tests, creating animations, reviewing PRs)
42	3. Whether this is a common enough task that a skill likely exists
43	
44	### Step 2: Check the Leaderboard First
45	
46	Before running a CLI search, check the [skills.sh leaderboard](https://skills.sh/) to see if a well-known skill already exists for the domain. The leaderboard ranks skills by total installs, surfacing the most popular and battle-tested options.
47	
48	For example, top skills for web development include:
49	- `vercel-labs/agent-skills` — React, Next.js, web design (100K+ installs each)
50	- `anthropics/skills` — Frontend design, document processing (100K+ installs)
51	
52	### Step 3: Search for Skills
53	
54	If the leaderboard doesn't cover the user's need, run the find command:
55	
56	```bash
57	npx skills find [query]
58	```
59	
60	For example:
61	
62	- User asks "how do I make my React app faster?" → `npx skills find react performance`
63	- User asks "can you help me with PR reviews?" → `npx skills find pr review`
64	- User asks "I need to create a changelog" → `npx skills find changelog`
65	
66	### Step 4: Verify Quality Before Recommending
67	
68	**Do not recommend a skill based solely on search results.** Always verify:
69	
70	1. **Install count** — Prefer skills with 1K+ installs. Be cautious with anything under 100.
71	2. **Source reputation** — Official sources (`vercel-labs`, `anthropics`, `microsoft`) are more trustworthy than unknown authors.
72	3. **GitHub stars** — Check the source repository. A skill from a repo with <100 stars should be treated with skepticism.
73	
74	### Step 5: Present Options to the User
75	
76	When you find relevant skills, present them to the user with:
77	
78	1. The skill name and what it does
79	2. The install count and source
80	3. The install command they can run
81	4. A link to learn more at skills.sh
82	
83	Example response:
84	
85	```
86	I found a skill that might help! The "react-best-practices" skill provides
87	React and Next.js performance optimization guidelines from Vercel Engineering.
88	(185K installs)
89	
90	To install it:
91	npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-skills@react-best-practices
92	
93	Learn more: https://skills.sh/vercel-labs/agent-skills/react-best-practices
94	```
95	
96	### Step 6: Offer to Install
97	
98	If the user wants to proceed, you can install the skill for them:
99	
100	```bash
101	npx skills add <owner/repo@skill> -g -y
102	```
103	
104	The `-g` flag installs globally (user-level) and `-y` skips confirmation prompts.
105	
106	## Common Skill Categories
107	
108	When searching, consider these common categories:
109	
110	| Category        | Example Queries                          |
111	| --------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
112	| Web Development | react, nextjs, typescript, css, tailwind |
113	| Testing         | testing, jest, playwright, e2e           |
114	| DevOps          | deploy, docker, kubernetes, ci-cd        |
115	| Documentation   | docs, readme, changelog, api-docs        |
116	| Code Quality    | review, lint, refactor, best-practices   |
117	| Design          | ui, ux, design-system, accessibility     |
118	| Productivity    | workflow, automation, git                |
119	
120	## Tips for Effective Searches
121	
122	1. **Use specific keywords**: "react testing" is better than just "testing"
123	2. **Try alternative terms**: If "deploy" doesn't work, try "deployment" or "ci-cd"
124	3. **Check popular sources**: Many skills come from `vercel-labs/agent-skills` or `ComposioHQ/awesome-claude-skills`
125	
126	## When No Skills Are Found
127	
128	If no relevant skills exist:
129	
130	1. Acknowledge that no existing skill was found
131	2. Offer to help with the task directly using your general capabilities
132	3. Suggest the user could create their own skill with `npx skills init`
133	
134	Example:
135	
136	```
137	I searched for skills related to "xyz" but didn't find any matches.
138	I can still help you with this task directly! Would you like me to proceed?
139	
140	If this is something you do often, you could create your own skill:
141	npx skills init my-xyz-skill
142	```
143
```
</details></tool-use>
