1	# AGENTS-CONVENTIONS.md
2	
3	Code conventions for the portfolio project — JSDoc guidelines that go beyond what the linter and TypeScript enforce.
4	
5	> **Before implementing complex type logic, generics, or utility types, execute the following skill** — read the SKILL.md and follow its instructions:
6	>
7	> 1. `.cursor/skills/typescript-advanced-types/SKILL.md`
8	
9	---
10	
11	## JSDoc
12	
13	Since TypeScript already provides type safety, use JSDoc to add **semantic context** — the "why", not the "what". Do not restate information that types already express.
14	
15	### When to Document
16	
17	Document when there is:
18	
19	- Non-obvious logic or business rules
20	- Side effects (revalidation, redirects, external calls)
21	- Security assumptions or constraints
22	- Possible errors or edge cases
23	- Deprecations or temporary workarounds
24	
25	Skip JSDoc for:
26	
27	- Self-explanatory functions where the name + types say it all
28	- Simple component props already typed with an interface
29	- One-liner utilities with clear names (e.g., `formatDate`)
30	
31	### Approved Tags
32	
33	| Tag           | Use for                                                                   | Example context                                      |
34	| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
35	| `@param`      | Only when the name/type isn't self-explanatory, or to clarify constraints | `@param id - Must be > 0, validated upstream by Zod` |
36	| `@returns`    | Only when the return value has non-obvious meaning                        | `@returns null when the user has no active session`  |
37	| `@throws`     | Server actions / functions that throw or redirect                         | `@throws Redirects to /login if unauthenticated`     |
38	| `@example`    | Complex utilities where usage isn't obvious                               | `@example cn("base", condition && "extra")`          |
39	| `@deprecated` | Superseded code that still exists                                         | `@deprecated Use getServerSession() instead`         |
40	| `@see`        | Link to related code, docs, or decisions                                  | `@see AGENTS-SECURITY.md for auth pattern`           |
41	| `@todo`       | Known improvements pending                                                | `@todo Add Zod validation (issue #42)`               |
42	
43	Avoid `@type`, `@typedef`, `@callback` — TypeScript handles these.
44	
45	### Where to Prioritize
46	
47	| Location                               | Priority   | Reason                                             |
48	| -------------------------------------- | ---------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
49	| `lib/actions/*` (Server Actions)       | **High**   | Side effects, auth checks, revalidation, redirects |
50	| `lib/auth.ts`, `lib/server-session.ts` | **High**   | Security assumptions, session flow                 |
51	| `db/schema/*`                          | **Medium** | Relationships, constraints, enum meanings          |
52	| `components/ui/*` (reusable)           | **Medium** | Prop behavior, variants, accessibility notes       |
53	| `lib/utils.ts`                         | **Low**    | Only if logic is non-trivial                       |
54	| Page/layout components                 | **Low**    | Only for unusual data fetching or auth patterns    |
55	
56	### Examples
57

59

61	/**
62	 * Updates a project and its associated skills.
63	 * Revalidates both the dashboard and public page caches.
64	 *
65	 * @throws Redirects to /login if the session is invalid.
66	 * @throws Error if the project ID does not exist.
67	 */
68	export async function updateProject(formData: FormData) {
69		// ...
70	}
71	```
72	
73	**Schema** (`db/schema/`):
74

76	/**
77	 * Tracks employment status changes over time.
78	 * Each row is an immutable snapshot — never update, only insert.
79	 */
80	export const employmentHistory = sqliteTable('employment_history', {
81		// ...
82	});
83	```
84	
85	**Auth helper** (`lib/`):
86	
87	```typescript
88	/**
89	 * Retrieves the current admin session from cookies.

2	
3	Design patterns and architecture guidelines for the portfolio project.

5	> **Before refactoring component architecture or splitting components, execute the following skill** — read the SKILL.md and follow its instructions:
6	>

9	> **Before implementing Next.js file-system conventions or App Router patterns, execute the following skills** — read each SKILL.md and follow its instructions:
10	>
11	> 1. `.cursor/skills/next-best-practices/SKILL.md`
12	> 2. `.cursor/skills/nextjs-app-router-patterns/SKILL.md`
13	
14	> **Before optimizing Server Actions or React performance, execute the following skill** — read the SKILL.md and follow its instructions:
15	>
16	> 1. `.cursor/skills/vercel-react-best-practices/SKILL.md`
17	
18	**Related coverage in other AGENTS files (do not duplicate):**
19	
20	- `AGENTS-SECURITY.md` — Server Action auth/validation rules, CSP nonce in `proxy.ts`
21	- `AGENTS-TESTING.md` — TDD for Zod schemas, Server Action test patterns
22	- `AGENTS-PERFORMANCE.md` — Server vs Client decision tree, loading/streaming
23	- `AGENTS-ACCESSIBILITY.md` — Semantic layout landmarks, heading hierarchy
24	- [AGENTS-SEO.md](./AGENTS-SEO.md) — Metadata templates, OG images, sitemap, robots
25	
26	---
27	
28	## Overview
29	
30	| Pattern                  | What It Solves                                            | Where It Applies                   |
31	| ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
32	| Container-Presentational | Page files mix data fetching with 200+ lines of UI        | Admin dashboard pages, public page |
33	| Server Action Hardening  | Actions have no auth, no validation, no error handling    | All `lib/actions/` files           |
34	| Data Access Facade       | DB queries duplicated inline across page files            | All pages that query the database  |
35	| Error Boundaries         | Zero error recovery — failed DB query crashes entire page | All route segments                 |
36	
37	---
38	
39	## 1. Container-Presentational Pattern
40	
41	Split each page into a **Container** (the `page.tsx` — fetches data, checks auth, passes props) and a **Presentational** component (receives data via props, renders UI).
42	
43	```
44	app/(admin)/dashboard/projects/
45	├── page.tsx                    # Container — ~50 lines max
46	components/admin/
47	├── projects-table.tsx          # Presentational — table UI
48	├── entity-empty-state.tsx      # Shared reusable empty state
49	```
50	
51	### Template
52	
53	```typescript
54	// app/(admin)/dashboard/projects/page.tsx
55	import { getProjectsWithSkills } from "@/lib/queries/projects";
56	import { ProjectsTable } from "@/components/admin/projects-table";
57	import { getServerSession } from "@/lib/server-session";
58	import { redirect } from "next/navigation";
59	
60	export default async function ProjectsPage() {
61	  const session = await getServerSession();
62	  if (!session) redirect("/login");
63	
64	  const projects = await getProjectsWithSkills();
65	  return <ProjectsTable projects={projects} />;
66	}
67	```
68	
69	### Rules
70	
71	- **Page files (`page.tsx`) must not exceed ~50 lines** — if they do, UI is leaking into the container
72	- **Presentational components receive all data via props** — never call `db` directly
73	- **Shared formatting utilities go in `lib/utils.ts`** — not redefined per page (`formatDate`, `getStatusVariant`)
74	- **Presentational components are `"use client"` only when they need interactivity** (delete buttons, sort toggles) — keep as Server Components when purely displaying data
75	- **Empty states use a shared `EntityEmptyState` component** — same pattern across all entities
76	
77	---
78	
79	## 2. Server Action Hardening (Strategy-like)
80	
81	Every Server Action follows a **4-step strategy**: authenticate → validate → execute → revalidate. Each entity defines its own Zod schema in `lib/schemas/`, but the structure is identical.
82	
83	### 4-Step Template
84	
85	```typescript
86	'use server';
87	
88	import { getServerSession } from '@/lib/server-session';
89	import { redirect } from 'next/navigation';
90	import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache';
91	import { db } from '@/db';
92	import { entitySchema } from '@/lib/schemas/entity';
93	
94	export async function createEntity(formData: FormData) {
95		// 1. AUTHENTICATE
96		const session = await getServerSession();
97		if (!session) redirect('/login');
98	
99		// 2. VALIDATE
100		const parsed = entitySchema.safeParse({
101			name: formData.get('name'),
102		});
103		if (!parsed.success) return { error: parsed.error.flatten().fieldErrors };
104	
105		// 3. EXECUTE
106		try {
107			await db.insert(table).values(parsed.data);
108		} catch {
109			return { error: 'Failed to create entity.' };
110		}
111	
112		// 4. REVALIDATE / REDIRECT
113		redirect('/dashboard/entities');
114	}
115	```
116	
117	### Action Return Type
118	
119	```typescript
120	type ActionResult = { error: string } | { error: Record<string, string[]> } | void; // success — redirect happens
121	```
122	
123	### Rules
124	
125	- **Every action starts with `getServerSession()`** — no exceptions; redirect to `/login` if `null`
126	- **Every action validates with Zod `.safeParse()`** — never trust `formData.get()` directly
127	- **Wrap DB operations in try-catch** — return user-friendly messages, never expose raw errors
128	- **Remove all `console.log` statements** from actions
129	- **Transform empty strings to `undefined`** — forms submit `""` for empty optional fields; use `.or(z.literal(""))` or `.transform()`
130	- **Zod schemas live in `lib/schemas/`** — one file per entity (projects.ts, experiences.ts, skills.ts, social-links.ts, settings.ts)
131	
132	### Migration Order (per entity)
133	
134	1. Create Zod schema in `lib/schemas/`
135	2. Write Vitest tests for the schema (TDD — see `AGENTS-TESTING.md`)
136	3. Add auth + validation + try-catch to each action
137	4. Remove `console.log` statements
138	5. Test the full flow in the browser
139	
140	---
141	
142	## 3. Data Access Facade
143	
144	Encapsulate all Drizzle read queries in `lib/queries/` — one file per entity. Pages import these functions instead of using `db` directly.
145	
146	```
147	lib/queries/
148	├── projects.ts        # getProjectsWithSkills, getProjectById
149	├── experiences.ts     # getExperiencesWithSkills, getExperienceById
150	├── skills.ts          # getAllSkills
151	├── social-links.ts    # getAllSocialLinks
152	├── settings.ts        # getSiteSettings
153	```
154	
155	### Template
156	
157	```typescript
158	// lib/queries/projects.ts
159	import 'server-only';
160	import { db } from '@/db';
161	import { projects } from '@/db/schema/portfolio';
162	import { asc, eq } from 'drizzle-orm';
163	
164	export async function getProjectsWithSkills() {
165		return db.query.projects.findMany({
166			with: {
167				projectSkills: { columns: {}, with: { skill: { columns: { id: true, name: true } } } },
168			},
169			orderBy: [asc(projects.order)],
170		});
171	}
172	```
173	
174	### Rules
175	
176	- **Pages never import `db` directly** — always go through `lib/queries/`
177	- **Server Actions still use `db` directly** — writes don't benefit from a read-only facade
178	- **One file per entity** — mirrors `lib/actions/` structure
179	- **Add `"server-only"` import** — prevents accidental client-side import
180	- **Keep functions simple** — one Drizzle query per function, no business logic
181	- **Caching goes here** — add `"use cache"` + `cacheLife()` inside facade functions; all callers benefit automatically
182	
183	---
184	
185	## 4. Error Boundaries
186	
187	Add `error.tsx` and `loading.tsx` files to route segments for error recovery and loading states.
188	
189	### Minimum Required Files
190	
191	| File                                | Catches                                     |
192	| ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
193	| `app/error.tsx`                     | Root-level fallback for any unhandled error |
194	| `app/(admin)/dashboard/error.tsx`   | Database failures, auth errors in dashboard |
195	| `app/(public)/error.tsx`            | Database failures on public portfolio page  |
196	| `app/(admin)/dashboard/loading.tsx` | Skeleton while dashboard data loads         |
197	| `app/(public)/loading.tsx`          | Skeleton while public page data loads       |
198	| `app/not-found.tsx`                 | Custom 404 page                             |
199	
200	### Template
201	
202	```typescript
203	// app/(admin)/dashboard/error.tsx
204	"use client";
205	
206	export default function DashboardError({
207	  error,
208	  reset,
209	}: {
210	  error: Error & { digest?: string };
211	  reset: () => void;
212	}) {
213	  // Log error, show generic message, provide reset button + "go back" link
214	  return (/* Card with error icon, message, reset button, home link */);
215	}
216	```
217	
218	### Rules
219	
220	- **`error.tsx` must have `"use client"`** — required by Next.js
221	- **Never display `error.message` to users** — may contain SQL errors or stack traces; show generic message
222	- **Always provide a `reset` button** and a "go back" escape hatch
223	- **Use `error.digest` for server-side error correlation** — matches server logs
224	- **Root `error.tsx` does NOT catch root layout errors** — use `global-error.tsx` only if root layout can fail (unlikely in this project)
225	- **Pair `error.tsx` with `loading.tsx`** — error boundaries handle failures; loading files handle the pending state
226	- **Skeleton UIs must match the shape of actual content** — minimizes layout shift during streaming
227	
228	---
229	
230	## 5. Next.js File-System Conventions (Summary)
231	
232	> Full convention reference with detailed explanations and code: [AGENTS-PATTERNS-REFERENCE.md](./AGENTS-PATTERNS-REFERENCE.md)
233	
234	### Quick Reference
235	
236	| Convention           | File                    | Used in Project                                | Status                       |
237	| -------------------- | ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
238	| Page                 | `page.tsx`              | Yes — 9 pages                                  | Active                       |
239	| Layout               | `layout.tsx`            | Yes — root, admin, public                      | Active                       |
240	| Loading              | `loading.tsx`           | No                                             | **Needed**                   |
241	| Error                | `error.tsx`             | No                                             | **Needed**                   |
242	| Global Error         | `global-error.tsx`      | No                                             | Optional                     |
243	| Not Found            | `not-found.tsx`         | No                                             | **Needed**                   |
244	| Forbidden            | `forbidden.tsx`         | No                                             | Experimental — not yet       |
245	| Unauthorized         | `unauthorized.tsx`      | No                                             | Experimental — not yet       |
246	| Route Handler        | `route.ts`              | Yes — auth routes                              | Active                       |
247	| Proxy                | `proxy.ts`              | Yes — auth + CSP                               | Active                       |
248	| Template             | `template.tsx`          | No                                             | Not needed                   |
249	| Default              | `default.tsx`           | No                                             | Not needed                   |
250	| Route Groups         | `(folder)`              | Yes — `(admin)`, `(public)`                    | Active                       |
251	| Dynamic Segments     | `[param]`, `[...param]` | Yes — `[id]`, `[...all]`                       | Active                       |
252	| Parallel Routes      | `@folder`               | No                                             | Not needed                   |
253	| Intercepting Routes  | `(.)folder`             | No                                             | Not needed                   |
254	| Route Segment Config | `export const dynamic`  | No                                             | Prefer `"use cache"` instead |
255	| Metadata Files       | Various                 | Partial — see [AGENTS-SEO.md](./AGENTS-SEO.md) | **Needed**                   |
256	
257	### Files to Create Before Production
258	
259	| Priority   | File                                                                         | Why                                        |
260	| ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
261	| **High**   | `app/error.tsx`, `app/(admin)/dashboard/error.tsx`, `app/(public)/error.tsx` | Error recovery                             |
262	| **High**   | `app/(admin)/dashboard/loading.tsx`, `app/(public)/loading.tsx`              | Loading skeletons                          |
263	| **High**   | `app/not-found.tsx`                                                          | Custom 404                                 |
264	| **Medium** | `app/sitemap.ts`, `app/robots.ts`, OG image, favicons                        | SEO (see [AGENTS-SEO.md](./AGENTS-SEO.md)) |
265	| **Low**    | `app/(admin)/dashboard/not-found.tsx`                                        | Admin 404 for missing entities             |
266	| **Low**    | `instrumentation.ts`                                                         | Production error tracking                  |
267	
268	### Key Convention Rules
269	
270	- `params` and `searchParams` are **promises** in Next.js 16 — always `await` before accessing
271	- Pages are async Server Components — keep them as thin containers after applying pattern 1
272	- Every admin page must call `getServerSession()` at the top
273	- Layouts **cannot** access `searchParams` — only `params` and `children`
274	- A `route.ts` in the same segment as `page.tsx` will conflict — they can't coexist
275	- Route Segment Config (`export const dynamic`, etc.) is disabled when `cacheComponents: true` — prefer `"use cache"` directive
276	
277	---
278	
279	## Pattern Interaction
280	
281	The four patterns work together in a typical admin page:
282	
283	```
284	Request → page.tsx (Container)
285	            ├── getServerSession()            ← Error Boundary catches auth failures
286	            ├── getProjectsWithSkills()       ← Data Access Facade (lib/queries/)
287	            │                                    └── Error Boundary catches DB failures
288	            └── <ProjectsTable />             ← Presentational Component
289	                    └── deleteProject()        ← Hardened Server Action
290	                          ├── getServerSession()
291	                          ├── Zod safeParse
292	                          ├── try-catch DB operation
293	                          └── revalidatePath
294	```
295	
296	### Migration Flow
297	
298	When refactoring existing pages, follow this order:
299	
300	1. Create Zod schemas (`lib/schemas/`)
301	2. Harden server actions (auth + validation + try-catch)
302	3. Create data access facades (`lib/queries/`)
303	4. Extract presentational components (`components/admin/`)
304	5. Simplify page files to containers
305	6. Add `error.tsx` and `loading.tsx` files
306	
307	---
308	
309	## Implementation Checklist
310

312	
313	- [ ] Zod schema in `lib/schemas/` + Vitest tests

324	- [ ] Shared `EntityEmptyState` component

```text
1	# AGENTS-SECURITY.md
2	
3	Security guidelines for the portfolio project — all security layers for a Next.js 16 app deployed on Vercel with better-auth, Drizzle ORM, and Turso.
4	
5	> Full implementation code (proxy.ts, next.config.ts headers, SDK examples, audit commands): [AGENTS-SECURITY-REFERENCE.md](./AGENTS-SECURITY-REFERENCE.md)
6	
7	> **Before implementing or modifying authentication, execute the following skill** — read the SKILL.md and follow its instructions:
8	>
9	> 1. `.cursor/skills/better-auth-best-practices/SKILL.md`
10	
11	> **Before writing or reviewing database queries, execute the following skill** — read the SKILL.md and follow its instructions:
12	>
13	> 1. `.cursor/skills/drizzle-orm/SKILL.md`
14	
15	> **Before hardening Server Actions, execute the following skills** — read each SKILL.md and follow its instructions:
16	>
17	> 1. `.cursor/skills/vercel-react-best-practices/SKILL.md`
18	> 2. `.cursor/skills/next-best-practices/SKILL.md`
19	
20	---
21	
22	## Content Security Policy (CSP)
23	
24	CSP protects against XSS, clickjacking, and code injection by declaring trusted content sources. Implemented via nonces in `proxy.ts`.
25	
26	**How it works**: `proxy.ts` generates a unique nonce per request → adds it to the `Content-Security-Policy` header → Next.js applies the nonce to scripts/styles → only matching scripts execute.
27	
28	### CSP Skeleton (in proxy.ts)
29	
30	```typescript
31	const nonce = Buffer.from(crypto.randomUUID()).toString('base64');
32	const isDev = process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development';
33	
34	const cspHeader = `
35	  default-src 'self';
36	  script-src 'self' 'nonce-${nonce}' 'strict-dynamic'${isDev ? " 'unsafe-eval'" : ''};
37	  style-src 'self'${isDev ? " 'unsafe-inline'" : ` 'nonce-${nonce}'`};
38	  img-src 'self' blob: data: https:;
39	  font-src 'self';
40	  object-src 'none';
41	  base-uri 'self';
42	  form-action 'self';
43	  frame-ancestors 'none';
44	  upgrade-insecure-requests;
45	`;
46	// Set on both request and response headers. Full implementation in reference file.
47	```
48	
49	### Rules
50	
51	- **Dev mode requires `'unsafe-eval'`** for React error stack traces and `'unsafe-inline'` for Tailwind HMR — NOT in production
52	- **CSP makes pages dynamically rendered** — nonces change per request, so CSP pages cannot be statically generated
53	- **If adding third-party scripts**, add their domains to `script-src` and `connect-src`
54	- **Read the nonce** in Server Components via `(await headers()).get("x-nonce")` for `<Script>` tags
55	
56	> Full `proxy.ts` CSP implementation and CSP directives reference: [AGENTS-SECURITY-REFERENCE.md](./AGENTS-SECURITY-REFERENCE.md#csp-full-implementation)
57	
58	---
59	
60	## Security Headers
61	
62	Six headers configured in `next.config.ts` via the `headers()` function:
63	
64	| Header                                             | Purpose                                                    |
65	| -------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
66	| `X-DNS-Prefetch-Control: on`                       | DNS prefetching for external links                         |
67	| `Strict-Transport-Security`                        | Forces HTTPS for 2 years, all subdomains, preload-eligible |
68	| `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN`                      | Prevents iframe embedding (clickjacking)                   |
69	| `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`                  | Prevents MIME-type sniffing                                |
70	| `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin` | Limits referrer info on cross-origin                       |
71	| `Permissions-Policy`                               | Disables camera, microphone, geolocation, browsing-topics  |
72	
73	### Rules
74	
75	- **Do NOT add `X-XSS-Protection`** — deprecated, can introduce vulnerabilities. CSP replaces it
76	- **Do NOT set `Cache-Control` for `_next/static`** — Next.js handles immutable caching automatically
77	- **HSTS preload** — only submit to preload list after confirming HTTPS on all subdomains (irreversible)
78	
79	> Full `next.config.ts` headers implementation: [AGENTS-SECURITY-REFERENCE.md](./AGENTS-SECURITY-REFERENCE.md#security-headers-implementation)
80	
81	---
82	
83	## Auth Protection Pattern
84	
85	Two-layer approach as recommended by [better-auth Next.js docs](https://www.better-auth.com/docs/integrations/next#auth-protection):
86	
87	**Layer 1 — Optimistic redirects via `proxy.ts`** (UX only, NOT secure):
88	
89	- Checks cookie existence only — no DB call, no session validation
90	- Logged-in users on `/login` → redirect to `/dashboard`
91	- Logged-out users on `/dashboard` → redirect to `/login`
92	- Anyone can forge a cookie — this layer is purely for avoiding page flash
93	
94	**Layer 2 — Real auth in every page/action** (the actual security):
95	
96	```typescript
97	// Every protected page and Server Action must do this:
98	const session = await getServerSession();
99	if (!session) redirect('/login');
100	```
101	
102	`getServerSession()` in `lib/server-session.ts` validates the session against the database, wrapped in `cache()` to deduplicate within a request.
103	
104	### Rules
105	
106	- **NEVER rely on `proxy.ts` for security** — it only checks cookie existence
107	- **ALWAYS call `getServerSession()` in every protected page and every Server Action**
108	- **`cache()` wrapping** ensures multiple calls in the same request only hit the DB once
109	- **Session cookie cache (5 min)** in `lib/auth.ts` reduces DB load — tradeoff: revoked session valid up to 5 min
110	- **Add `"server-only"` import** to `server-session.ts`
111	
112	---
113	
114	## Server Actions Security
115	
116	Every action follows the **4-step pattern**: authenticate → validate → execute → revalidate. See [AGENTS-PATTERNS.md § Server Action Hardening](./AGENTS-PATTERNS.md#2-server-action-hardening-strategy-like) for the template.
117	
118	### Rules
119	
120	- **Step 1 (Auth) is mandatory** — `getServerSession()` first, redirect if `null`
121	- **Step 2 uses Zod `.safeParse()`** — never trust `formData.get()` directly
122	- **Step 3 uses Drizzle ORM** — never concatenate strings into SQL
123	- **Never expose internal errors** — return user-friendly messages, log internals server-side
124	- **`formData.get()` returns `FormDataEntryValue | null`** — handle `null` before Zod
125	- **Remove all `console.log` statements** from production code
126	
127	### Revalidate vs Redirect (Step 4)
128	
129	| Scenario                              | Use                                     | Why                   |
130	| ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
131	| **Create** (user on `/new` or dialog) | `redirect("/dashboard/entities")`       | Navigate back to list |
132	| **Update** (user stays on same page)  | `revalidatePath("/dashboard/entities")` | Refresh in-place      |
133	| **Delete** (user stays on same page)  | `revalidatePath("/dashboard/entities")` | Seamless UI refresh   |
134	
135	`redirect()` already triggers a fresh render — a preceding `revalidatePath()` to the same path is redundant.
136	
137	---
138	
139	## Input Validation with Zod
140	
141	Schemas in `lib/schemas/` — see [AGENTS-PATTERNS.md § Zod Schemas](./AGENTS-PATTERNS.md#2-server-action-hardening-strategy-like).
142	
143	- **Validate on the server** — client-side validation is UX only; the Server Action is the security boundary
144	- **Use `.safeParse()`** — graceful error handling without try-catch
145	- **Set max lengths** — prevent DoS via long inputs; match DB column constraints
146	- **Use `.or(z.literal(""))` for optional URL fields** — empty form strings aren't valid URLs
147	- **Transform empty strings to `undefined`** via `.transform()`
148	
149	---
150	
151	## SQL Injection Prevention
152	
153	Drizzle ORM produces parameterized queries by default. Safe patterns:
154	
155	```typescript
156	db.select().from(projects).where(eq(projects.id, id)); // Query builder — safe
157	db.insert(projects).values({ title, description }); // Insert — safe
158	sql<number>`COALESCE(MAX(${projects.order}), 0)`; // sql template — safe (parameterized)
159	```
160	
161	**Never do**:
162	
163	- `db.execute(\`SELECT \* FROM projects WHERE id = ${id}\`)` — SQL injection
164	- `sql.raw(\`... WHERE title = '${title}'\`)` — SQL injection
165	- Dynamic table/column names from user input
166	
167	### Rules
168	
169	- **Always use the Drizzle query builder** or `sql` template literal
170	- **Never use `sql.raw()` with user input**
171	- **Validate IDs as numbers before queries** — even though Drizzle parameterizes
172	
173	---
174	
175	## Secure Environment Variables
176	
177	| Pattern         | Exposure                                   | Examples                                                       |
178	| --------------- | ------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
179	| `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` | Bundled in client JS (visible to everyone) | `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL`                                          |
180	| No prefix       | Server-only (never sent to browser)        | `TURSO_DATABASE_URL`, `TURSO_AUTH_TOKEN`, `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` |
181	
182	### Rules
183	
184	- **NEVER prefix secrets with `NEXT_PUBLIC_`**
185	- **NEVER commit `.env.local` to git** — verify `.gitignore` includes it
186	- **Generate `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`** with `openssl rand -base64 32` (at least 32 chars)
187	- **On Vercel, use Sensitive Environment Variables** — encrypted, non-readable after creation
188	- **Use different values per environment** (Production, Preview, Development)
189	
190	---
191	
192	## CSRF Protection
193	
194	- **better-auth verifies `Origin` header** on all mutation requests — rejects if origin doesn't match `trustedOrigins`
195	- **Next.js Server Actions are protected by default** — framework validates `Origin` header; no additional CSRF tokens needed
196	- **Do NOT set `disableCSRFCheck: true`** or `disableOriginCheck: true` in better-auth
197	- **Session cookies use `SameSite: 'lax'`** by default — allows top-level navigations, blocks cross-site form submissions
198	- **Custom API routes** (beyond `/api/auth/*`) need manual CSRF token verification
199	
200	---
201	
202	## Secure Cookies & Sessions
203	
204	better-auth manages session cookies with flags: `httpOnly: true`, `secure: true` (production), `sameSite: 'lax'`, `path: '/'`.
205	
206	- **Never access session cookies in client JavaScript** — `httpOnly` by design
207	- **Cookie cache (5 min)** — revoked session valid up to 5 minutes; acceptable for single-admin dashboard
208	- **Don't implement custom session timeout** — better-auth handles expiration/renewal
209	- **Custom cookies** must always set: `httpOnly`, `secure`, `sameSite`, reasonable `maxAge`
210	
211	---
212	
213	## Rate Limiting
214	
215	**Use Vercel WAF as the primary rate limiting layer** — operates at the edge with global state, before your code runs. In-memory counters (LRU, Map, better-auth `"memory"` storage) are unreliable on serverless — instances don't share memory, cold starts reset counters.
216	
217	### Recommended WAF Rules
218	
219	| Rule            | Path          | Limit   | Window | Action     |
220	| --------------- | ------------- | ------- | ------ | ---------- |
221	| Auth protection | `/api/auth/*` | 20 req  | 60s    | Deny (429) |
222	| General API     | `/api/*`      | 100 req | 60s    | Deny (429) |
223	
224	### Rules
225	
226	- **Enable better-auth rate limiting** as defense in depth — use `"database"` storage for production, `"memory"` acceptable as basic deterrent for low-traffic single-admin
227	- **Stricter limits on auth endpoints** (10-20 req/min) — most targeted
228	- **Return `429 Too Many Requests`** with `Retry-After` header when possible
229	- **Use `@vercel/firewall` SDK** for application-level context (user ID, etc.) — requires matching dashboard rule
230	
231	> Full `@vercel/firewall` SDK examples and WAF plan limits: [AGENTS-SECURITY-REFERENCE.md](./AGENTS-SECURITY-REFERENCE.md#rate-limiting-details)
232	
233	---
234	
235	## Source Maps & Production Hardening
236	
237	- **Never enable `productionBrowserSourceMaps: true`** — exposes source code
238	- **Add `removeConsole` to `next.config.ts`** — strips `console.log`/`debug`/`info`/`trace`, keeps `error`/`warn`
239	- **Never log sensitive data** — tokens, passwords, DB URLs must never appear in logs
240	
241	---
242	
243	## Dependency Security
244	
245	- **Run `pnpm audit` before every deployment** — no high/critical vulnerabilities
246	- **`pnpm up` weekly** (within semver ranges), `pnpm dlx npm-check-updates` monthly (check majors)
247	- **Lock file is your friend** — always commit `pnpm-lock.yaml`
248	- **Ignore unfixable CVEs explicitly** in `auditConfig.ignoreCves` rather than ignoring the entire audit
249	
250	> Full audit commands and workflow: [AGENTS-SECURITY-REFERENCE.md](./AGENTS-SECURITY-REFERENCE.md#dependency-audit-commands)
251	
252	---
253	
254	## Vercel Security Features
255	
256	| Automatic (no config)        | Needs Configuration                       |
257	| ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
258	| HTTPS + SSL/TLS certificates | Mark secrets as Sensitive in dashboard    |
259	| DDoS mitigation              | Attack Challenge Mode (CAPTCHA for bots)  |
260	| Edge network / global CDN    | Deployment Protection (restrict previews) |
261	| Encrypted env vars at rest   | WAF rate limit rules                      |
262	
263	### Rules
264	
265	- **Always mark secrets as Sensitive** — `TURSO_AUTH_TOKEN`, `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, `TURSO_DATABASE_URL`
266	- **Do not expose admin routes in preview deployments**
267	
268	---
269	
270	## Defense in Depth Summary
271	
272	| Layer          | Protection            | This Project                         |
273	| -------------- | --------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
274	| Network        | DDoS, HTTPS           | Vercel (automatic)                   |
275	| Edge           | Rate limiting         | Vercel WAF rules                     |
276	| Transport      | HSTS, TLS             | Security headers in `next.config.ts` |
277	| Application    | CSP, headers          | `proxy.ts` + `next.config.ts`        |
278	| Authentication | Session validation    | better-auth + `getServerSession()`   |
279	| Input          | Validation            | Zod schemas + Drizzle ORM            |
280	| Data           | Parameterized queries | Drizzle ORM (automatic)              |
281	| Dependencies   | Vulnerability audit   | `pnpm audit`                         |
282	
283	---
284

288	- [ ] Add security headers to `next.config.ts`
289	- [ ] Add `removeConsole` compiler option to `next.config.ts`

293	- [ ] Add WAF rate limit rules (`/api/auth/*` 20 req/min, `/api/*` 100 req/min)
294	- [ ] Enable `rateLimit` in `lib/auth.ts`
295	- [ ] Add audit scripts to `package.json`
296
```

```text
1	# AGENTS-TESTING.md
2	
3	Testing strategy, conventions, and project-specific patterns for a Next.js 16 application tested with Vitest (unit) and Playwright (E2E).
4	
5	> Full mock code blocks, CI workflow YAML, and auth setup: [AGENTS-TESTING-REFERENCE.md](./AGENTS-TESTING-REFERENCE.md)
6	
7	> **Before writing Vitest unit tests, execute the following skill** — read the SKILL.md and follow its instructions:
8	>
9	> 1. `.cursor/skills/vitest/SKILL.md`
10	
11	> **Before writing Playwright E2E tests, execute the following skill** — read the SKILL.md and follow its instructions:
12	>
13	> 1. `.cursor/skills/playwright-best-practices/SKILL.md`
14	
15	**Related coverage in other AGENTS files (do not duplicate):**
16	
17	- `AGENTS-SECURITY.md` — 4-step authenticate/validate/execute/revalidate pattern that tests must verify
18	- `AGENTS-ACCESSIBILITY.md` — Manual a11y testing checklist
19	
20	---
21	
22	## Testing Philosophy
23	
24	### TDD Where It Hurts
25	
26	Use TDD (test first) where bugs have real impact and the feedback loop is fast. Use Test-After for framework-coupled or UI-heavy code.
27	
28	| Code Layer                           | Strategy                                  | Tool         |
29	| ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------- | ------------ |
30	| Zod validation schemas               | **TDD** (test first)                      | Vitest       |
31	| Utility functions (`lib/utils.ts`)   | **TDD** (test first)                      | Vitest       |
32	| Server Action logic                  | **TDD for validation, Test-After for DB** | Vitest       |
33	| Junction table sync logic            | **Test-After**                            | Vitest       |
34	| Client Components with custom logic  | **Test-After** (optional)                 | Vitest + RTL |
35	| Pages, layouts, route flows          | **Test-After**                            | Playwright   |
36	| Auth flows (login, protected routes) | **Test-After**                            | Playwright   |
37	| Public page rendering                | **Test-After**                            | Playwright   |
38	
39	**TDD cycle**: Red (failing test) → Green (minimum code to pass) → Refactor (clean up, tests stay green) → Repeat.
40	
41	### When NOT to Write Tests
42	
43	- **shadcn/ui primitives** — already tested by Radix UI upstream
44	- **better-auth configuration** — declarative config, not testable logic
45	- **Tailwind CSS classes** — visual output, not unit-testable
46	- **Next.js framework behavior** (routing, layouts, streaming) — tested by the Next.js team
47	- **Simple data fetching pages** with no business logic — covered by E2E naturally
48	- **React Server Components with unit tests** — async RSCs not supported by any unit testing tool; use Playwright
49	
50	---
51	
52	## Tool Setup
53	
54	### Vitest
55	
56	**Config file**: `vitest.config.mts` — already in the repo.
57	
58	Project-specific settings:
59	
60	- `environment: 'jsdom'` — simulates DOM for component tests (override per-file with `// @vitest-environment node`)
61	- `plugins: [tsconfigPaths()]` — resolves `@/*` path alias
62	- `include: ['tests/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}']` — only `tests/` directory
63	- `exclude: ['e2e/**']` — keeps Playwright tests separate
64	- `globals: false` — explicit imports required
65	- `css: false` — skips Tailwind processing in tests
66	
67	### Playwright
68	
69	**Config file**: `playwright.config.ts` — already in the repo.
70	
71	Project-specific settings:
72	
73	- `testDir: './e2e'` — all E2E tests in `e2e/`
74	- `baseURL: 'http://localhost:3000'` — enables `page.goto('/')`
75	- `webServer: { command: 'pnpm dev' }` — auto-starts dev server
76	- `trace: 'on-first-retry'` — captures traces for debugging CI failures
77	- `forbidOnly: !!process.env.CI` — fails CI if `.only` is left in
78	
79	---
80	
81	## Test File Location & Naming
82	
83	```
84	tests/                         # Vitest unit & component tests
85	├── schemas/                   # Zod schema validation tests
86	│   ├── project.test.ts
87	│   ├── experience.test.ts
88	│   ├── skill.test.ts
89	│   ├── social-link.test.ts
90	│   └── settings.test.ts
91	├── actions/                   # Server Action logic tests
92	│   └── projects.test.ts       # (one per entity)
93	├── utils/
94	│   └── utils.test.ts
95	└── components/                # Client component tests (optional)
96	
97	e2e/                           # Playwright E2E tests
98	├── auth.spec.ts               # Login, logout, protected route redirects
99	├── projects.spec.ts           # CRUD flows
100	├── public-page.spec.ts        # Public portfolio rendering
101	└── accessibility.spec.ts      # axe-core automated checks
102	```
103	
104	### Naming Rules
105	
106	| Convention | Vitest                                                         | Playwright                                   |
107	| ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
108	| Extension  | `.test.ts` / `.test.tsx`                                       | `.spec.ts`                                   |
109	| Directory  | `tests/`                                                       | `e2e/`                                       |
110	| File names | Mirror source (`projects.test.ts` → `lib/actions/projects.ts`) | Named by flow (`auth.spec.ts`)               |
111	| Test names | Behavior: `"rejects empty title"`                              | User action: `"should create a new project"` |
112	
113	---
114	
115	## Mocking Strategy
116	
117	> Full mock code blocks with complete implementations: [AGENTS-TESTING-REFERENCE.md](./AGENTS-TESTING-REFERENCE.md#mocking-code-blocks)
118	
119	### Summary
120	
121	| Dependency                | Mock Target            | Pattern                                                                  |
122	| ------------------------- | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
123	| Database (Turso/Drizzle)  | `@/db`                 | `vi.mock("@/db", () => ({ db: { insert: vi.fn()... } }))`                |
124	| Authentication            | `@/lib/server-session` | `vi.mock(...)` then `vi.mocked(getServerSession).mockResolvedValue(...)` |
125	| `redirect()`              | `next/navigation`      | Mock to throw `Error("REDIRECT:/path")` — mirrors Next.js behavior       |
126	| `revalidatePath()`        | `next/cache`           | `vi.mock("next/cache", () => ({ revalidatePath: vi.fn() }))`             |
127	| `headers()` / `cookies()` | `next/headers`         | `vi.mock("next/headers", ...)`                                           |
128	| `FormData`                | Manual creation        | Helper: `createFormData(record)` — see reference file                    |
129	
130	### Rules
131	
132	- **Mock at the module level** (`vi.mock(...)`) — Vitest hoists these calls automatically
133	- **Use `vi.mocked()` for type-safe mock access** — gives TypeScript autocompletion
134	- **Reset mocks between tests** — `beforeEach(() => { vi.clearAllMocks(); })`
135	- **Don't mock what you're testing** — test the schema? Don't mock Zod. Test the action? Mock the DB, not the action
136	- **Prefer shallow mocks** — only mock what the specific test needs
137	
138	---
139	
140	## What to Test Per Entity
141	
142	### Vitest (Unit Tests)
143	
144	| What to Test                                  | Example                                                        |
145	| --------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
146	| Schema accepts valid data                     | All required fields present, correct types                     |
147	| Schema rejects missing required fields        | Empty title, empty description                                 |
148	| Schema rejects invalid values                 | Status `"deleted"` (not in enum), title over 200 chars         |
149	| Schema handles optional fields                | Empty URL allowed, invalid URL rejected                        |
150	| Schema `.or(z.literal(""))` for optional URLs | Empty string passes, `"not-a-url"` fails                       |
151	| Action authenticates before executing         | Returns redirect when session is null                          |
152	| Action validates input before DB call         | Invalid data never reaches `db.insert()`                       |
153	| Action calls correct Drizzle operations       | `db.insert()` called with validated data                       |
154	| Action revalidates/redirects correctly        | `redirect()` or `revalidatePath()` called                      |
155	| Junction table sync adds/removes skills       | New skills inserted, removed skills deleted, unchanged ignored |
156	
157	### Playwright (E2E Tests)
158	
159	| What to Test             | Example                                             |
160	| ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------- |
161	| Login flow               | Credentials → redirect to dashboard                 |
162	| Auth protection          | `/dashboard` without session → redirect to `/login` |
163	| Create entity            | Fill form → submit → entity in list                 |
164	| Edit entity              | Click edit → modify → save → changes visible        |
165	| Delete entity            | Click delete → confirm → removed from list          |
166	| Validation errors        | Submit empty form → error messages visible          |
167	| Public page renders      | Visit `/` → all sections visible                    |
168	| Accessibility (axe-core) | No WCAG 2.2 AA violations                           |
169	
170	---
171	
172	## Playwright E2E Patterns
173	
174	### Authentication Setup
175	
176	Log in once and reuse the session across tests via Playwright's storage state. See [AGENTS-TESTING-REFERENCE.md](./AGENTS-TESTING-REFERENCE.md#playwright-auth-setup) for full auth setup code and project config.
177	
178	Key points:
179	
180	- `e2e/auth.setup.ts` logs in and saves cookies to `e2e/.auth/user.json`
181	- Add `e2e/.auth/` to `.gitignore`
182	- Authenticated projects depend on the setup project
183	
184	### Locator Priority
185	
186	1. `getByRole` (best — matches accessibility tree)
187	2. `getByLabel` (form inputs)
188	3. `getByText` (visible text)
189	4. `getByTestId` (last resort — add `data-testid` only when no accessible locator works)
190	5. CSS selectors (avoid — fragile)
191	
192	### Page Object Pattern
193	
194	Use sparingly for pages with many repeated interactions:
195	
196	```typescript
197	// e2e/pages/projects-page.ts
198	export class ProjectsPage {
199		constructor(private page: Page) {}
200		async goto() {
201			await this.page.goto('/dashboard/projects');
202		}
203		async createProject(data: { title: string }) {
204			/* fill + submit */
205		}
206		async expectProjectVisible(title: string) {
207			/* assert */
208		}
209	}
210	```
211	
212	---
213	
214	## Good Practices
215	
216	### Vitest
217	
218	- **One assertion per concept** — `"rejects invalid URLs"` tests only URL validation
219	- **Arrange-Act-Assert** — set up data, call function, check result
220	- **Test edge cases** — empty strings, `null`, boundary values, special characters
221	- **Use `it.each` for parameterized tests** — same behavior, different inputs
222	- **Keep tests independent** — `beforeEach` to reset, never rely on execution order
223	
224	### Playwright
225	
226	- **Test user-visible behavior** — `toBeVisible`, `toContainText`, not DOM structure
227	- **Use auto-waiting** — don't add `page.waitForTimeout()` unless absolutely necessary
228	- **Test the unhappy path** — error messages, unauthorized redirects, delete confirmations
229	
230	### General
231	
232	- **Run `pnpm test` before committing**
233	- **Run `pnpm test:e2e` before deploying**
234	- **Don't aim for 100% coverage** — focus on code where bugs have real impact
235	- **Keep Vitest suite under 10 seconds** — if slower, check for real network calls or missing mocks
236	
237	---
238	
239	## Setup Checklist (TODO)
240	
241	- [ ] Add `e2e/.auth/` to `.gitignore`
242	- [ ] Install `@axe-core/playwright` for accessibility testing
243	- [ ] Create GitHub Actions workflow — see [AGENTS-TESTING-REFERENCE.md](./AGENTS-TESTING-REFERENCE.md#ci-github-actions-workflow)
244	- [ ] Set up test database credentials as GitHub Actions secrets
245	- [ ] Replace `e2e/example.spec.ts` with real project tests
246
```

1	# AGENTS-DESIGN.md
2	
3	Visual design system for the portfolio's public page — theme tokens, bento grid vocabulary, card anatomy, pill navbar, and interactive patterns.
4	
5	> **Before applying or extending this design system, execute the following skills** — read each SKILL.md and follow its instructions:
6	>
7	> 1. `.cursor/skills/shadcn/SKILL.md` (component styling, token usage)
8	> 2. `.cursor/skills/tailwind-design-system/SKILL.md` (Tailwind v4 `@theme`, OKLCH)
9	> 3. `.cursor/skills/frontend-design/SKILL.md` (visual quality, polish)
10	> 4. `.cursor/skills/web-design-guidelines/SKILL.md` (compliance review)
11	
12	**Related coverage in other AGENTS files (do not duplicate):**
13	
14	- `AGENTS-ANIMATIONS.md` — timing, easing, Motion/NumberFlow rules
15	- `AGENTS-ACCESSIBILITY.md` — contrast ratios, touch targets, reduced motion, landmarks
16	- `AGENTS-PERFORMANCE.md` — code splitting, loading states, bundle optimization
17	
18	---
19	
20	## 1. Design Philosophy
21	
22	Spatial density and card scale ARE the visual language. Visual hierarchy comes from card size contrast, not from typographic weight or color loudness. The portfolio should feel **technical but warm** — a developer who cares about craft.
23	
24	### Principles
25	
26	1. **Cards first** — every piece of content lives inside a card. The grid IS the layout.
27	2. **Generous radii** — large corner radii on cards, pill-shaped nav. Soften the technical content.
28	3. **Surface contrast, not shadow** — cards float via background-to-card color difference, not drop shadows.
29	4. **Luminous accent on dark** — dark mode is the hero. Primary cyan glows, amber accent energizes.
30	5. **Restraint** — one primary, one accent, cool neutrals. No color noise.
31	6. **Every decision works in both themes** — light and dark are designed in parallel, not as afterthoughts.
32	
33	---
34	
35	## 2. Theme Tokens
36	
37	All color values are in OKLCH for perceptual uniformity (as recommended by the `tailwind-design-system` skill). The tokens map directly to shadcn/ui's variable system and the existing `@theme inline` block in `globals.css`.
38	
39	> **Implementation note**: when applying these tokens, replace the hex values in `:root` and `.dark` selectors in `globals.css`. The `@theme inline` block that maps `--color-*: var(--*)` stays unchanged.
40	
41	### 2.1 Color Palette — Light Mode
42	
43	Design intent: Lavender-tinted off-white background, pure white cards, deep sapphire primary, vivid warm gold accent. Distinctly indigo-leaning — not teal.
44	
45	```css
46	:root {
47		--background: oklch(0.975 0.008 270);
48		--foreground: oklch(0.155 0.025 270);
49	
50		--card: oklch(1 0 0);
51		--card-foreground: oklch(0.155 0.025 270);
52	
53		--popover: oklch(1 0 0);
54		--popover-foreground: oklch(0.155 0.025 270);
55	
56		--primary: oklch(0.4 0.17 250);
57		--primary-foreground: oklch(0.985 0.005 250);
58	
59		--secondary: oklch(0.945 0.012 270);
60		--secondary-foreground: oklch(0.195 0.025 270);
61	
62		--muted: oklch(0.92 0.008 270);
63		--muted-foreground: oklch(0.43 0.02 265);
64	
65		--accent: oklch(0.7 0.18 55);
66		--accent-foreground: oklch(0.2 0.05 55);
67	
68		--destructive: oklch(0.55 0.22 25);
69		--destructive-foreground: oklch(0.985 0.005 25);
70	
71		--border: oklch(0.885 0.012 270);
72		--input: oklch(0.885 0.012 270);
73		--ring: oklch(0.48 0.17 250);
74	}
75	```
76	
77	### 2.2 Color Palette — Dark Mode
78	
79	Design intent: Deep indigo-black surface with real blue tint, elevated cards with indigo sheen, electric blue primary, vivid gold accent. Moody and immersive.
80	
81	```css
82	.dark {
83		--background: oklch(0.12 0.025 275);
84		--foreground: oklch(0.95 0.008 265);
85	
86		--card: oklch(0.175 0.022 270);
87		--card-foreground: oklch(0.95 0.008 265);
88	
89		--popover: oklch(0.175 0.022 270);
90		--popover-foreground: oklch(0.95 0.008 265);
91	
92		--primary: oklch(0.75 0.17 235);
93		--primary-foreground: oklch(0.12 0.035 235);
94	
95		--secondary: oklch(0.225 0.018 275);
96		--secondary-foreground: oklch(0.91 0.008 265);
97	
98		--muted: oklch(0.225 0.018 275);
99		--muted-foreground: oklch(0.58 0.016 265);
100	
101		--accent: oklch(0.8 0.17 50);
102		--accent-foreground: oklch(0.12 0.045 50);
103	
104		--destructive: oklch(0.64 0.2 25);
105		--destructive-foreground: oklch(0.12 0.025 25);
106	
107		--border: oklch(0.265 0.018 275);
108		--input: oklch(0.265 0.018 275);
109		--ring: oklch(0.75 0.17 235);
110	}
111	```
112	
113	### 2.3 Color Design Rationale
114	
115	| Token              | Light                                        | Dark                                         | Design intent                                                   |
116	| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
117	| `background`       | Lavender off-white (L=0.975, C=0.008, H=270) | Deep indigo-black (L=0.12, C=0.025, H=275)   | Tinted surfaces with personality, not neutral                   |
118	| `card`             | Pure white (L=1.0)                           | Elevated indigo (L=0.175, C=0.022, H=270)    | Cards float above background via surface contrast               |
119	| `primary`          | Deep sapphire (L=0.40, C=0.17, H=250)        | Electric blue (L=0.75, C=0.17, H=235)        | Signature color — rich indigo-blue, clearly different from teal |
120	| `accent`           | Vivid warm gold (L=0.70, C=0.18, H=55)       | Bright gold (L=0.80, C=0.17, H=50)           | Complementary warmth, high saturation for CTAs                  |
121	| `muted-foreground` | Mid gray (L=0.43)                            | Subdued gray (L=0.58)                        | Secondary text — verify ≥ 4.5:1 contrast during implementation  |
122	| `border`           | Cool lavender line (L=0.885, C=0.012, H=270) | Indigo-tinted line (L=0.265, C=0.018, H=275) | Visible but non-competing                                       |
123	
124	The hue axis centers on **H=250** (sapphire-indigo) for primary and **H=50–55** (warm gold) for accent — a complementary pair that creates strong visual tension. All neutral surfaces share **H=265–275** (cool indigo-gray) for cohesion. Chroma is pushed higher than typical (C=0.17) for both primary and accent to give the palette real personality.
125

201	### 2.7 Typography Tokens
202

205	| Token               | Value                  | Use                      |

211	
212	### 2.8 Border Radius
213	
214	| Element                  | Class                             | Value          | Purpose                              |
215	| ------------------------ | --------------------------------- | -------------- | ------------------------------------ |
216	| Grid cards               | `rounded-4xl`                     | 2rem (32px)    | Signature aesthetic — generous, soft |
217	| Pill navbar              | `rounded-full`                    | 9999px         | Capsule shape                        |
218	| Nav active indicator     | `rounded-full`                    | 9999px         | Pill highlight inside navbar         |
219	| shadcn components        | `rounded-lg` (default `--radius`) | 0.5rem (8px)   | Buttons, inputs, dialogs             |
220	| Nested elements in cards | `rounded-xl`                      | 0.75rem (12px) | Tags, badges, inner containers       |
221

229	> }
230	> ```

232	### 2.9 Shadows
233	
234	Minimal shadow usage — cards float via surface color contrast.
235	
236	| Element          | Light mode                      | Dark mode                             |
237	| ---------------- | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
238	| Grid cards       | `shadow-none` or `shadow-sm`    | `shadow-none`                         |
239	| Popover/dropdown | `shadow-md`                     | `shadow-lg` (needs more lift on dark) |
240	| Navbar           | `shadow-sm` or frosted backdrop | `shadow-none` + border                |
241	
242	The base `Card` component in `components/ui/card.tsx` has `shadow-sm` by default. Grid cards override this in `GridItem` if needed.
243	
244	---
245	
246	## 3. Grid System
247	
248	The bento grid uses `react-grid-layout` (Responsive). This section defines the shared vocabulary for grid configuration.
249	
250	### 3.1 Breakpoints & Columns
251	
252	| Breakpoint | Name    | Min width | Columns | Use                 |
253	| ---------- | ------- | --------- | ------- | ------------------- |
254	| `lg`       | Desktop | 996px     | 8       | Full bento layout   |
255	| `md`       | Tablet  | 768px     | 4       | Simplified 2-column |
256	| `sm`       | Mobile  | 0px       | 1       | Single column stack |
257	
258	### 3.2 Row Height & Gap
259	
260	| Property            | Value         | Notes                                                  |
261	| ------------------- | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
262	| `rowHeight`         | `30px`        | Base unit — card height = `h × 30px`                   |
263	| Gap (margin)        | `16px` (1rem) | Inter-card spacing via react-grid-layout `margin` prop |
264	| Container max-width | `1200px`      | `max-w-[1200px] mx-auto`                               |
265	| Container padding   | `px-[3.5vw]`  | Responsive horizontal breathing room                   |
266	
267	### 3.3 Named Card Sizes
268	
269	Shared vocabulary for layout composition. Sizes refer to `{w, h}` values in react-grid-layout at the `lg` breakpoint (8 columns).
270	
271	| Name         | w × h  | Pixel size (approx)    | Use                                              |
272	| ------------ | ------ | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
273	| **hero**     | 4 × 16 | ~half width × 480px    | Primary content — about, featured project        |
274	| **wide**     | 4 × 8  | ~half width × 240px    | Standard wide — project card, about              |
275	| **standard** | 2 × 8  | ~quarter width × 240px | Default — map, contact, compact project          |
276	| **tall**     | 2 × 16 | ~quarter width × 480px | Vertical emphasis — detailed project, experience |
277	| **compact**  | 2 × 4  | ~quarter width × 120px | Minimal — stat, link, social                     |
278	
279	At `md` (4 columns): hero → 4×12, wide → 4×8, standard → 2×8, tall → 2×12, compact → 2×4.
280	
281	At `sm` (1 column): all cards become 1×auto (full width, content-driven height).
282	
283	### 3.4 Content Adaptation Rules
284	
285	- When a card goes from **tall** to **wide** (responsive rearrangement), content reflows from vertical to horizontal. Use `flex-direction` or `grid-template` changes.
286	- **Never truncate essential content to fit a card size** — resize the card instead.
287	- Images and maps in cards use `object-cover` + `overflow-hidden` on the card for radius clipping.
288	
289	### 3.5 Responsive Priority
290	
291	At `sm` (1 column), not all cards need to show. Priority order:
292	
293	1. **about** — always visible, first position
294	2. **project** (featured) — max 2–3 cards
295	3. **experience** — collapsed or summary
296	4. **contact** — always visible
297	5. **map** — hidden or moved to bottom
298	
299	---
300	
301	## 4. Card System
302	
303	The card is the fundamental unit of the design. All content lives inside a `Card` component with variant-specific composition.
304	
305	### 4.1 Base Card
306	
307	```tsx
308	<Card className="size-full min-h-0 min-w-0 overflow-hidden bg-card rounded-4xl">
309	```
310	
311	| Property   | Value                        | Notes                                                                     |
312	| ---------- | ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
313	| Background | `bg-card`                    | Uses `--card` token                                                       |
314	| Radius     | `rounded-4xl` (2rem)         | Overrides Card's default `rounded-xl`                                     |
315	| Border     | Subtle or none               | Light: `border` (default). Dark: consider `border-border/50` for subtlety |
316	| Shadow     | `shadow-none` to `shadow-sm` | Minimal — cards float via surface contrast                                |
317	| Overflow   | `overflow-hidden`            | Clips children to rounded corners                                         |
318	| Min sizing | `min-h-0 min-w-0`            | Required for react-grid-layout                                            |
319	
320	### 4.2 Content-Type Variants
321	
322	| Variant      | Padding     | Structure                                                | Notes                                  |
323	| ------------ | ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
324	| `about`      | `py-6 px-6` | Free-form children (image, text, CTA)                    | Flexible layout via flex/grid          |
325	| `project`    | `py-6`      | `CardHeader` → `CardContent` → `CardFooter` (3-row grid) | Status badges use semantic tokens      |
326	| `experience` | `py-6 px-6` | Role, company, dates, skill tags                         | Compact for standard/wide sizes        |
327	| `contact`    | `py-6 px-6` | CTA-focused, minimal content                             | Accent color for CTA button            |
328	| `map`        | `p-0`       | Full-bleed map, zero padding                             | `overflow-hidden` clips to card radius |
329	| `media`      | `p-0`       | Full-bleed image/screenshot                              | Same as map — future use               |
330	
331	### 4.3 Internal Spacing
332	
333	| Zone                             | Value                    | Notes                         |
334	| -------------------------------- | ------------------------ | ----------------------------- |
335	| Card outer padding               | `py-6` (24px top/bottom) | Non-map variants              |
336	| Header/Content/Footer horizontal | `px-6` (24px left/right) | Via shadcn Card subcomponents |
337	| Content gap                      | `gap-6` (24px)           | Default Card flex gap         |
338	| Between title and description    | `gap-2` (8px)            | Via CardHeader grid           |
339	
340	### 4.4 Interactive States
341	
342	| State            | Treatment                                  | Reference                |
343	| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------ |
344	| Hover            | Subtle border shift to `border-primary/30` | Soft glow, not jarring   |
345	| Focus (keyboard) | `ring-2 ring-ring ring-offset-2`           | WCAG 2.4.7 focus visible |
346	| Active/pressed   | `scale-[0.99]` via transition              | Micro-feedback           |
347	| Disabled         | `opacity-60 pointer-events-none`           | Standard pattern         |
348	
349	Hover animation timing: `transition-colors duration-200 ease-out`. See `AGENTS-ANIMATIONS.md` for the full timing table.
350	
351	---
352	
353	## 5. Navigation — Pill Navbar
354	
355	The navigation is a floating pill-shaped bar anchored at the top-center of the viewport.
356	
357	### 5.1 Shape & Structure
358	
359	```
360	┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
361	│  [●All]    Projects    Experience    Contact  [◐] │
362	└──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
363	       ↑ active indicator (sliding pill)        ↑ theme toggle
364	```
365	
366	| Property             | Value                                                                  |
367	| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
368	| Container shape      | `rounded-full` (pill)                                                  |
369	| Container background | Light: `bg-secondary` — Dark: `bg-card` with `border border-border/50` |
370	| Container height     | `h-12` to `h-14` (48–56px) — NOT the current `h-32`                    |
371	| Horizontal padding   | `px-2`                                                                 |
372	| Item padding         | `px-4 py-2`                                                            |
373	| Item font            | `text-sm font-medium`                                                  |
374	
375	### 5.2 Active Indicator
376	
377	A colored pill that slides behind the active nav item, animated with Motion's `layoutId`:
378	
379	```tsx
380	{
381		isActive && (
382			<motion.span
383				layoutId="nav-indicator"
384				className="bg-primary absolute inset-0 rounded-full"
385				transition={{ type: 'spring', stiffness: 350, damping: 30 }}
386			/>
387		);
388	}
389	```
390	
391	| Property         | Value                                                                      |
392	| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
393	| Background       | `bg-primary` (cyan-blue in both themes)                                    |
394	| Text on active   | `text-primary-foreground`                                                  |
395	| Text on inactive | `text-muted-foreground`                                                    |
396	| Animation        | `layoutId` spring transition (see `AGENTS-ANIMATIONS.md` for Motion rules) |
397	
398	### 5.3 Theme Toggle
399	
400	Place the theme toggle as the last element in the navbar, visually separated with subtle spacing. Use the existing `ModeToggle` component. Inside the pill navbar, render it as an icon-only button (`size="icon"`) with `rounded-full`.
401	
402	### 5.4 Placement & Responsiveness
403	
404	| Breakpoint  | Placement                   | Adaptation                                     |
405	| ----------- | --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
406	| `lg` / `md` | Top-center, fixed or sticky | Full labels + icons                            |
407	| `sm`        | Bottom-center, fixed        | Icons only — active item expands to show label |
408	
409	Mobile bottom placement: `fixed bottom-4 left-1/2 -translate-x-1/2 z-50`. Add `pb-20` to the main container on mobile to prevent overlap.
410	
411	---
412	
413	## 6. Typography
414	
415	Type scale designed for card-constrained layouts where space is limited.
416	
417	### 6.1 Type Scale
418	
419	| Role              | Classes                                | Use                                               |
420	| ----------------- | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
421	| Page heading      | `text-2xl font-bold tracking-tight`    | User's name (only element outside card hierarchy) |
422	| Card title        | `text-base font-semibold leading-none` | CardTitle (shadcn default)                        |
423	| Card title (hero) | `text-lg font-semibold tracking-tight` | Larger cards (hero, wide)                         |
424	| Card description  | `text-sm text-muted-foreground`        | CardDescription (shadcn default)                  |
425	| Body text         | `text-sm`                              | In-card body content                              |
426	| Metadata          | `text-xs text-muted-foreground`        | Dates, counts, secondary info                     |
427	| Code / technical  | `font-mono text-xs`                    | Tech stack tags, code references                  |
428	
429	### 6.2 Letter Spacing
430	
431	| Element                  | Class            | Value    |
432	| ------------------------ | ---------------- | -------- |
433	| Page heading             | `tracking-tight` | -0.025em |
434	| Card titles (hero)       | `tracking-tight` | -0.025em |
435	| Card titles (standard)   | default          | 0        |
436	| Body & metadata          | default          | 0        |
437	| All-caps labels (if any) | `tracking-wide`  | +0.025em |
438	
439	### 6.3 Truncation & Clamping
440	
441	For card descriptions that may overflow:
442	
443	```tsx
444	<p className="text-muted-foreground line-clamp-2 text-sm">{description}</p>
445	```
446	
447	| Card size   | Line clamp              |
448	| ----------- | ----------------------- |
449	| compact     | `line-clamp-1`          |
450	| standard    | `line-clamp-2`          |
451	| wide        | `line-clamp-3`          |
452	| tall / hero | No clamp (content fits) |
453

456	## 7. Iconography & Media
457	
458	### 7.1 Icon Sizing
459	
460	| Context              | Size class            | Pixels  | Example                 |
461	| -------------------- | --------------------- | ------- | ----------------------- |
462	| Inline with text     | `size-4`              | 16px    | Status icon, metadata   |
463	| Standalone button    | `size-5`              | 20px    | External link, GitHub   |
464	| Primary action / nav | `size-5` to `size-6`  | 20–24px | Nav icons, theme toggle |
465	| Hero / decorative    | `size-8` to `size-10` | 32–40px | Card accent icon        |
466	
467	### 7.2 Icon Libraries
468	
469	| Library         | Use                                         | Import                                   |
470	| --------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
471	| **Lucide**      | UI actions (arrows, edit, trash, etc.)      | `lucide-react`                           |
472	| **react-icons** | Brand logos (GitHub, LinkedIn, tech stacks) | `react-icons/fa`, `react-icons/ri`, etc. |
473	
474	Decorative icons use `aria-hidden="true"`. Functional icons in icon-only buttons need `aria-label` on the button (see `AGENTS-ACCESSIBILITY.md`).
475	
476	### 7.3 Profile Image
477	
478	| Property  | Value                                                    |
479	| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
480	| Component | `next/image`                                             |
481	| Shape     | `rounded-2xl` or `rounded-full`                          |
482	| Size      | Constrained by card — `max-w-full h-auto object-contain` |
483	| Alt text  | Descriptive: `"Gonzalo Pozo, Full Stack Developer"`      |
484	
485	### 7.4 Map Card
486	
487	Full-bleed treatment — the map fills the entire card:
488	
489	```tsx
490	<GridItem variant="map" ...>
491	  <Map center={...} zoom={13} attributionControl={false}>
492	    <MapControls />
493	  </Map>
494	</GridItem>
495	```
496	
497	The `variant="map"` applies `p-0` and `overflow-hidden` clips the map to `rounded-4xl`.

500	
501	## 8. Interactive Patterns
502	
503	### 8.1 Link & Button Treatment
504	
505	| Element              | Pattern                                                      | Notes                                    |
506	| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------- |
507	| External link (icon) | `text-muted-foreground hover:text-primary transition-colors` | Replaces hardcoded `hover:text-blue-600` |
508	| CTA button           | `bg-primary text-primary-foreground hover:bg-primary/90`     | Default shadcn Button                    |
509	| Accent CTA           | `bg-accent text-accent-foreground hover:bg-accent/90`        | High-emphasis actions                    |
510	| Ghost button         | `hover:bg-secondary hover:text-secondary-foreground`         | Low-emphasis, in-card actions            |
511	| Icon button          | `rounded-full` variant, `size="icon"`                        | GitHub, external link icons              |
512	
513	### 8.2 Card-Level vs Element-Level Click Areas
514	
515	- **Navigational cards** (e.g., "See more projects"): the entire card is the click target. Use a wrapping `<a>` or button with `absolute inset-0`.
516	- **Content cards** with multiple actions (repo link, live link, "show more"): individual clickable elements. No card-level click.
517	
518	### 8.3 External Link Pattern
519	
520	Replace the current `IconContext.Provider` approach with explicit token-based styling:
521	
522	```tsx
523	<a
524		href={url}
525		target="_blank"
526		rel="noopener noreferrer"
527		className="text-muted-foreground hover:text-primary transition-colors"
528		aria-label="View repository on GitHub"
529	>
530		<FaGithub className="size-5" aria-hidden="true" />
531	</a>
532	```
533	
534	### 8.4 Theme Toggle in Navbar
535	
536	Use the existing `ModeToggle` component. Style it to match the navbar's pill aesthetic:
537	
538	- `rounded-full` shape
539	- Same padding as other nav items
540	- No outline/border — blends into the navbar

543	
544	## 9. Responsive Behavior
545	
546	### 9.1 Breakpoint Summary
547	
548	| Breakpoint     | Grid cols | Nav placement | Cards visible          |
549	| -------------- | --------- | ------------- | ---------------------- |
550	| `lg` (≥ 996px) | 8         | Top-center    | All                    |
551	| `md` (≥ 768px) | 4         | Top-center    | All (rearranged)       |
552	| `sm` (< 768px) | 1         | Bottom-center | Priority subset (§3.5) |
553	
554	### 9.2 Content Priority at Narrow Widths
555	
556	At `sm`, the grid becomes a single column. Content ordering:
557	
558	1. About card (always first)
559	2. Featured project(s) (1–2 max)
560	3. Contact card
561	4. Additional content (collapsed or hidden)
562	5. Map card (last or hidden)
563	
564	### 9.3 Touch Targets
565	
566	Per WCAG 2.5.8 and `AGENTS-ACCESSIBILITY.md`:
567	
568	- Minimum touch target: **44 × 44px**
569	- Nav items: `min-h-11` (44px) ensures compliance
570	- Icon buttons: `size="icon"` (40 × 40px default) — add `min-w-11 min-h-11` if used as primary actions
571	- Card "Show more" buttons: standard Button size (≥ 44px height)
572	
573	### 9.4 Nav Adaptation
574	
575	- **Desktop / Tablet**: full labels (`All`, `Projects`, `Experience`, `Contact`) + theme toggle
576	- **Mobile**: icons only, active item shows label. Container shrinks. Fixed to bottom of viewport.
577	- **Transition**: `md` breakpoint triggers the switch. Use CSS `hidden md:inline` for label visibility.
578

582	
583	When applying or modifying this design system:
584	
585	- [ ] All text-on-surface combinations meet WCAG AA contrast (4.5:1 normal, 3:1 large) — use WebAIM Contrast Checker
586	- [ ] `muted-foreground` on `background` meets 4.5:1 in both themes
587	- [ ] `primary` as text on `card` meets 4.5:1 in both themes
588	- [ ] Cards visually separate from background in both themes (surface contrast)
589	- [ ] No hardcoded colors remain — all use design tokens
590	- [ ] Status colors use `text-status-*` instead of `text-green-600` etc.
591	- [ ] External link hover uses `hover:text-primary` instead of `hover:text-blue-600`
592	- [ ] Grid card radius is consistently `rounded-4xl`
593	- [ ] Navbar height is `h-12` to `h-14`, not `h-32`
594	- [ ] Run `AGENTS-ACCESSIBILITY.md` pre-production audit after visual changes
