16	## Next.js Components over HTML
17	
18	**Always use Next.js components instead of HTML equivalents** — they provide built-in optimizations and accessibility.
19	
20	| HTML                 | Next.js Component | Import             | Why                                                          |
21	| -------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
22	| `<a>`                | `<Link>`          | `next/link`        | Client-side nav, prefetching, accessible by default          |
23	| `<form>`             | `<Form>`          | `next/form`        | Prefetches loading UI, progressive enhancement               |
24	| `<img>`              | `<Image>`         | `next/image`       | Lazy loading, responsive srcset, enforces `alt` + dimensions |
25	| Manual font `<link>` | `next/font`       | `next/font/google` | Self-hosted, zero layout shift                               |
26	| `<script>`           | `<Script>`        | `next/script`      | Loading strategies, avoids blocking                          |
27	
28	### Rules
29	
30	- **Never use `<a>` for internal links** — use `<Link>` (renders `<a>` with prefetching)
31	- **Never use `<img>`** — use `<Image>` which requires `alt`, `width`, `height` (or `fill`)
32	- **Never load fonts via `<link>` tags** — use `next/font` for self-hosting
33	- **Use `<Form>` from `next/form` for navigation forms** (search, filters); regular `<form>` with `action` is fine for Server Action mutations
34	
35	---
36	
37	## Semantic Layout Structure
38	
39	The public portfolio page must use semantic HTML landmarks in `(public)/layout.tsx`:
40	
41	```typescript
42	<>
43	  <SkipLink />
44	  <header>
45	    <nav aria-label="Main navigation">{/* Links */}</nav>
46	  </header>
47	  <main id="main-content" tabIndex={-1}>
48	    {children}
49	  </main>
50	  <footer>
51	    <nav aria-label="Social links">{/* Links */}</nav>
52	  </footer>
53	</>
54	```
55	
56	### Rules
57	
58	- Exactly **one `<main>`** per page
59	- `<nav>` needs `aria-label` when multiple navs exist on the same page
60	- Use `<section aria-labelledby="heading-id">` for major content sections (projects, experiences, skills)
61	- Admin dashboard uses shadcn `Sidebar` which handles landmarks via Radix
62	
63	### Section Pattern
64	
65	```typescript
66	<section aria-labelledby="projects-heading">
67	  <h2 id="projects-heading">Projects</h2>
68	  {/* Cards */}
69	</section>
70	```
71	
72	---
73	
74	## Skip Link
75	
76	Required for WCAG 2.4.1 (Bypass Blocks). Place as first child inside `<body>` or public layout.
77	
78	```typescript
79	// components/skip-link.tsx
80	export function SkipLink() {
81	  return (
82	    <a
83	      href="#main-content"
84	      className="sr-only focus:not-sr-only focus:absolute focus:top-4 focus:left-4 focus:z-50 focus:px-4 focus:py-2 focus:bg-primary focus:text-primary-foreground focus:rounded-md focus:outline-none focus:ring-2 focus:ring-ring focus:ring-offset-2"
85	    >
86	      Skip to main content
87	    </a>
88	  );
89	}
90	```
91	
92	The `<main>` element must have `id="main-content"` and `tabIndex={-1}` to receive focus.
93	
94	---
95	
96	## shadcn Component Accessibility Notes
97	
98	### Icon Buttons Need `aria-label`
99	
100	```typescript
101	// Icon-only button — MUST have aria-label
102	<Button variant="ghost" size="icon" aria-label="Delete project">
103	  <Trash2 className="h-4 w-4" aria-hidden="true" />
104	</Button>
105	```
106	
107	### Dialog — Auto-Accessible
108	
109	shadcn `Dialog` (Radix) automatically traps focus, returns focus on close, closes on Escape. **Always include `DialogTitle` and `DialogDescription`** — Radix uses them for `aria-labelledby`/`aria-describedby`. Hide description visually with `sr-only` if needed.
110	
111	### Table — Add `scope` and `caption`
112	
113	```typescript
114	<Table>
115	  <TableCaption>Portfolio projects managed from the dashboard</TableCaption>
116	  <TableHeader>
117	    <TableRow>
118	      <TableHead scope="col">Title</TableHead>
119	      <TableHead scope="col">Status</TableHead>
120	      <TableHead scope="col">Actions</TableHead>
121	    </TableRow>
122	  </TableHeader>
123	  <TableBody>
124	    {projects.map((p) => (
125	      <TableRow key={p.id}>
126	        <TableCell>{p.title}</TableCell>
127	        <TableCell>{p.status}</TableCell>
128	        <TableCell>
129	          <Button variant="ghost" size="icon" aria-label={`Edit ${p.title}`}>
130	            <Pencil className="h-4 w-4" aria-hidden="true" />
131	          </Button>
132	        </TableCell>
133	      </TableRow>
134	    ))}
135	  </TableBody>
136	</Table>
137	```
138	
139	### Select, DropdownMenu, Tabs
140	
141	Auto-accessible via Radix. Just ensure: `Select` has a visible label (or `aria-label`), `DropdownMenu` trigger has a descriptive name, `Tabs` content is associated automatically.
142	
143	---
144	
145	## Accessible Forms
146	
147	Every form field must have: (1) visible `<Label>`, (2) error messages via `aria-describedby`, (3) `aria-invalid` on error, (4) `aria-required` for required fields.
148	
149	shadcn's `FormField` + `FormLabel` + `FormMessage` handles this automatically with React Hook Form. Add `aria-required="true"` on required inputs.
150	
151	### Required Field Indication
152	
153	```typescript
154	<FormLabel>
155	  Project Title <span aria-label="required" className="text-destructive">*</span>
156	</FormLabel>
157	```
158	
159	### Rules
160	
161	- **Never use toasts as the only error feedback** — show inline errors via `FormMessage` first; toasts are supplementary
162	- **Toast messages must convey meaning via text** — screen readers can't see icon colors
163	
164	---
165	
166	## Sonner Toasts
167	
168	Sonner handles ARIA live regions automatically:
169	
170	- Success/info toasts: `aria-live="polite"` (non-interrupting)
171	- Error toasts: `role="alert"` (interrupting)
172	- Keyboard-dismissible
173	
174	**Rules**: Always provide descriptive text messages. Keep to 1-2 sentences.
175	
176	---
177	
178	## Accessible Images
179	
180	Always use `next/image` which enforces `alt` at the TypeScript level.
181	
182	| Image Type         | Alt Text                                                          |
183	| ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
184	| Project screenshot | Describe what it shows: `"Dashboard view of task management app"` |
185	| Company logo       | Company name: `"Vercel logo"`                                     |
186	| Decorative         | `alt="" aria-hidden="true"`                                       |
187	| Profile photo      | `"Gonzalo Pozo, Full Stack Developer"`                            |
188	
189	### Rules
190	
191	- **Informative images need meaningful alt text** — TypeScript enforces the prop exists but not the value
192	- **Decorative images**: `alt=""` + `aria-hidden="true"`
193	- **Complex images**: use `<figure>` + `<figcaption>` + `aria-describedby`
194	
195	---
196	
197	## Motion Preferences
198	
199	Add to `app/globals.css` to disable animations for users who prefer reduced motion:
200	
201	```css
202	@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
203		*,
204		*::before,
205		*::after {
206			animation-duration: 0.01ms !important;
207			animation-iteration-count: 1 !important;
208			transition-duration: 0.01ms !important;
209			scroll-behavior: auto !important;
210		}
211	}
212	
213	@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) {
214		html {
215			scroll-behavior: smooth;
216		}
217	}
218	```
219	
220	For Windows High Contrast mode, ensure focus uses `outline` not `box-shadow`:
221	
222	```css
223	@media (forced-colors: active) {
224		:focus-visible {
225			outline: 2px solid CanvasText;
226			outline-offset: 2px;
227		}
228	}
229	```
230	
231	---
232	
233	## Color Contrast
234	
235	### WCAG AA Thresholds
236	
237	| Element                                     | Minimum Ratio |
238	| ------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
239	| Normal text (< 18px or < 14px bold)         | 4.5:1         |
240	| Large text (>= 18px or >= 14px bold)        | 3:1           |
241	| UI components (borders, icons, focus rings) | 3:1           |
242	
243	### Rules
244	
245	- **Never use `outline: none` without a replacement** — keyboard users need visible focus indicators
246	- **Verify `muted-foreground`** meets 4.5:1 against background when customizing the theme
247	- **Destructive actions**: red is not the only indicator — always include text like "Delete" alongside color
248	- **Use WebAIM Contrast Checker** or DevTools when changing theme colors
249	
250	---
251	
252	## Responsive Accessibility
253	
254	### Mobile Navigation
255	
256	Hamburger menus need these a11y attributes:
257	
258	```typescript
259	<Button
260	  aria-expanded={isOpen}
261	  aria-controls="mobile-menu"
262	  aria-label={isOpen ? "Close menu" : "Open menu"}
263	  className="md:hidden"
264	>
265	  {isOpen ? <X aria-hidden="true" /> : <Menu aria-hidden="true" />}
266	</Button>
267	
268	{isOpen && <ul id="mobile-menu">{/* links */}</ul>}
269	```
270	
271	### Reflow (WCAG 1.4.10)
272	
273	- Usable at 320px viewport width (400% zoom on 1280px)
274	- No horizontal scrolling for text content
275	- Touch targets at least 44x44px (WCAG 2.5.8)
276	
277	---
278	
279	## Heading Hierarchy
280	
281	### Public Page
282	
283	```
284	h1: "Gonzalo Pozo" (one per page)
285	  h2: "Projects"
286	    h3: Project titles
287	  h2: "Experience"
288	    h3: Role @ Company
289	  h2: "Skills"
290	  h2: "Contact" / "Social Links"
291	```
292	
293	### Rules
294	
295	- **Exactly one `<h1>` per page**
296	- **Never skip heading levels** — no `<h1>` → `<h3>`
297	- **Headings describe content** — not decorative
298	- DialogTitle renders as `<h2>` inside dialogs — correct and accessible
299	
300	---
301	
302	## Route Announcements
303	
304	Next.js has a built-in route announcer for client-side navigation. It announces page changes using: `document.title` → `<h1>` → URL pathname (in that order). Ensure every page has a unique `<title>` (via `metadata` export) and an `<h1>`.
305	
306	---
307	
308	## ESLint Accessibility
309	
310	Next.js includes `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y` by default. Run `pnpm lint` to catch: missing `alt`, invalid ARIA attributes, missing required ARIA props. **Do not disable jsx-a11y rules** — fix the underlying issue instead.
311	
312	---
313	
314	## Pre-Production Audit
315	
316	### Lighthouse
317	
318	Run before every deployment: `pnpm build && pnpm start`, then Chrome Incognito > DevTools > Lighthouse > Accessibility. **Target: >= 90** for the public page.
319	
320	### Manual Testing Checklist
321	
322	- [ ] Keyboard-only: Tab through entire page, all interactive elements reachable
323	- [ ] Skip link: Tab once → "Skip to main content" appears and works
324	- [ ] Focus visible: every focused element has visible outline/ring
325	- [ ] Screen reader: VoiceOver (Cmd+F5) — headings, landmarks, links announced correctly
326	- [ ] Zoom: usable at 200% and 400% without horizontal scrolling
327	- [ ] Reduced motion: enable "Reduce motion" in OS → no animations play
328	- [ ] Color contrast: no text below 4.5:1 ratio
329	- [ ] Alt text: every `<Image>` has meaningful alt (or `alt=""` for decorative)
330	- [ ] Form labels: every input has a visible label
331	- [ ] Error messages: announced to screen readers, linked to fields
332	- [ ] Dialog: traps focus, closes on Escape, returns focus to trigger
333
```

2	
3	Performance guidelines for the portfolio project — project-specific guidance that ties together the installed skills.
4	
5	> **Before implementing caching (`use cache`, PPR, `cacheLife`, `cacheTag`), execute the following skill** — read the SKILL.md and follow its instructions:
6	>
7	> 1. `.cursor/skills/next-cache-components/SKILL.md`
8	
9	> **Before optimizing bundle or rendering performance, execute the following skill** — read the SKILL.md and follow its instructions:
10	>
11	> 1. `.cursor/skills/vercel-react-best-practices/SKILL.md`
12	
13	> **Before adjusting Next.js data patterns or RSC boundaries, execute the following skill** — read the SKILL.md and follow its instructions:
14	>
15	> 1. `.cursor/skills/next-best-practices/SKILL.md`
16	
17	> **Before restructuring component tree for performance, execute the following skill** — read the SKILL.md and follow its instructions:
18	>
19	> 1. `.cursor/skills/vercel-composition-patterns/SKILL.md`

21	---
22	
23	## React Compiler
24	
25	Enabled in this project (`reactCompiler: true` in `next.config.ts`). Automatically inserts memoization at build time.
26	
27	| Before (manual)                     | After (compiler handles it)         |
28	| ----------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
29	| `useMemo(() => calc(data), [data])` | `const result = calc(data)`         |
30	| `useCallback((id) => fn(id), [fn])` | `const handler = (id) => fn(id)`    |
31	| `React.memo(Component)`             | `function Component(props) { ... }` |
32	
33	### Rules
34	
35	- **Do NOT use `useMemo`, `useCallback`, or `React.memo`** — redundant with the compiler
36	- **Write plain, readable code** — the compiler optimizes it
37	- **Keep components pure** — same output for same props, no mutations during render
38	- **Side effects only in `useEffect`, event handlers, or Server Actions**
39	- **Do NOT use `React.forwardRef`** — React 19 supports `ref` as a regular prop
40	- If the compiler can't safely optimize code, it silently skips it (no errors)
41	
42	---
43	
44	## Dynamic Imports & Code Splitting
45	
46	Use `next/dynamic` to reduce initial JS bundle:
47	
48	```typescript
49	import dynamic from "next/dynamic";
50	
51	const HeavyEditor = dynamic(() => import("@/components/admin/editor"), {
52	  loading: () => <Spinner />,
53	});
54	
55	const ChartComponent = dynamic(() => import("@/components/chart"), {
56	  ssr: false,
57	  loading: () => <div className="h-64 animate-pulse bg-muted rounded-md" />,
58	});
59	```
60	
61	### When to Use
62	
63	- Heavy components not visible on initial load (modals, editors, charts)
64	- Admin-only components behind authentication
65	- Client-only libraries using browser APIs (`window`, `document`)
66	
67	### What NOT to Dynamically Import
68	
69	- Layout components (header, sidebar) — always needed immediately
70	- Small, lightweight components — overhead outweighs savings
71	- Server Components — automatically code-split by Next.js
72	
73	### Project-Specific Guidance
74	
75	| Component                  | Dynamic? | Reason                          |
76	| -------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------- |
77	| Admin sidebar/header       | No       | Always visible                  |
78	| Login form                 | No       | Lightweight, needed immediately |
79	| Skills multi-select (cmdk) | Yes      | Heavy dependency, only in forms |
80	| Data tables                | No       | Primary dashboard content       |
81	| Delete confirmation dialog | Yes      | Only on user action             |
82	| Public portfolio page      | No       | All content is primary          |
83	
84	---
85	
86	## Loading Files & Streaming
87	
88	`loading.tsx` files wrap their sibling `page.tsx` in `<Suspense>` automatically, streaming the layout while data loads.
89	
90	### Skeleton Pattern
91	
92	```typescript
93	// app/(admin)/dashboard/projects/loading.tsx
94	export default function Loading() {
95	  return (
96	    <div className="space-y-4">
97	      <div className="flex items-center justify-between">
98	        <div className="h-8 w-48 animate-pulse rounded-md bg-muted" />
99	        <div className="h-10 w-32 animate-pulse rounded-md bg-muted" />
100	      </div>
101	      {/* Match the shape of actual content to minimize layout shift */}
102	    </div>
103	  );
104	}
105	```
106	
107	### Granular Streaming
108	
109	For pages with multiple independent data sources, use separate `<Suspense>` boundaries:
110	
111	```typescript
112	<Suspense fallback={<StatsSkeleton />}>
113	  <DashboardStats />
114	</Suspense>
115	<Suspense fallback={<ProjectsSkeleton />}>
116	  <RecentProjects />
117	</Suspense>
118	```
119	
120	### Where to Add Loading Files
121	
122	| Route                                    | Needed? | Reason                     |
123	| ---------------------------------------- | ------- | -------------------------- |
124	| `app/(admin)/dashboard/*/page.tsx` (all) | Yes     | All fetch from DB          |
125	| `app/(public)/page.tsx`                  | Yes     | Fetches all portfolio data |
126	| `app/(admin)/login/page.tsx`             | No      | No data fetching           |
127	
128	---
129	
130	## Bundle Optimization
131	
132	### `optimizePackageImports`
133	
134	Already configured in `next.config.ts` for `lucide-react`, `react-icons`, `@radix-ui/react-icons`. Ensures only used exports are bundled even with barrel file imports.
135	
136	### Rules
137	
138	- **Import specific exports** — `import { Heart } from "lucide-react"`, not `import * as Icons`
139	- **No barrel imports** (`import * as ...`) — tree shaking may miss some
140	- **Analyze periodically** — `pnpm next experimental-analyze` to find oversized dependencies
141	
142	---
143	
144	## Server vs Client Decision Tree
145	
146	```
147	Is the component interactive (onClick, onChange, state, effects)?
148	├── NO → Server Component (default, no directive)
149	│   - Zero client JS, direct DB access, secrets stay on server
150	│
151	└── YES → Does the ENTIRE component need interactivity?
152	    ├── NO → Split: data fetching in Server Component, pass props to Client
153	    └── YES → Client Component ("use client")
154	        - Keep small, import into Server parent, never fetch data inside
155	```
156	
157	### Project-Specific Boundaries
158	
159	| Component                  | Type   | Reason                         |
160	| -------------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------ |
161	| Dashboard layout           | Server | Static structure               |
162	| Sidebar navigation         | Client | Active state, mobile toggle    |
163	| Projects list page         | Server | Data fetching, table rendering |
164	| Delete confirmation dialog | Client | Modal state, click handlers    |
165	| Login form                 | Client | Form state, submission         |
166	| Public portfolio page      | Server | Static rendering, SEO          |
167	| Skills multi-select        | Client | Combobox interactivity (cmdk)  |
168	
169	---
170	
171	## Core Web Vitals
172	
173	### LCP (Largest Contentful Paint) — Loading
174	
175	| Rating            | Threshold |
176	| ----------------- | --------- |
177	| Good              | <= 2.5s   |
178	| Needs Improvement | 2.5s–4.0s |
179	| Poor              | > 4.0s    |
180	
181	**Optimizations in this project**: `priority` on above-fold images, `next/font` for fonts, `"use cache"` + `cacheLife` for data, Server Components on public page, `loading.tsx` for instant shell.
182	
183	### INP (Interaction to Next Paint) — Interactivity
184	
185	| Rating            | Threshold   |
186	| ----------------- | ----------- |
187	| Good              | <= 200ms    |
188	| Needs Improvement | 200ms–500ms |
189	| Poor              | > 500ms     |
190	
191	**Optimizations**: React Compiler auto-memoization, Server Components by default (minimal client JS), dynamic imports for heavy components, `startTransition` for mutations.
192	
193	### CLS (Cumulative Layout Shift) — Visual Stability
194	
195	| Rating            | Threshold |
196	| ----------------- | --------- |
197	| Good              | <= 0.1    |
198	| Needs Improvement | 0.1–0.25  |
199	| Poor              | > 0.25    |
200	
201	**Optimizations**: `next/image` with dimensions (prevents shift), `next/font` (no FOUT), skeleton UIs matching content shape, no content injection above existing elements.
202

205	## Monitoring with `useReportWebVitals`

211	import { useReportWebVitals } from 'next/web-vitals';

223	}
224	```

1	# AGENTS-ANIMATIONS.md
2	
3	Animation guidelines for the portfolio project — when and how to use the three animation layers: Tailwind CSS, Motion (Framer Motion), and NumberFlow.
4	
5	**Animation libraries in this project:**
6	
7	- `tw-animate-css` — Tailwind-compatible animation utilities used by shadcn/ui (fadeIn, slideIn, etc.)
8	- `motion` (v12+) — React animation library for layout, gestures, exit animations, orchestration
9	- `@number-flow/react` — Animated number component for counters and statistics
10	
11	> **Before designing or implementing animations/visual polish, execute the following skill** — read the SKILL.md and follow its instructions:
12	>
13	> 1. `.cursor/skills/frontend-design/SKILL.md`
14	
15	**Related coverage in other AGENTS files (do not duplicate):**
16	
17	- `AGENTS-ACCESSIBILITY.md` > Motion Preferences — `prefers-reduced-motion` CSS
18	- `AGENTS-PERFORMANCE.md` > Dynamic Imports — `next/dynamic` for heavy components
19	
20	---
21	
22	## When to Use Each Layer
23	
24	| Situation                                    | Use                                                 | Why                              |
25	| -------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
26	| Spinners, pulses, simple hover effects       | **Tailwind** (`animate-*`, `transition-*`)          | Zero JS, GPU-accelerated         |
27	| shadcn component transitions (Dialog, Sheet) | **tw-animate-css** (built in)                       | Pre-configured, consistent       |
28	| Icon state changes (copy→check, like toggle) | **Motion** (`AnimatePresence`)                      | CSS can't do enter/exit cleanly  |
29	| Layout animations (list reorder, add/remove) | **Motion** (`layout` prop)                          | CSS can't animate FLIP           |
30	| Animated number counters                     | **NumberFlow**                                      | Purpose-built, accessible        |
31	| Page transitions                             | **Motion** or CSS View Transitions                  | Prefer CSS for simple fades      |
32	| Scroll-triggered animations                  | **Motion** (`useInView`) or Tailwind `motion-safe:` | Motion for complex orchestration |
33	
34	### Rules
35	
36	- **Default to Tailwind** — no JS overhead
37	- **Motion requires `"use client"`** — uses hooks and event handlers
38	- **NumberFlow only for numeric values**
39	- **Never install GSAP, anime.js, etc.** — Motion covers all needs
40	
41	---
42	
43	## Tailwind CSS Animations
44	
45	### Built-in Utilities
46	
47	| Utility          | Use                    |
48	| ---------------- | ---------------------- |
49	| `animate-spin`   | Loading spinners       |
50	| `animate-ping`   | Notification badges    |
51	| `animate-pulse`  | Skeleton loaders       |
52	| `animate-bounce` | Scroll-down indicators |
53	
54	### Transition Pattern
55	
56	```typescript
57	<div className="transition-transform duration-200 ease-out hover:-translate-y-0.5">
58	  {/* Card hover lift */}
59	</div>
60	```
61	
62	### Reduced Motion
63	
64	Use `motion-safe:` and `motion-reduce:` variants:
65	
66	```typescript
67	<svg className="motion-safe:animate-spin h-5 w-5" />
68	```
69	
70	### Custom Animations
71	
72	Define in `globals.css` via `@theme` directive for reusable animations:
73	
74	```css
75	@theme {
76		--animate-wiggle: wiggle 0.3s ease-in-out;
77		@keyframes wiggle {
78			0%,
79			100% {
80				transform: rotate(-3deg);
81			}
82			50% {
83				transform: rotate(3deg);
84			}
85		}
86	}
87	```
88	
89	Use as `animate-wiggle`. Prefer this over inline `animate-[...]` for animations used more than once.
90	
91	---
92	
93	## Motion (Framer Motion)
94	
95	Import from `motion/react` (not `framer-motion` — package renamed):
96	
97	```typescript
98	'use client';
99	import { motion, AnimatePresence } from 'motion/react';
100	```
101	
102	### Basic Animation
103	
104	```typescript
105	<motion.div
106	  initial={{ opacity: 0, y: 10 }}
107	  animate={{ opacity: 1, y: 0 }}
108	  transition={{ duration: 0.3, ease: "easeOut" }}
109	>
110	  {children}
111	</motion.div>
112	```
113	
114	### Enter/Exit Animations (AnimatePresence)
115	
116	Wrap items that mount/unmount to animate exits:
117	
118	```typescript
119	<AnimatePresence mode="wait" initial={false}>
120	  {isCopied ? (
121	    <motion.div key="check"
122	      initial={{ scale: 0 }} animate={{ scale: 1 }} exit={{ scale: 0 }}
123	      transition={{ duration: 0.15 }}>
124	      <Check className="h-4 w-4" aria-hidden="true" />
125	    </motion.div>
126	  ) : (
127	    <motion.div key="copy" /* same animation props */>
128	      <Copy className="h-4 w-4" aria-hidden="true" />
129	    </motion.div>
130	  )}
131	</AnimatePresence>
132	```
133	
134	### Layout Animations
135	
136	Use `layout` prop for automatic FLIP when size/position changes:
137	
138	```typescript
139	<motion.ul layout>
140	  <AnimatePresence>
141	    {items.map((item) => (
142	      <motion.li key={item.id} layout
143	        initial={{ opacity: 0 }} animate={{ opacity: 1 }} exit={{ opacity: 0 }}
144	        transition={{ duration: 0.2 }}>
145	        {item.title}
146	      </motion.li>
147	    ))}
148	  </AnimatePresence>
149	</motion.ul>
150	```
151	
152	### Key Concepts
153	
154	| Concept                        | What It Does                        | When to Use                      |
155	| ------------------------------ | ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
156	| `initial` / `animate` / `exit` | Mount/unmount states                | Entrance/exit animations         |
157	| `transition`                   | Duration, easing, spring config     | Fine-tune any animation          |
158	| `layout` / `layoutId`          | FLIP layout animations              | List reorder, shared transitions |
159	| `AnimatePresence`              | Keeps children until exit completes | Anything that mounts/unmounts    |
160	| `whileHover` / `whileTap`      | Hover/press animations              | Interactive elements             |
161	| `useInView` / `useScroll`      | Viewport/scroll tracking            | Scroll-triggered animations      |
162	
163	### With Server Components
164	
165	Motion components must be Client Components. Wrap only the animated part:
166	
167	```typescript
168	// components/animated-section.tsx — "use client"
169	<motion.section
170	  initial={{ opacity: 0, y: 20 }}
171	  whileInView={{ opacity: 1, y: 0 }}
172	  viewport={{ once: true, margin: "-100px" }}
173	  transition={{ duration: 0.4 }}>
174	  {children}
175	</motion.section>
176	
177	// Server Component imports and passes children as props
178	```
179	
180	---
181	
182	## NumberFlow
183	
184	Smooth animated transitions between numeric values. Accessible by default (`respectMotionPreference: true`).
185	
186	```typescript
187	"use client";
188	import NumberFlow from "@number-flow/react";
189	
190	<NumberFlow value={count} locales="en-US" className="text-3xl font-bold tabular-nums" />
191	
192	// With formatting
193	<NumberFlow value={price} format={{ style: "currency", currency: "USD" }} />
194	<NumberFlow value={pct} format={{ style: "percent", minimumFractionDigits: 1 }} />
195	<NumberFlow value={total} suffix=" projects" />
196	```
197	
198	### Where to Use
199	
200	| Location                       | Value                          | Format           |
201	| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------ | ---------------- |
202	| Dashboard overview stats       | Project/experience/skill count | Integer          |
203	| Public page (if showing stats) | Years of experience            | Integer + suffix |
204	
205	### Rules
206	
207	- **Always `"use client"`** — uses browser APIs
208	- **Use `tabular-nums` class** — prevents layout shift during transitions
209	- **Set `locales` explicitly** — consistent formatting
210	- **Do NOT set `respectMotionPreference: false`** — respects reduced motion by default
211	
212	---
213	
214	## Animation Performance
215	
216	### Animate Only Composite Properties (GPU-accelerated)
217	
218	| Safe (GPU)                             | Avoid (triggers layout)          |
219	| -------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
220	| `transform` (translate, scale, rotate) | `width`, `height`                |
221	| `opacity`                              | `top`, `right`, `bottom`, `left` |
222	| `filter` (blur, brightness)            | `margin`, `padding`              |
223	| `clip-path`                            | `border-width`, `font-size`      |
224	
225	### Rules
226	
227	- **`will-change`** — only on elements that animate frequently; too many wastes GPU memory. Motion handles it internally for its animated properties
228	- **Keep Motion out of pages that don't need it** — dynamically import animated components if only used on specific pages
229	- **All animations must maintain 60fps** — test on throttled CPU (Chrome DevTools > Performance > 4x slowdown)
230	
231	---
232	
233	## Animation UX Guidelines
234	
235	### Timing
236	
237	| Type                                        | Duration  | Easing               |
238	| ------------------------------------------- | --------- | -------------------- |
239	| Micro-interaction (button press, icon swap) | 100-200ms | `ease-out`           |
240	| Enter/appear                                | 200-300ms | `ease-out`           |
241	| Exit/disappear                              | 150-250ms | `ease-in`            |
242	| Layout change (reorder, resize)             | 200-400ms | `ease-in-out`        |
243	| Page transition                             | 300-500ms | `ease-in-out`        |
244	| Number transition                           | 300-750ms | spring or `ease-out` |
245	
246	### Easing Rule of Thumb
247	
248	- **Enters** → `ease-out`
249	- **Leaves** → `ease-in`
250	- **Moves while staying** → `ease-in-out`
251	- **Never stops** (spinners) → `linear`
252	
253	### Do's and Don'ts
254	
255	- Animate to provide **feedback** or **guide attention** — every animation needs a purpose
256	- Keep durations **short** — users see them hundreds of times
257	- Use `AnimatePresence` for exits — elements shouldn't just vanish
258	- Use `viewport={{ once: true }}` for scroll-triggered animations
259	- **Don't** animate for decoration only
260	- **Don't** use bouncy springs for frequent/repetitive actions
261	- **Don't** animate more than 2-3 elements simultaneously
262	- **Don't** add entrance animations to admin data tables (too frequent)
263	- **Don't** use `animate-spin` on anything except loading indicators
264
```
</details></tool-use>

14	
15	## Prerequisites
16	
17	- Node.js 24+
18	- pnpm 10.33.0 via the repo's `packageManager` field
19	- Turso CLI (optional, for local DB management)
20	
21	## Environment Variables
22	
23	Create a `.env.local` file:
24	
25	```env
26	TURSO_DATABASE_URL=libsql://your-database.turso.io
27	TURSO_AUTH_TOKEN=your-auth-token
28	BETTER_AUTH_SECRET=your-secret-key
29	BETTER_AUTH_URL=http://localhost:3000
30	```
31	
32	## Installation
33	
34	```bash
35	pnpm i
36	pnpm run hooks:install
37	```
38	
39	`ignore-scripts=true` is enabled in `.npmrc`, so lifecycle scripts do not run during install. Husky hooks must be installed manually with `pnpm run hooks:install`.
40	
41	## Making Schema Changes
42	
43	1. Edit schema files in `db/schema/`
44	2. Run `pnpm db:setup` to generate migrations and push to Turso
45	
46	## Agent Skills Installation Policy
47	
48	- Every new skill installed via `skills.sh` CLI must also be added to the `skills:install` script in `package.json`.
49	- Keep `skills:install` as the single source of truth for reproducible skill setup across environments.

```md
description: JSDoc conventions — when and how to document code. Applies to lib/, db/, and components/.
globs:
  - "lib/**"
  - "db/**"

---

## JSDoc Rules

TypeScript provides type safety — use JSDoc only for **semantic context** (the "why", not the "what").

**Document when**: non-obvious logic, side effects (revalidation, redirects), security assumptions, edge cases, deprecations.

**Skip JSDoc for**: self-explanatory functions, typed component props, one-liner utilities with clear names.

### Approved Tags

- `@param` — only when name/type isn't self-explanatory
- `@returns` — only when return value has non-obvious meaning
- `@throws` — actions that throw or redirect
- `@example` — complex utilities only
- `@deprecated`, `@see`, `@todo` — standard usage

**Never use** `@type`, `@typedef`, `@callback` — TypeScript handles these.

### Style

- Use `/** ... */` (not `//` or `/* */`)
- First line: concise summary, imperative mood ("Retrieves...", not "This function retrieves...")
- Blank line before tags if there's a description body
- Keep under 80 chars per line

### Priority

| Location | Priority |
|---|---|
| `lib/actions/*` | **High** — side effects, auth, revalidation |
| `lib/auth.ts`, `lib/server-session.ts` | **High** — security assumptions |
| `db/schema/*` | **Medium** — relationships, constraints |
| `components/ui/*` | **Medium** — prop behavior, a11y notes |
| `lib/utils.ts`, pages/layouts | **Low** — only if non-trivial |

Full examples and context: see AGENTS-CONVENTIONS.md

```

```md
---
description: Architecture pattern rules — Container-Presentational, Server Action hardening, Data Access Facade, Error Boundaries.
globs:
  - "app/**"
  - "lib/actions/**"
  - "lib/queries/**"
  - "lib/schemas/**"
  - "components/admin/**"
---

## Architecture Rules

### Container-Presentational

- **page.tsx must not exceed ~50 lines** — if it does, UI is leaking into the container
- Presentational components receive all data via props — never call `db` directly
- Presentational components are `"use client"` only when they need interactivity
- Shared formatting goes in `lib/utils.ts`, not redefined per page

### Server Action Hardening (every action, no exceptions)

1. **Authenticate**: `getServerSession()` first, redirect to `/login` if null
2. **Validate**: Zod `.safeParse()` — never trust `formData.get()` directly
3. **Execute**: try-catch around DB operations, return user-friendly errors
4. **Revalidate**: `redirect()` for create, `revalidatePath()` for update/delete

- Zod schemas live in `lib/schemas/` — one file per entity
- Transform empty strings to `undefined` — forms submit `""` for empty optional fields
- Remove all `console.log` from actions

### Data Access Facade

- **Pages never import `db` directly** — always go through `lib/queries/`
- Server Actions still use `db` directly (writes don't need the facade)
- One file per entity in `lib/queries/`, add `"server-only"` import
- Caching goes here — `"use cache"` + `cacheLife()` inside facade functions

### Error Boundaries

- `error.tsx` must have `"use client"` — required by Next.js
- Never display `error.message` to users — show generic message
- Always provide a reset button and a "go back" link

### Next.js 16 Specifics

- `params` and `searchParams` are **promises** — always `await` before accessing
- Every admin page must call `getServerSession()` at the top
- Layouts cannot access `searchParams` — only `params` and `children`
- `route.ts` and `page.tsx` cannot coexist in the same segment

Full templates and checklists: see AGENTS-PATTERNS.md

```

```md
---
description: Security rules — auth patterns, input validation, CSP, environment variables. Critical for actions, auth, and API routes.
globs:
  - "lib/actions/**"
  - "lib/auth*.ts"
  - "lib/server-session.ts"
  - "lib/schemas/**"
  - "app/api/**"
  - "proxy.ts"
---

## Security Rules

### Auth Protection (two-layer)

- **NEVER rely on `proxy.ts` for security** — it only checks cookie existence (UX redirect)
- **ALWAYS call `getServerSession()` in every protected page and every Server Action**
- `cache()` wrapping in `server-session.ts` deduplicates DB calls within a request

### Server Actions

- Every action: authenticate → validate (Zod `.safeParse()`) → execute (try-catch) → revalidate
- **Never expose internal errors** — return user-friendly messages, log server-side
- `formData.get()` returns `FormDataEntryValue | null` — handle null before Zod
- Remove all `console.log` statements from production code

### Input Validation

- Validate on the server — client-side is UX only
- Use `.safeParse()` — graceful errors without try-catch
- Set max lengths — prevent DoS, match DB constraints
- Use `.or(z.literal(""))` for optional URL fields

### SQL Injection Prevention

- **Always use Drizzle query builder** or `sql` template literal
- **Never use `sql.raw()` with user input**
- **Never concatenate strings into SQL** — `db.execute(\`...\`)` with interpolation is injection

### Environment Variables

- **NEVER prefix secrets with `NEXT_PUBLIC_`**
- **NEVER commit `.env.local` to git**
- Generate `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` with `openssl rand -base64 32`

### CSP

- Dev mode needs `'unsafe-eval'` and `'unsafe-inline'` — NOT in production
- If adding third-party scripts, add domains to `script-src` and `connect-src`

### Headers

- Do NOT add `X-XSS-Protection` — deprecated, CSP replaces it
- Do NOT set `Cache-Control` for `_next/static` — Next.js handles it

### CSRF

- Do NOT set `disableCSRFCheck: true` or `disableOriginCheck: true` in better-auth
- Custom API routes beyond `/api/auth/*` need manual CSRF token verification

Full implementation details: see AGENTS-SECURITY.md and AGENTS-SECURITY-REFERENCE.md

```

```md
description: Accessibility rules — semantic HTML, ARIA, forms, images, focus, contrast. Applies to all UI code.
globs:

## Accessibility Rules

### Use Next.js Components Over HTML

| HTML | Use Instead | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `<a>` (internal) | `<Link>` from `next/link` | Prefetching, client-side nav |
| `<img>` | `<Image>` from `next/image` | Enforces alt, lazy loading |
| `<form>` (navigation) | `<Form>` from `next/form` | Progressive enhancement |
| Font `<link>` | `next/font` | Zero layout shift |
| `<script>` | `<Script>` from `next/script` | Loading strategies |

### Landmarks & Structure

- Exactly **one `<main>`** per page with `id="main-content"` and `tabIndex={-1}`
- `<nav>` needs `aria-label` when multiple navs exist on the same page
- Use `<section aria-labelledby="heading-id">` for major content sections
- Exactly **one `<h1>` per page** — never skip heading levels

### Skip Link

Required (WCAG 2.4.1). Place as first child in public layout. Target: `#main-content`.

### Components

- **Icon-only buttons MUST have `aria-label`** — decorative icons use `aria-hidden="true"`
- **Dialog**: always include `DialogTitle` and `DialogDescription` (Radix needs them for aria-labelledby)
- **Tables**: add `<TableCaption>` and `scope="col"` on headers

### Forms

- Every field: visible `<Label>` + `aria-describedby` for errors + `aria-invalid` on error + `aria-required`
- **Never use toasts as the only error feedback** — inline errors first, toasts supplementary
- Required fields: mark with `<span aria-label="required">*</span>`

### Images

- Informative: meaningful alt text describing content
- Decorative: `alt="" aria-hidden="true"`
- Complex: `<figure>` + `<figcaption>` + `aria-describedby`

### Color & Focus

- Normal text: 4.5:1 contrast minimum. Large text: 3:1. UI components: 3:1.
- **Never use `outline: none` without a replacement** focus indicator
- Red is not the only indicator for destructive actions — always include text

### Responsive

- Usable at 320px viewport (400% zoom)
- Touch targets: minimum 44×44px (WCAG 2.5.8)
- **Do not disable `jsx-a11y` ESLint rules** — fix the issue instead

Full guidelines and audit checklist: see AGENTS-ACCESSIBILITY.md
```

```md
description: Testing conventions — file locations, naming, mocking patterns, what to test. Applies to test files.
globs:

  - "e2e/**"

  - "playwright.config.*"

## Testing Rules

### Strategy

| Code Layer | Strategy | Tool |
|---|---|---|
| Zod schemas | **TDD** (test first) | Vitest |
| Utility functions | **TDD** | Vitest |
| Server Action logic | **TDD for validation, test-after for DB** | Vitest |
| Junction table sync | Test-after | Vitest |
| Client components | Test-after (optional) | Vitest + RTL |
| Pages, auth flows | Test-after | Playwright |

**Don't test**: shadcn/ui primitives, better-auth config, Tailwind classes, Next.js framework behavior, simple data-fetching pages, async RSCs (use Playwright instead).

### File Locations & Naming

- Vitest: `tests/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}` — mirror source structure
- Playwright: `e2e/**/*.spec.ts` — named by flow (`auth.spec.ts`)
- Test names: behavior for Vitest (`"rejects empty title"`), user action for Playwright (`"should create a new project"`)

### Mocking

- **Mock at module level** with `vi.mock(...)` — Vitest hoists automatically
- **Use `vi.mocked()` for type-safe access** to mocked functions
- **Reset mocks**: `beforeEach(() => { vi.clearAllMocks(); })`
- **Don't mock what you're testing** — test schema? don't mock Zod. Test action? mock db, not the action.
- `redirect()` mock: throw `Error("REDIRECT:/path")` to mirror Next.js behavior
- `revalidatePath()`: `vi.mock("next/cache", () => ({ revalidatePath: vi.fn() }))`

### Vitest Practices

- One assertion per concept
- Arrange-Act-Assert pattern
- Test edge cases: empty strings, null, boundary values, special characters
- Use `it.each` for parameterized tests
- Keep suite under 10 seconds — if slower, check for real network calls or missing mocks

### Playwright Practices

- Locator priority: `getByRole` > `getByLabel` > `getByText` > `getByTestId` > CSS selectors
- Test user-visible behavior (`toBeVisible`, `toContainText`), not DOM structure
- Don't add `page.waitForTimeout()` — use auto-waiting
- Test the unhappy path: errors, unauthorized redirects, delete confirmations

Full mock code blocks and CI setup: see AGENTS-TESTING.md and AGENTS-TESTING-REFERENCE.md
```
